A **nonexistent** `Manifests` is not an error: empty result with readable roots, and the core marks Epic installs as removed (the launcher has none; revised after the auditor, M3). Reason: installs do not hang from the data folder but from other roots, and marking only the data one would let the core remove all of Epic because of a passing failure. Malformed JSON: that file is skipped. Any other `internal` is propagated.
- **Log:** only counters and codes. No paths, no titles, no Epic IDs (they are 32-character hexadecimals that the redactor masks anyway).

#### 4. Play and Install

**Options for Play:**

- **A. Launcher URI** (chosen): `com.epicgames.launcher://apps/<namespace>%3A<catalogItemId>%3A<appName>?action=launch&silent=true`. It is the format of the shortcuts the launcher itself creates (assumption E3).
  - Advantages: the launcher does what an `exec` cannot: many Epic games need to be passed, at startup, an exchange code from the user's session (`-AUTH_PASSWORD=<code> -AUTH_TYPE=exchangecode`) and, some, an ownership token (`-epicovt=<file>`). `legendary` does it that way when launching without the launcher (assumption E9). In addition, the launcher syncs cloud saves, applies pending updates and opens the overlay. It has the same shape as Steam: no `exec` and no executable confinement.
  - Costs: it requires the launcher to be installed (it is if there is a `.item`) and starts it in the background if it was closed; the process detection of 55 is indirect, as in Steam.
- **B. `exec` of `InstallLocation\LaunchExecutable`.** It would work with DRM-free games, but would silently break those that require Epic authentication. Doing it properly requires the user's session (slice 2) and reimplementing `legendary`'s launch (exchange code, ownership token, arguments `-epicapp`, `-epicenv`, `-epicusername`…). Discarded.
- **C. The short form `apps/<appName>`** (forums): some use it, but the current launcher writes the three-part one in its shortcuts. Discarded.

**`resolveAction`** (`connectors/epic/src/launch.ts`):

1. Action other than `play` (slice 1) or than `play` and `install` (slice 2): `null`.
2. `storeGameId` must match the pattern of point 6; otherwise `action.unsupported` with `connectors.epic.errors.invalidId`. ~~It is split into its three segments~~ The URI is built from **the three capture groups** of the pattern (not by splitting the text on `:`), which by the pattern need no encoding, joined with `%3A`; before returning it, a final assertion checks that the whole URI matches `^com\.epicgames\.launcher://apps/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}%3A[0-9a-f]{32}%3A[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,60}\?action=(launch&silent=true|install)$` (revised after the auditor).
3. `play`: null `installPath` → `launch.not-installed`. It returns `{ kind: 'uri', uri: 'com.epicgames.launcher://apps/<ns>%3A<cat>%3A<app>?action=launch&silent=true' }`. **Without checking the launcher:** if the game has a `.item`, the launcher is installed; if it was uninstalled afterwards, Windows shows its own "no application for this link" notice. `shortcut:` the check is added if the manual test shows that this case is common.
4. `install` (slice 2): the same URI with `?action=install` (without `silent`, so that the launcher shows its dialog; assumption E4). If `ctx.launchersResolved` and the `epic-launcher` location has no `EpicGamesLauncher.exe`: `launch.launcher-missing` with `connectors.epic.errors.launcherMissing` ("The Epic Games launcher is required to install this game. Download it from epicgames.com"). ~~The location and the check are only added **if the slice 1 test confirms assumption E5**; if not, Install returns the URI without checking.~~ (Revised after the auditor: E5 is verified; the check always goes in slice 2.) **Launcher present** = some resolved `epic-launcher` location whose path is a file that exists and ends in `EpicGamesLauncher.exe` (case-insensitive); the location already points to the `.exe`, not to a folder.
- **Slice 2 location:** `epic-launcher` (`launcher`) with two sources: `{ kind: 'registry-value', hive: 'HKCU', key: 'Software\\Epic Games\\EOS', value: 'ModSdkCommand' }` (the path of the launcher executable, according to its installer; assumption E5) and `{ kind: 'known-folder', folder: 'ProgramFilesX86', relative: 'Epic Games\\Launcher\\Portal\\Binaries\\Win64\\EpicGamesLauncher.exe' }`, the default folder. Only the registry one would find the user's launcher on `E:`. ~~That is why it is not used without confirming it, so as not to give a false "the launcher is required".~~ Checked on 22-10-2026: `ModSdkCommand` exists in `HKCU`, with the path of the `.exe` using `/` as separator and without quotes. The platform does not change because of this: the location resolver already normalizes each path (`files.normalize`) and checks that it exists before returning it (`location-resolver.ts`). A resolver test with a path using `/` fixes it.
- **Core and platform:** no changes. `checkSpec` already validates scheme and shape; `validateLaunchUri` accepts `%3A`, `?`, `&` and `=`. `uriSchemes: ['com.epicgames.launcher']` meets `SCHEME_RE`.
- The web shows "Opening Epic Games…" with `game.launching` (and `game.installing` in slice 2) and `{store}`.

#### 5. Covers

- **Slice 1, no account: Epic catalog with an application token** (chosen).
  - `POST https://account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com/account/api/oauth/token`, form `grant_type=client_credentials` and `token_type=eg1`, with the `basic` header of point 2. It gives an application token, with no user, which `legendary` and `egs-api` use for public data (assumption E7). It lives in memory during that `resolveMedia` call, as a `Secret`, and is not stored.
  - For each **namespace** of the batch (DLC share the game's): `GET https://catalog-public-service-prod06.ol.epicgames.com/catalog/api/shared/namespace/<ns>/bulk/items?id=<cat>&id=<cat>…&includeDLCDetails=false&includeMainGameDetails=true&country=US&locale=<ctx.locale>`, with `authorization: bearer <token>` as a `Secret`. It is the request made by `legendary`, Playnite and `egs-api` (assumption E11). The repeated `id` does not fit in `query` (an object), so the connector builds the query in the `url` itself with `URLSearchParams`; the `HttpClient` already preserves it and adds that of `query`.
  - **Discarded:** the store's GraphQL (`store.epicgames.com/graphql`, protected against non-browser clients and with undocumented queries); the cross-namespace variant `POST …/catalog/api/shared/bulk/namespaces/items` of `egs-api` (fewer requests, but the shape of its response is not known: reviewed if a large library does not fit in time, point 8); and the public promotions feed (only games on sale).
- **`resolveMedia`** (`connectors/epic/src/media.ts`), with the rules of 76:
  - each ID is revalidated with the pattern of point 6 before anything else; one that does not match is omitted without a request; **if no valid ID is left, the application token is not requested** and an empty map is returned (revised after the auditor);
  - at most **50 IDs per catalog request**, here too (the core's batch is already 50, but the rule belongs to the connector);
  - token first: 400, 401 or 403 → `store.unexpected-response` for the batch; 429 → `store.rate-limited`;
  - at most **6 catalog requests at a time**, 8 s each; with the first 429 no more are launched and `store.rate-limited` is thrown with `Retry-After`;
  - 200: an object with one entry per catalog ID. From each, `keyImages` (list of `{ type, url }`): `coverUrl` = that of `DieselGameBoxTall` or, if missing, `OfferImageTall`; `heroUrl` = that of `DieselGameBox` or, if missing, `OfferImageWide`. Each URL: `https`, host in `mediaHosts`, no user or password, at most 2048 characters. One from another host is omitted and counted, logging **only the host** (it is not personal data and it closes assumption E8). An ID that does not come back stays out of the map;
  - 404 for a namespace: its IDs stay out of the map; any other status or a body that is not an object: `store.unexpected-response` for the batch (throw instead of omit, for the same reason as 76).
  - **If Epic does not accept the application token in the catalog** (assumption E7 false): slice 1 is left without covers (degraded) and `resolveMedia` is removed from the manifest in the same change, without another decision; with slice 2 they arrive through `listLibrary` (below). **This is what happens (checked on 22-10-2026, point 15):** `resolveEpicMedia` remains implemented and tested, but is **not declared** in the manifest, because it would send Epic the IDs of the installed games without obtaining anything. Slice 1 has no covers for installed games until the account is connected.
- **Slice 2:** `listLibrary` already requests the catalog for titles (point 8) and returns `media` with the same rules in each entry, with the user's token. Owned games have a cover even if E7 fails.
- **`mediaHosts`: `['cdn1.epicgames.com', 'cdn2.unrealengine.com']`.** Both appear in the images of the store's public feed (checked on 22-10-2026; the vertical ones at `cdn1.epicgames.com/offer/…` and `cdn1.epicgames.com/spt-assets/…`, others at `cdn2.unrealengine.com`). The CSP and `vite.config.ts` add them (parity test of 71). Whether the catalog's `keyImages` use only those hosts is unverified (assumption E8): if the test shows another, it is added after checking it.
- **Privacy (invariant 9):** what goes out to Epic is the namespaces and catalog IDs of the detected Epic games and the IP, with the application token, without cookies or its own `User-Agent`; the same as the launcher would request. The docs-writer adds it to the guide.

#### 6. Ownership identifier (small core change)

- **`storeGameId` = `<namespace>:<catalogItemId>:<appName>`**, with the pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}:[0-9a-f]{32}:[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,60}$` (assumption E6). The catalog ID and the namespace **only if it is a 32-character hexadecimal** (revised after the auditor: a readable namespace such as `fn` is left as is) are lowercased when read, in the scan and in the library, so that the same game gives the same ID by both routes.
  - Reason: it is the only thing that the URI (all three) and the catalog (the first two) need at the same time, and it arrives the same from the `.item` and from the library. With only the catalog ID, Install on a not-installed game could not build the URI (`StoreEntry` carries no `launchData`). With only `appName`, the catalog could not be requested.
- **The core today limits `storeGameId` to 64 characters** (`packages/core/src/validate.ts`, in the scan and library validations), and Epic's reaches 158. **It is decided to raise the limit to 160** in both validations. The column is `text` with no limit and the unique index does not change. It is a compatible relaxation: `contractVersion` stays at 1. The comment on `StoreEntry.storeGameId` and `InstalledEntry.storeGameId` in `contracts` says "1 to 160 characters, without control characters or line separators". The conformance test rule for hostile IDs (`{1,64}`) does not change: it only looks at hostile IDs.

#### 7. Account (slice 2): login, exchange and session

- **Outbound (fixed URL built in `auth.ts`):** `https://www.epicgames.com/id/login?redirectUrl=<encoded URL>`, with `redirectUrl` = `https://www.epicgames.com/id/api/redirect?clientId=<client_id>&responseType=code`. It is the URL that `legendary.gl/epiclogin` redirects to (checked on 22-10-2026). It opens in a new tab. `authHosts: ['www.epicgames.com']`.
- **Return:** the final page, on `www.epicgames.com`, is a JSON with `warning`, `redirectUrl`, `authorizationCode`, `exchangeCode` and `sid` (shape checked on 22-10-2026 without a session, with null codes; assumption EA2). The user copies the page and presses Paste.
- **`login` step:** `open-external`, `awaits: 'input'`, with the outbound URL. Body: "Sign in to Epic Games in the new tab. When you finish you will see text between braces: copy all of it and press Paste. Epic warns not to share that code: Ludiary uses it only on this computer to talk to Epic". Field `authorizationCode`: `secret: true`, `paste: true`, `extract: 'json-field:authorizationCode'`, `pattern: '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'` (assumption EA3), `maxLength: 4096`. A single step, with no `choose`, like GOG. The simulator (`apps/web/src/data/mock.ts`) changes Epic's step from `awaits: 'callback'` to this one.
- **More tolerant `extract: 'json-field:…'` (core and web, same change):** today the core (`cleanField` in `packages/core/src/wizards.ts`) rejects anything that is not a JSON, and the web (`validate.ts`) also accepts the bare value: they do not match. The same rule is decided for both: (1) the text is parsed as JSON; (2) if that fails, the piece between the first `{` and the last `}` is parsed (Chrome also copies the "Pretty print" checkbox if the whole page is selected); (3) if the text has no `{`, it is taken as is, without quotes around it (`legendary` also accepts the bare code). What is extracted then goes through `pattern`, which is the real validation. No type changes. **Clarified after the auditor:** if the parsed JSON is an object, the requested field is valid only if it is text (if it is missing or not text, there is no value); if it is a JSON text (`"…"`), that text is valid as a bare value; any other JSON (number, list, `null`) is treated as a bare value, which will then not pass `pattern`.
  - **Only the extracted value travels (M2):** with `json-field`, the web sends the server **only** the extracted value, never the pasted text. `exchangeCode` and `sid` from the same page are credentials: neither the web, nor the core, nor the connector reads them, logs them or returns them in an error or a message.
  - No host check like that of `url-query` (77, M1): a JSON has no origin to check. The risk is the same one 77 accepted: that someone convinces the user to paste a code from **another** account, which only connects Ludiary to that account. It is accepted.
- **Exchange** (`exchangeCode`): `POST https://account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com/account/api/oauth/token`, `basic` header, form `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code` (as a `Secret`) and `token_type=eg1` (assumption EA4).
  - 200 with `access_token` and `refresh_token` that match `^eg1~[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` and are 16 to 8192 long: correct (`eg1` is a signed JWT with the prefix `eg1~`). If not: `store.unexpected-response`.
  - 400 or 401: `auth.invalid` with `connectors.epic.error.code` ("The code has expired or was already used. Sign in again and copy the new text"). If the body has `errorCode` equal to `errors.com.epicgames.oauth.corrective_action_required` (Epic asks to accept something on its website): `auth.invalid` with `connectors.epic.error.corrective` ("Epic is asking you to confirm something on its website. Go to epicgames.com, accept it and connect again") (assumption EA6). From the error body only `errorCode` is compared with that constant; `errorMessage` is never read or logged.
  - 429: `store.rate-limited`. Other status: `store.unexpected-response`.
  - From the response, `displayName` → `accountLabel` is also read (without control characters, trimmed to 64; if missing, `done` without a name). **No other request is needed for the name**, unlike GOG. `account_id` and the rest are discarded; only the numbers `refresh_expires` and `expires_in` (seconds), which are not personal data, are logged, to close assumption EA5; also on each renewal.
- **On submit:** exchange → `secrets.set('refreshToken', …)` → `done` (with a name if there is one). The access token from the exchange is discarded. Nothing goes through `wizardState` (77, B4).
- **Renewal** (`refreshSession`, at the start of each `listLibrary`): the same `POST` with `grant_type=refresh_token`, `refresh_token` (as a `Secret`) and `token_type=eg1`.
  - Valid 200: **the first thing** is `secrets.set('refreshToken', <new>)` (Epic delivers a new one on each renewal; assumption EA5). If `set` fails, the error is propagated (77, A2).
  - 400, 401 or 403: `auth.expired` with `connectors.epic.error.expired`. 429 and network: as in 77. No readable `refreshToken`: `auth.required`.
- **Session lifetime (assumption EA5):** it is not known how long an unused launcher refresh token lasts; community documentation shows 28,800 s (8 h) for another client. If it were that short, someone who opens Ludiary once a day would have to reconnect almost every time. It will be known from the number logged in the manual test; if it is short, it is decided separately (for example, a warning on the Epic card). Nothing is added before knowing.
- **`status`, `disconnect`, epoch, `expired` and gray veil:** identical to 77 (points 5 and 9), with the scope `store:epic`. No remote revocation: `legendary` has a `DELETE …/oauth/sessions/kill/<token>`, but the `HttpClient` does not support `DELETE` and is not extended for this. `connectors.epic.disconnect.hint`: "Ludiary deletes its Epic session from this computer. To sign out of all sessions, change your password at epicgames.com".
- **Redactor** (`makeRedactor`, `runtime/src/files.ts`): adds `eg1~[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` → `[redacted]`, before the long-token pattern. It is a superset of the acceptance pattern (without it, the JWT header, under 64 characters, would remain visible; it is not secret, but this way nothing of the token is left). The authorization code, the `client_secret`, the `client_id` and the Epic IDs are 32-character hexadecimals: the Steam key pattern already masks them.

#### 8. Library (slice 2)

- **Time limit (added after the code audit, 22-10-2026):** each library catalog request carries 8 s like `resolveMedia`, so that a slow one does not consume the operation's 60 s. Requests already in flight when another fails finish on their own (the `HttpClient` has no per-request signal; a limitation accepted as in 76). The concurrency split (6 at a time) lives in `connectors/epic/src/pool.ts`.
- **`listLibrary`** (`connectors/epic/src/library.ts`):
  1. `refreshSession`.
  2. `GET https://library-service.live.use1a.on.epicgames.com/library/api/public/items` with `includeMetadata=true` and `platform=Windows` (Playnite), `authorization: bearer` as a `Secret`. Next page with `cursor` = `responseMetadata.nextCursor` until it does not come (assumption EA7). The cursor must be text of 1 to 2048 characters without control characters and is passed through `query`, never glued to the URL; a repeated cursor (loop) is `store.unexpected-response` (revised after the auditor). At most 200 pages and 50,000 records; if exceeded: `store.unexpected-response`. 401 or 403: `auth.expired`; 429; other status or a body without `records` as a list: `store.unexpected-response`.
  3. From each record, `namespace`, `catalogItemId` and `appName` with the shapes of point 6. A malformed one is skipped and leaves `complete: false` (rule of 74). `namespace === 'ue'` (Unreal Engine content) is skipped and counted, without touching `complete`. Duplicates by `storeGameId` are dropped.
  4. Catalog by namespace with the request of point 5, but with the user's token; at most 50 IDs per request and **6 requests at a time**. At most **2000 namespaces per sync** (revised after the auditor): the excess are not requested and the snapshot comes out with `complete: false`, so nothing is removed for not fitting. Per element:
     - `categories` with an `addons` path, or `mainGameItem` or `mainGameItemList` present (point 15): DLC, skipped and counted;
     - with a path that starts with `games`: game, `{ storeGameId, kind: 'game', title, media }`, with `title` sanitized and at most 300 (if missing, `Epic <appName>`) and `media` with the rules of point 5;
     - everything else (applications, digital content, engines): skipped and counted by type (assumption EA10);
     - a requested ID that does not come back: skipped and counted, without touching `complete`; the same `shortcut:` as 77 (a game withdrawn from the catalog does not appear).
     - 401 or 403: `auth.expired`; 429: `store.rate-limited`; other status or a body that is not an object: `store.unexpected-response` for the entire sync (the library is not touched).
  5. `complete: true` if everything went well, there were no malformed records and the namespace cap was not exceeded.
- **Time (assumption EA9):** 1 renewal, a few pages and about N/6 catalog rounds (N = namespaces). With 1000 games and about 300 ms per request that is about 50 s, close to the operation's 60 s (74). `shortcut:` if a real library does not fit, it moves to the cross-namespace request of point 5, after checking its response. Epic libraries grow with the weekly free games: the tester notes the number of games and the duration in the test.
- **Core:** no changes. Same `storeGameId` as the scan = same ownership; the API title replaces `DisplayName` (rule of 74); intervals of 50 and 74 (30-minute floor, 12 hours on opening the web).

#### 9. Manifest and contract (`contractVersion` stays at 1)

```ts
// connectors/epic/src/index.ts — cut 1 (ADR 78)
export function createEpicConnector(): StoreConnector {
  return {
    contractVersion: 1,
    id: "epic",
    nameKey: "connectors.epic.name" as I18nKey,
    access: "unofficial-api",
    capabilities: {
      library: false, scan: true, dlc: "none",
      actions: ["play"], launchKinds: ["uri"], uriSchemes: ["com.epicgames.launcher"],
      storePlaytime: false, price: false,
    },
    minSyncIntervalMs: 1_800_000,                 // ADR 50
    authHosts: [],
    apiHosts: ["account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com", "catalog-public-service-prod06.ol.epicgames.com"],
    mediaHosts: ["cdn1.epicgames.com", "cdn2.unrealengine.com"],
    locations: EPIC_LOCATIONS,                    // epic-launcher-data (point 3)
    externalTools: [],                            // point 2
    scanInstalled: scanEpicInstalled,
    discoverRoots: discoverEpicRoots,
    // resolveMedia: resolveEpicMedia — not declared: the catalog answers app tokens with stubs (point 15)
    resolveAction: resolveEpicAction,
  };
}
// cut 2: library: true; actions ["play", "install"]; authHosts ["www.epicgames.com"];
// apiHosts += "library-service.live.use1a.on.epicgames.com"; locations += epic-launcher (always: E5 verified, see points 4 and 14);
// connection: epicConnection; listLibrary: listEpicLibrary.
```

- **No new types.** Changes outside the connector, all small and compatible:
  - slice 1: `storeGameId` limit to 160 in `core` and its comment in `contracts` (point 6); invented Epic IDs in `privacy.ts` (point 10);
  - slice 2: tolerant `json-field` in `core` and `web` (point 7); `eg1~` pattern in the redactor; invented tokens in `privacy.ts`.
- **Package `connectors/epic`** (`@ludiary/connector-epic`, `"private": true`): `src/` (`manifest.ts`, `item.ts`, `ids.ts`, `scan.ts`, `launch.ts`, `auth.ts`, `media.ts`, `index.ts`; in slice 2 also `wizard.ts` and `library.ts`), `locales/es.json` and `en.json` (`connectors.epic.*`), `fixtures/` and tests with `connector-testkit`. `auth.ts` already exists in slice 1: the client constants and the application token.
- **`runtime`:** `createConnectors()` adds `createEpicConnector()`; `packages/i18n/src/connectors.ts` its line. The platform already supports `uri`.
- **Web:** slice 1, the Epic card stays as GOG's did in 76 (installed-only mode active, wizard still in the simulator). Slice 2, `real.ts` extends the closed list of stores with a real wizard to `['steam', 'gog', 'epic']`, without `sessionStorage` (no redirect, like GOG).
- **New texts** (es and en): `connectors.epic.errors.invalidId`, `connectors.epic.errors.launcherMissing` (slice 2), `connectors.epic.login.title`, `.login.body`, `.login.field`, `connectors.epic.error.code`, `.error.corrective`, `.error.expired` and `connectors.epic.disconnect.hint`.

#### 10. Tests

- **Invented fixtures.** The privacy check (`packages/connector-testkit/src/privacy.ts`) rejects any 32-character hexadecimal, and Epic's namespaces, catalog IDs, `client_id`, `client_secret` and codes are such. That is why there is **no real recorded response** from Epic, not even from the public catalog, and:
  - `ALLOWED` admits as fictional the 32-character hexadecimals that start with 24 zeros: `(?<![0-9A-Za-z])0{24}[0-9a-f]{8}(?![0-9A-Za-z])`. No real ID has that shape. The namespace `000000000000000000000000000000a1`…, catalog ID `00000000000000000000000000000001`…, `appName` `TestGame01`…, code `00000000000000000000000000c0de01` and `account_id` `00000000000000000000000000000a01` are used;
  - slice 2: `FICTIONAL_EPIC_VALUES` with `eg1~epic-test.access.token`, `eg1~epic-test.refresh.token`, `eg1~epic-test.refresh.token-2` and `eg1~epic-test.client.token` (they match the acceptance pattern). `displayName` `TestUser`;
  - images with the shape `https://cdn1.epicgames.com/offer/000000000000000000000000000000a1/test-cover_1200x1600-0000`; paths under `C:\Games` or `X:\Epic Games`, never `C:\Users\…`;
  - the tests compare the `basic` header with the one computed from the constants of `auth.ts`; the `client_secret` appears in no file under `fixtures/` or in tests. A repository test checks that its value is only in `connectors/epic/src/auth.ts` (like B1 of 77). **Clarified after the auditor:** the test walks **all** the files of `git ls-files`, including `docs/` and `.claude/`, and searches for both the secret and `base64(client_id:client_secret)`.
  - `privacy.ts` adds a rule of its own, "Epic eg1 token", which rejects any `eg1~` followed by token characters that is not one of `FICTIONAL_EPIC_VALUES` (revised after the auditor).
- **Slice 1, `connectors/epic`:**
  - `.item`: with and without BOM, broken JSON, missing each required field, `InstallLocation` relative, with `/`, with a trailing slash or with a control character, and each case of the strict rule of point 14, M1 (skipped and counted, never `internal`); `bIsIncompleteInstall`; DLC by `MainGameAppName` and by `addons`; `AppCategories` without `games`; namespace `ue`; title missing, non-ASCII and over 300; catalog ID in uppercase (comes out lowercase).
  - `discoverRoots`: data folder always; parents grouped case-insensitively; drive root → game folder with `tag: 'game'`; no `Manifests` → only the data folder; incomplete games and DLC generate no root.
  - `scanInstalled` with `memoryFiles`: data folder not among the roots → empty; game inside an active root; game whose root is not there (disabled) → skipped **without** touching the disk outside roots; nonexistent `InstallLocation`; locked `.item` and `readDir` of `Manifests` with an error → **all** roots unreadable; nonexistent `Manifests` → empty with readable roots; a join that escapes → skipped; cap of 2000; repeated ID; the log carries no paths, titles or IDs.
  - `resolveAction`: exact `play` URI with the three segments and `%3A`, built from the groups and with the final assertion; namespace `fn` preserved and uppercase hexadecimal namespace lowercased; ID that does not match the pattern (with an extra `:`, `/`, `?`, `&`, spaces, uppercase in the catalog ID) → `action.unsupported` without echo; null `installPath` → `not-installed`; other actions → `null`.
  - `resolveMedia` with `fakeHttp`: application token (exact form and header); grouping by namespace with repeated `id` in the URL; `DieselGameBoxTall` and its fallback `OfferImageTall`; disallowed host omitted; ID that does not come back; 404; 401 and 403 of the token; 429 that cuts immediately; over 8 s; 500 and a body that is not an object → throws; at most 6 in flight; more than 50 IDs of one namespace → several requests; batch with no valid ID → no request, not even the token one; the application token never appears in the log or in an error.
  - `assertConnectorConformance`.
- **Slice 1, outside the connector:** `core`, a 158-character `storeGameId` is accepted in scan and library and a 161-character one is rejected; `runtime`, registration of the three connectors and CSP parity with the two new hosts; `i18n`, parity with `connectors/epic/locales`; `privacy.ts`, the zeros pattern is admitted and any other 32-character hexadecimal is still rejected; Playwright, an Epic data tree in a temporary folder (manifest and game folder), `LocationResolver` double and a `ProcessLauncher` that records: the game appears with the unofficial-route icon and Play records the exact URI.
- **Slice 2:** the same tests as 77 adapted: exact outbound URL (with encoded `redirectUrl`); exchange with exact form, header and `token_type`; 400 and 401 → `auth.invalid`; `corrective_action_required` → its key; `errorMessage` never in the result or in the log; tokens that do not match the pattern; `displayName` sanitized and absent; `refresh_expires` and `expires_in` logged as numbers; renewal with `set` **before** the first request to the library; 400, 401 and 403 → `auth.expired`; cursor pagination, repeated cursor, empty cursor, over 2048 or with control characters, cap on pages and records, malformed record (`complete: false`), namespace `ue`; more than 2000 namespaces → `complete: false` without requesting the excess; catalog with game, DLC (`addons` and `mainGameItem`), application and ID that does not come back; `bearer` only to the Epic hosts that need it, never to the CDN; Install with launcher, without launcher and with `ModSdkCommand` with `/`; epoch changed midway. In `core` and `web`, `json-field` with JSON, with text around the braces, with the bare code, between quotes, with a JSON text, with a number or a list, with a JSON without the field and with the field not text; the web sends only the extracted value; `exchangeCode` and `sid` with a value do not appear in the request, in the log or in any error. In `runtime`, the redactor masks a whole `eg1~` token. Playwright: Epic wizard against an Epic double → not-installed games → Install records the URI with `action=install` → disconnecting leaves the veil.
- **Manual guide** (`docs/manual-tests/epic.md`, prepared by the `tester` and run by the user; point 11).

#### 11. Manual test (slice 1, and "Account" section for slice 2)

- **Preparation:** sign in to the Epic launcher, get **Home – A Unique Horror Adventure** (free on the Epic store from 22-10-2026 at 17:00 to 29-10-2026 at 16:00, peninsular Spanish time, according to the public promotions feed consulted on 22-10-2026; it is a small 2D game) and install it in a folder with spaces and an "ñ", for example `X:\Epic Games ñ`. If the user already has another small Epic game in their account, that one will do. It has to be obtained **before 29-10-2026**.
- **Slice 1, what to check:**
  1. A `.item` appears in `C:\ProgramData\Epic\EpicGamesLauncher\Data\Manifests`. Copy into the ADR, sanitized (without user paths), the names of its fields and the values of `AppCategories`, `bIsIncompleteInstall`, `MainGameAppName` and the shape (length and characters, not the value) of `CatalogNamespace`, `CatalogItemId` and `AppName` (E2, E6). Look whether the game folder has `.egstore\*.mancpn` and which fields it carries (E10).
  2. ~~`reg query "HKCU\Software\Epic Games\EOS" /v ModSdkCommand`: note whether it exists and whether it points to the `EpicGamesLauncher.exe` on `E:` (E5).~~ Already checked on 22-10-2026 (E5). Only check that Settings shows the data folder resolved by `AppDataPath` (E1).
  3. Ludiary with autodetection: Settings shows the data folder and the Epic library; after the scan, the game appears with its title and its vertical cover (E7, E8). If there is no cover, note the image host from the log.
  4. Play with the launcher **closed**: it starts the launcher in the background and then the game, without showing the launcher window (E3). Repeat with the launcher open.
  5. Disable the library folder in Settings: the game disappears after the scan. Enable it again.
  6. With "manual folders only": Epic does not show the game (decided behavior, point 13.3).
  7. Uninstall from the launcher and scan: the game disappears.
  8. The exported log contains no Epic paths, titles or IDs.
- **Slice 2, "Account (ADR 78)" section:**
  1. Connect in Chrome, Edge and Firefox: the login opens in a new tab, the final page is the JSON and Paste accepts it, both copying the whole page and copying only the code (EA2, EA3). Note only the shape of the code.
  2. "Connected as <name>".
  3. Not-installed games: the number matches the library on Epic's website without DLC; note the number of games and how long the first sync takes (EA9). No owned game is missing; if any is missing, note its title.
  4. The installed game appears only once, with the API title.
  5. Install a not-installed game: the launcher opens its installation dialog (E4). If it does nothing, note what happens.
  6. Note the `refresh_expires` and the `expires_in` from the log (EA5). Sync twice, more than 30 minutes apart, and the next day: it stays connected, or becomes "Needs reconnecting".
  7. Change the password at epicgames.com and sync: `expired`; reconnect.
  8. Disconnect: gray veil on the not-installed games; the installed one is still playable.
  9. The exported log contains no `authorizationCode`, `eg1~`, `bearer`, `basic`, account name or Epic IDs.

#### 12. Implementation order and parallel work

1. **First** (`developer`, small): `storeGameId` limit to 160 in `core` with its comment in `contracts` and its tests; the fictional ID pattern in `privacy.ts`.
2. **In parallel:**
   - `connectors`: the complete slice 1 `connectors/epic` against `connector-testkit` (points 3 to 6 and 9, and their tests);
   - `developer`: registration in `runtime`, CSP and `vite.config.ts`, `i18n` line;
   - `auditor`: review of this design before the code (the launcher client in the repository, the application token, the root rule of `scanInstalled` and the limit of 160).
3. **Afterwards:** Playwright and `auditor` review of the code.
4. **Manual test of slice 1** (point 11) with the E assumptions closed in this ADR, and the `docs-writer`: guide (Epic detected only with autodetection; Play opens the launcher), privacy (Epic catalog with the detected IDs) and notice about the unofficial route.
5. **Slice 2**, with what was learned: first tolerant `json-field` in `core` and `web`, the redactor and the fictional values; in parallel `connectors` (`auth.ts`, `wizard.ts`, `library.ts`, `install`, the `epic-launcher` location) and `developer` (`real.ts`, simulator); `auditor` review before and after; manual test of the account; `docs-writer`: connection guide with screenshots (copying the text between braces, Epic's warning), privacy and troubleshooting.

#### 13. What the user decides (product only)

**Applied by default (22-10-2026), unless the user says otherwise**, by analogy with what they chose for Steam and GOG: 13.1 (a), 13.2 (a) and 13.3 (a).

1. **Account name:** (a) "Connected as <name>", with `displayName` from the exchange response, with no extra request (recommended); (b) just "Connected".
2. **Installing without the Epic launcher:** (a) message "The Epic Games launcher is required" (E5 already checked); (b) open the store page in the browser, which needs a new decision (like 12.2 of 77).
3. **"Manual folders only" mode:** (a) Epic does not detect installed games without its manifests, and the guide says so (recommended: zero code, and Play needs the launcher anyway); (b) add the game folder by hand and read `.egstore\*.mancpn`, only if the test confirms E10, in a small later change.
4. **Test game:** Home – A Unique Horror Adventure, which has to be obtained before 29-10-2026, or another small game already in their account.

#### 14. Auditor review of the design (October 22, 2026)

No critical or high findings. Everything is incorporated into the previous points; here, the summary and what does not fit in them.

- **M1. The `.item` files are untrusted input.** `C:\ProgramData\Epic` gives full control to `BUILTIN\Users` (checked on 22-10-2026): any account on the computer can write a manifest. `InstallLocation` must meet the **same rule as `localPath` in `process-launcher.ts`** (decision 76, second barrier), and in addition not be a drive root:
  - it starts with `^[A-Za-z]:\\` (no UNC, `\\?\` or `\\.\`), after changing `/` to `\` and removing trailing slashes;
  - no component empty, `.` or `..`, nor ending in a dot or a space;
  - no `:` after position 1 and none of `"<>|?*` or control characters;
  - no component that is a reserved device name (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM0` to `COM9`, `LPT0` to `LPT9`, case-insensitive and also with an extension);
  - it is not a drive root (`C:\`).
  - If it does not comply: it is skipped and counted, **never** `internal` (a file from another user must not stop the scan). The same rule applies in `discoverRoots` before proposing a root. The maximum effect of a fake `.item`, once inside the roots, is to show a nonexistent game or one with another title, and Play only opens a launcher URI with validated IDs: there is no `exec`.
- **M2. `json-field`:** the web sends only the extracted value; `exchangeCode` and `sid` are never read, logged or returned (point 7).
- **M3. Nonexistent versus unreadable `Manifests`:** nonexistent → empty with readable roots (installs are marked removed); `readDir` with an error → all roots unreadable (point 3).
- **Low findings, incorporated:** exact `json-field` rule by JSON type (point 7); cursor validated and repeated → `store.unexpected-response` (point 8); cap of 2000 namespaces per sync with `complete: false` (point 8); 50 IDs per request and no application token if there is no valid batch (point 5); URI from the pattern groups with a final assertion and namespace lowercased only if it is a 32-character hexadecimal (points 4 and 6); `client_secret` test over all of `git ls-files` and also in base64 (point 10); own `privacy.ts` rule for `eg1~` (point 10); `expires_in` logged together with `refresh_expires` (point 7).
- **E5 verified** (`ModSdkCommand` in `HKCU`, with `/` and without quotes): the `epic-launcher` location and the Install check always go in slice 2; launcher present = location resolved to the `.exe` (point 4). **`AppDataPath`** (`HKLM`, 64-bit view, with trailing slash; it does not exist in `WOW6432Node`) becomes the first source of the data folder, with the known folder as a fallback (point 3). E1 is half-verified.
- **Outside the ADR, for the user:** the definitions of the `connectors` and `auditor` agents (`.claude/agents/`) still cite `legendary`. They are not touched here; the user decides whether to update them.

#### 15. Real requests without an account and slice 1 implementation decisions (October 22, 2026)

**Checked by the `connectors` agent with real requests without an account:**

- The application token (`client_credentials`, `token_type=eg1`) answers 200 with `expires_in` 14,400, without its own `User-Agent` (EA8, in part).
- The catalog by namespace answers 401 without a token and 200 with the application token. For the 11 third-party games of the free games feed it returns an incomplete element: no `keyImages`, with `categories` only `audience` or `public` and with internal titles (`DevGeneralAudience`). Only Fortnite (namespace `fn`) brings `keyImages` (`DieselGameBox` and `DieselGameBoxTall`, on `cdn1.epicgames.com`).
- **Consequence:** E7 is false in practice and `resolveMedia` is not declared (point 5). Slice 1 has no covers for installed games until the account is connected. The CSP keeps the two hosts, which slice 2 will use.

**Risk for slice 2:** if the catalog also returned incomplete elements without `categories` with the **user's** token, `listLibrary`, which filters by `games` paths (point 8), would come out empty. It is the **first** thing the slice 2 manual test checks, before the rest of the "Account" section. If it happens, the game criterion is decided separately (for example, the `.item` or the library records).

**Connector decisions, incorporated into the design:**

- **DLC:** a catalog element with `mainGameItemList` is also marked DLC, besides `mainGameItem` (point 8).
- **`.item` without `AppCategories`:** treated as a game (revises for that case step 5 of the scan in point 3, which skipped it). `shortcut:` an old or trimmed manifest must not hide an installed game; an `AppCategories` that is present and without `games` is still skipped.
- **Play without `installPath`:** `launch.not-installed` without `messageKey`. The interface uses the common text `connectors.common.errors.launch.not-installed`.
- **E5:** closed (point 14).

#### Epic assumptions, slice 1 (verify in the manual test; those marked "unverified" have no source other than the one indicated)

- **E1 (half-verified):** the manifests are in `<AppDataPath>\Manifests`. Checked on 22-10-2026: `AppDataPath` exists in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Epic Games\EpicGamesLauncher` (64-bit view, with trailing slash, not in `WOW6432Node`), the folder `C:\ProgramData\Epic\EpicGamesLauncher\Data\Manifests` exists with the launcher on `E:`, and GameFinder gives it as the default folder. It remains to be seen that the launcher writes the test game's `.item` there.
- **E2 (unverified):** each `.item` is a JSON with `DisplayName`, `AppName`, `CatalogNamespace`, `CatalogItemId`, `InstallLocation`, `LaunchExecutable`, `bIsIncompleteInstall`, `MainGameAppName` and `AppCategories`; games carry `games` in `AppCategories`, and DLC, `addons` or a different `MainGameAppName`. Sources: example from the GameFinder wiki and the jayd.ml article; the category rule has no direct source.
- **E3:** `com.epicgames.launcher://apps/<namespace>%3A<catalogItemId>%3A<appName>?action=launch&silent=true` starts the game. It is the format of the launcher's shortcuts (Steam forums thread with the Final Fantasy VII Remake one); the scheme is registered on the user's computer (checked). It remains to be seen that it starts with the launcher closed.
- **E4 (unverified):** the same URI with `action=install` opens the installation dialog. No direct source.
- **E5 (checked on 22-10-2026 on the user's computer):** `HKCU\Software\Epic Games\EOS`, value `ModSdkCommand`, holds the path of `EpicGamesLauncher.exe` (the one on `E:`), with `/` as separator and without quotes. GameFinder cites `ModSdkMetadataDir` in that key.
- **E6 (unverified):** the catalog ID is a 32-character hexadecimal; the namespace matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` and the `appName`, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,60}`, with the same use of uppercase in the `.item` and in the library. Those in the public feed are lowercase 32-character hexadecimals (checked on 22-10-2026); there are readable `appName`s (`Fortnite`) and others hexadecimal.
- **E7 (false in practice, checked on 22-10-2026):** the catalog accepts the `client_credentials` token (200; without a token, 401), but for third-party games it returns incomplete elements, without `keyImages`. Details in point 15.
- **E8 (in part):** the images are on `cdn1.epicgames.com` and `cdn2.unrealengine.com` (checked in the public feed on 22-10-2026); the types `DieselGameBoxTall` and `DieselGameBox` of the catalog, and their hosts, unverified.
- **E9:** many games need the launcher or an exchange code to start. Checked in the `legendary` code (`core.py`, `get_launch_parameters`: `-AUTH_PASSWORD` with an exchange code and `-epicovt` with an ownership token for games that ask for it). Which specific games require it is not known.
- **E10 (unverified):** the game folder has `.egstore\*.mancpn` with `AppName`, `CatalogNamespace` and `CatalogItemId`. No source; not used (point 13.3).
- **E11:** `GET …/catalog/api/shared/namespace/<ns>/bulk/items?id=…` returns an object with one entry per catalog ID, with `title`, `categories`, `keyImages` and `mainGameItem`. The request is confirmed by `legendary` (`egs.py`), Playnite (`EpicAccountClient.cs`) and `egs-api` (`egs.rs`); the shape of the response, only by how `legendary` uses it.

#### Epic account assumptions, slice 2

- **EA1 (unverified):** Epic does not offer third parties an OAuth registration with access to the library and tolerates the use of the launcher's client. Only its public use by `legendary`, Heroic, Playnite and `egs-api` is known.
- **EA2:** the login URL and the final page in JSON with `authorizationCode`. Checked on 22-10-2026: `legendary.gl/epiclogin` redirects to that URL, and `www.epicgames.com/id/api/redirect` answers, without a session, `{"warning":…,"redirectUrl":…,"authorizationCode":null,"exchangeCode":null,"sid":null}`. Still to do with a session.
- **EA3 (unverified):** the code is a lowercase 32-character hexadecimal (what the `validate.test.ts` test and public use expect). `legendary` accepts the JSON or the bare code (checked in `cli.py`).
- **EA4:** `POST /account/api/oauth/token` with a form, `basic` client authentication and `token_type=eg1`; response with `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, `refresh_expires`, `account_id` and `displayName`; `eg1` is a signed JWT with the prefix `eg1~`. Confirmed in `legendary` (`egs.py`), `egs-api` (`login.rs`), Playnite and the community documentation (FortniteEndpointsDocumentation, `Token.md`).
- **EA5 (unverified):** each renewal delivers a new refresh token; its lifetime is not known (28,800 s in the community documentation, for another client). It is closed with `refresh_expires` and `expires_in` logged.
- **EA6 (unverified):** an invalid code or refresh token gives 400 or 401 with `errorCode`; `corrective_action_required` exists. `legendary` treats any 4xx with `errorCode` as invalid credentials.
- **EA7:** `GET library-service…/library/api/public/items` with `includeMetadata`, paginated with `responseMetadata.nextCursor` and `cursor`. Confirmed in `legendary`, `egs-api` and Playnite (the latter with `platform=Windows`). That each record carries `namespace`, `catalogItemId` and `appName`, by how `legendary` uses it; without seeing a response.
- **EA8 (confirmed on 22-10-2026 for the application token):** Epic does not require a launcher `User-Agent`: `client_credentials` with `token_type=eg1` gives 200 without its own `User-Agent`. Still to do with user tokens.
- **EA9 (unverified):** request limits of the catalog and the library undocumented; 6 requests at a time and about 300 ms per request.
- **EA10 (unverified):** `categories` uses paths `games…`, `addons…`, `applications` and others, as in the public feed (checked there on 22-10-2026); `mainGameItem` marks a DLC (from `legendary`'s `includeMainGameDetails`).

Sources consulted on October 22, 2026: [`legendary`, `api/egs.py`](https://github.com/derrod/legendary/blob/master/legendary/api/egs.py), [`cli.py`](https://github.com/derrod/legendary/blob/master/legendary/cli.py) and [`core.py`](https://github.com/derrod/legendary/blob/master/legendary/core.py); [`legendary.gl/epiclogin`](https://legendary.gl/epiclogin) (redirect); [`www.epicgames.com/id/api/redirect`](https://www.epicgames.com/id/api/redirect); [`egs-api`](https://docs.rs/crate/egs-api/0.9.0), [`egs.rs`](https://github.com/AchetaGames/egs-api-rs/blob/master/src/api/egs.rs) and [`login.rs`](https://github.com/AchetaGames/egs-api-rs/blob/master/src/api/login.rs); [Playnite, `EpicAccountClient.cs`](https://github.com/JosefNemec/PlayniteExtensions/blob/master/source/Libraries/EpicLibrary/Services/EpicAccountClient.cs); [FortniteEndpointsDocumentation, `Token.md`](https://github.com/LeleDerGrasshalmi/FortniteEndpointsDocumentation/blob/main/EpicGames/AccountService/Authentication/Token.md); [GameFinder, Epic Games Store](https://github.com/erri120/GameFinder/wiki/Epic-Games-Store); [jayd.ml, Epic and Steam libraries](https://jayd.ml/games/2020/05/16/epic-games-store-steam-libraries.html); [Steam forums, Epic shortcut](https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/4286935719733617676/); [Epic public promotions feed](https://store-site-backend-static.ak.epicgames.com/freeGamesPromotions?locale=es-ES&country=ES&allowCountries=ES).

**Reason:** with the launcher's manifests, the URI of its own shortcuts and the catalog, Epic fits in the contract **without new types**: the only thing the contract did not allow was a 158-character ID, and raising a validation limit is the smallest way to carry in the ID everything the URI and the catalog ask for, without `launchData` in the library. Playing through the launcher is the only thing that works with games that require the Epic session at startup, and it has the same shape as Steam. Direct HTTP avoids, as in 77, a Python binary, one more GPL and the `ExternalToolRunner`. Separating two slices makes it possible to validate scan, Play and covers, the biggest risk, without secrets, and to postpone the account assumptions (session lifetime, library shape) until there is a real game to check them with. Alternatives discarded: `legendary` (point 2); direct `exec` (point 4); `LauncherInstalled.dat` and `.mancpn` as a source (point 3); the store's GraphQL for covers (point 5); storing the catalog ID alone and the rest in `launchData` (Install could not build the URI).

**Consequences:**

- Third store with network output and two more image hosts in the CSP. First application token (without a user) obtained with a public client.
- Rule 7 of decision 40 is revised for Epic as well: no store uses external tools, and the `legendary` license no longer affects distribution (decision 60). The Epic part of decision 43 is revised: without a `legendary` window, the pasted JSON is the route.
- The Epic row of the table of 40 becomes "`uri` (`com.epicgames.launcher`) of the launcher".
- The core accepts `storeGameId` of up to 160 characters for all stores.
- Without the launcher's data folder ("manual folders only" mode), Epic does not show installed games.
- Before closing each slice, the `auditor` reviews: the client constants and their single appearance in `auth.ts`, the application token, the root and error rule of `scanInstalled`, the limit of 160, and in slice 2 the save order, the `bearer` header as a `Secret`, the tolerant `json-field`, the `eg1~` redactor and the fixtures.
- The `tester` prepares `docs/manual-tests/epic.md` (point 11); the `docs-writer`, the guides of steps 4 and 5 of point 12.

#### 16. User's manual test (October 23, 2026, Windows 11, launcher in `X:\Epic Games\Launcher`, real account)

The user: "it comes out perfect". Before connecting the account only the installed game appeared, without a cover (as point 15 foresees: no `resolveMedia`); on connecting, all the account's games appeared, with covers. Review of the real logs, read-only:
- **Scan (slice 1):** `games=1 incomplete=0 dlc=0 notGame=0 outsideRoots=0 missing=0 invalid=0`: the real `.item` is read with the expected fields (E1, E2 as far as used) and the Play URI works (E3, according to the user).
- **Account (slice 2):** exchange and renewal correct; with the user's token the catalog does bring `categories` and `keyImages`, so the risk of point 15 (empty library because of stubs) **does not occur**. 27 DLC were skipped (`type_dlc=27`), no image from a foreign host (`foreignImageHosts` empty) and no malformed record.
- **EA5, closed:** `refreshExpires=31540000` (about 365 days) and `accessExpires=129600` (36 h). Periodic reconnection is not a problem.
- **Privacy:** in `server.log` and `launcher.log` there is no `eg1~`, `authorizationCode`, `exchangeCode`, 32-character hexadecimal, email, user path, Windows user name or `.exe`.
- Not tested in this pass: Install from Ludiary (E4), uninstalling, reconnecting and expired session; the user gave no step-by-step detail beyond "it comes out perfect".
### 79. Ubisoft Connect connector: installed games from the registry and Play with `uplay://` (extends decisions 40, 42 and 72; revises the Ubisoft row of the table in 40 and, from 72, what `LocationResolver` does when the registry cannot be read; covers, Install, account and library, and the dropping of `configurations` and `access`, revised in decision 80)

**Decision (recommended, October 22, 2026):** the user commissions the Ubisoft Connect connector on the `feature/ubisoftconector` branch. It is the equivalent of 76 for Ubisoft, but smaller: Ubisoft has no account or API (decisions 11, 16 and 40), so the whole slice is detecting the installed games and playing them. The numbering skips 78 (Epic), which is on another branch not yet merged.

**Starting point:** the user's PC has no Ubisoft Connect (checked on 22-10-2026, read-only: neither `HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Ubisoft\Launcher` nor `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Ubisoft\Launcher` exists, and the `uplay` and `ubisoft` schemes are not registered). What follows about Ubisoft comes from public sources (Playnite, Lutris and the GOG Galaxy integration for Uplay) and stays an assumption (list at the end) until the manual test in point 9.

#### 1. Scope

- **In:**
  - detection of the installed Ubisoft games through the registry (`Launcher\Installs\<gameId>`), with auto-detection (decision 42);
  - title taken from the game folder name (point 3);
  - Play with `uplay://launch/<gameId>/0`, after checking that Ubisoft Connect is installed (point 4);
  - the `connectors/ubisoft` connector registered in `runtime`, with its texts;
  - two small changes outside the connector that Ubisoft needs and that apply to all stores: the subkey name in registry locations, and telling "the key does not exist" apart from "it could not be read" (point 2).
- **Not applicable:**
  - **Install:** without an account there are no non-installed games (decision 16), so there is nothing to install. `actions: ['play']`. (Revised in decision 80: with the account connected, owned games that are not installed appear, and Install opens Ubisoft Connect with `uplay://install/<id>`.)
  - **Account, `connection` and `listLibrary`:** rule of decision 40 for `local-only` stores. (Revised in decision 80: Ubisoft has an account, with a built-in login window, `connection` and `listLibrary` using the Ubisoft API, and becomes `access: 'unofficial-api'`.)
- **Out:**
  - **Covers** (point 5): no cover, with the gradient.
  - **DLC:** `dlc: 'none'`. There is no evidence that Ubisoft creates `Installs` subkeys for its DLC (assumption U10).
  - **Cross-store matching** (decision 76, point 1): a Ubisoft game bought on Steam or Epic may appear twice (assumption U11).
  - **Playtime** (slice 2b, point 7).

#### 2. Contract (extends decisions 40 and 72; `contractVersion` stays at 1)

**Problem:** the game ID is only in the **name** of the subkey (`Installs\<gameId>`), and today `registry-subkeys` returns only the value (`InstallDir`), not the name. No file in the game folder gives the ID reliably (point 3). Without the name, Ludiary would know where Ubisoft games are, but not which ones they are, and could not launch them.

**Options:**

- **A. Subkey name in `ResolvedLocation`, and the connector stores it in the root's `tag`** (recommended). One discovered root per game, with `tag: 'game-<gameId>'`. The `tag` is already stored with the root (decision 72) and comes back in `ScanRoot`, so no migration or core change is needed for the ID to reach `scanInstalled`.
  - Advantages: one optional field in a type and one more list in the Go helper's response; no migration; works equally for other stores that keep data in the subkey name.
  - Costs: Settings shows one detected folder per Ubisoft game; the cap of 64 discovered roots per store (decision 72) limits it to 64 installed Ubisoft games; the `tag` stops being just a label and becomes connector data.
- **B. Pass the resolved locations to `ScanContext`.** The scan would see the (ID, folder) pairs without using the `tag`. Costs: a new field in `ScanContext`, and when discovery fails the core uses the stored roots, which do not have the names: they would have to be stored (migration) or Ubisoft would be left with no games in that case.
- **C. A new kind of `LocationSource` that returns several values per subkey.** This is what 76 rejected for GOG: more code in the helper and in the platform for the same result.

**A is chosen.** Changes:

```ts
// packages/contracts/src/connector.ts — ADR 79
export interface ResolvedLocation {
  readonly declarationId: string;
  readonly path: string;
  /** Opaque to the core, ^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$, stored with the root and handed back in ScanRoot. A connector may encode an id in it (ADR 79). */
  readonly tag?: string;
  /**
   * ADR 79. Only from a 'registry-subkeys' source: name of the subkey the path was read from. Untrusted text: the
   * connector validates it before any use. The core does not store it, so it never arrives in ScanRoot.
   */
  readonly subkey?: string;
}

// packages/contracts/src/ports.ts — ADR 79: comment of LocationResolver.resolve
/**
 * Every distinct existing path of the declaration on this OS, in source order (deduplicated with LocalFiles.compareKey).
 * A key or value that does not exist is not an error (it yields nothing). Throws if a registry source could not be read
 * (helper failed, access denied, any other error): absent and unreadable are not the same (ADR 79).
 */
resolve(decl: LocationDeclaration): Promise<readonly ResolvedLocation[]>;
```

- **Go helper** (`apps/desktop/tray-helper/registry.go`): with `kind: 'subkeys'`, the result adds `names`, the same length as `values` and in the same order: the name of each subkey whose value was read. The names already meet what the helper requires of a key (UTF-8, no NUL, at most 255 characters). ~~The cap of 256 subkeys does not change.~~ (Revised by the auditor, point 12, A2 and M3: a subkey is skipped only if its error is `not-found` or `unsupported-type`; and with more than 256 subkeys the response carries `truncated: true`, which counts as a failure.)
- **Platform** (`registry-protocol.ts` and `location-resolver.ts`):
  - `parseRegistryResponse` accepts `names` only if it has the same length as `values` and each name is text of 1 to 255 characters with no control characters. Otherwise that response counts as failed.
  - The resolver sets `subkey` on every location that comes from a `registry-subkeys` source, and on no other.
  - **Absent versus unreadable** (revises the sentence in 72 "callers see fewer locations, not an error"): a `not-found` or `unsupported-type` response is an absence and yields nothing. If the helper fails, or a response carries any other error (`access-denied`, `failed`, `invalid-*`), `resolve` **throws**. Reason: today, if the helper fails, the core receives an empty list, deletes the stored discovered roots, and the scan removes the games. With Steam and GOG that costs one library; with Ubisoft, where each game is a root, all the games would be lost because of a transient failure.
  - ~~Apart from this, the resolver stays the same: local, absolute, normalized and existing path, no duplicates.~~ (Corrected by the auditor, point 12, A3 and M4: existence tells absence apart from a read error, and duplicates are counted by path and `subkey`.)
- **Core**, two one-line changes that apply to all stores:
  - ~~`discover` (`sync.ts`): if `resolve` throws on **any** `scan` declaration of the connector, it returns `null`. The stored roots stay as they were (behavior that already exists for `null`), and the code is logged as today.~~ (Revised by the auditor, point 12, M1: it is decided per declaration.)
  - `resolveLauncherLocations` (`launch.ts`): if `resolve` throws on any `launcher` declaration, it returns `resolved: false` (with what was resolved, point 12, B1). This way a helper failure does not turn into "Steam not found" or "Ubisoft Connect not found" (the `launchersResolved` rule of 72: an empty unresolved list proves nothing).
- `validateDiscoveredRoots` does not change: it already keeps `tag` if it matches `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` and ignores `subkey`.
- **Web:** the `tag` of a root is not shown as is. Today the web does not show it; if it ever does, `game-*` is translated as "folder of a game".
- Everything is additive (an optional field, one more list in the helper's internal protocol) or a change in the behavior of an OS port, not of the connector contract: `contractVersion` stays at 1.

#### 3. Scan

- **Single source: the registry.** `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Ubisoft\Launcher\Installs\<gameId>`, value `InstallDir` (in the 32-bit view it is `WOW6432Node`). The folder uses `/` as separator and a trailing slash, for example `D:/Ubisoft Games/Trackmania/` (assumption U1); the platform already normalizes it, as it does with `SteamPath`.
- **Discarded as a source:**
  - `settings.yml` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ubisoft Game Launcher\settings.yml`, `game_installation_path`): it only gives the default folder to install into, not which games exist or their IDs.
  - The launcher's `cache\configuration\configurations`: it is binary protobuf with YAML inside (this is how Playnite and Lutris read it), it can exceed 1 MiB and `ScopedFileReader` only reads UTF-8 text. It would give titles and covers, but requires a parser for an undocumented binary format.
  - The launcher's `data\<gameId>\`: the folder names are IDs, but it does not say where each game is installed.
- **Manifest, `locations`:**
  - `ubisoft-installs` (`scan`): `{ kind: 'registry-subkeys', hive: 'HKLM', key: 'SOFTWARE\\Ubisoft\\Launcher\\Installs', value: 'InstallDir', view: '32' }` and, as a second source of the same declaration, the same with `view: '64'`, as Playnite does (Ubisoft Connect is 32-bit and normally only the first exists; the second costs one line).
  - `ubisoft-launcher` (`launcher`): `{ kind: 'registry-value', hive: 'HKLM', key: 'SOFTWARE\\Ubisoft\\Launcher', value: 'InstallDir', view: '32' }` and `{ kind: 'known-folder', folder: 'ProgramFilesX86', relative: 'Ubisoft\\Ubisoft Game Launcher' }`. This is the Ubisoft Connect folder (assumption U3).
- **`discoverRoots`** (`connectors/ubisoft/src/scan.ts`), no I/O, text only. For each location of `ubisoft-installs`:
  1. `subkey` must match `^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$`. If not (or missing), it is skipped and counted.
  2. The path is treated as untrusted input even though the platform already filtered it: `/` is turned into `\`, trailing slashes are removed and the strict local path rule of `localPath` (`packages/platform-windows/src/process-launcher.ts`) is required: drive letter and `\`, no control characters, none of `"<>|?*/`, no `:` after position 1, no component that is a reserved device name, ends in a dot or space, or is `..`. Also, at least one component after the drive: a drive root (`X:\`) is not a game folder. If it does not comply, it is skipped and counted; it is never `internal`.
     - The rule is copied into `connectors/ubisoft/src/paths.ts` (a connector does not import `platform-windows`, decision 38), with the same tests. The Epic branch has its own in `item.ts` (confirmed by the auditor): they are unified on merge.
  3. No duplicates by path (lowercase key): if two IDs point to the same folder, the lower number is kept and the other ID is logged. It is sorted by numeric ID so the result is stable.
  4. Returns `{ declarationId: 'ubisoft-installs', path, tag: 'game-<gameId>' }`.
  - In the log, only counters (`invalidIds`, `invalidPaths`, `duplicates`) and IDs, never paths.
  - The core validates as usual (absolute, local, existing folder, at most 64) and stores the roots. An uninstalled game disappears from the registry, its root stops coming back and the core deletes it and removes the game (decision 72).
- **`scanInstalled`**, without reading any file:
  - It only uses `discovered` roots of `ubisoft-installs` whose `tag` matches `^game-([1-9][0-9]{0,9})$`. The ID comes from the group. The other roots, including the user's, are ignored without counting them as unreadable.
  - An ID already seen is skipped.
  - `ctx.fs.exists(root.path)`:
    - `true`: entry `{ storeGameId: id, kind: 'game', title, installPath: root.path }`, with no `media` or `launchData`;
    - `false` (**absent**, the folder no longer exists): no entry, and the root does not count as unreadable, so the game is removed;
    - read error (**unreadable**, `scan.root-unreadable`) or `PathEscapesRootsError`: the root goes to `unreadableRoots` and the game is kept (point 11 of 72). Any other `internal` is propagated. Same `isHandled` classification as GOG, copied.
  - **Title:** the last component of the path, without control characters, with spaces trimmed and at most 200 characters. If it ends up empty, `Ubisoft <id>` (a piece of data, not an interface text). This is what Playnite does for installed games. Ubisoft usually names the folder after the game (assumption U5); if not, the title will look odd until there is a metadata fallback (decision 6).
    - Discarded alternative: `DisplayName` of `Uninstall\Uplay Install <gameId>`. It needs a location with an ID inside the key, which is not a fixed declaration, or reading all of `Uninstall` with `registry-subkeys`, which often exceeds the cap of 256 subkeys and where "Uplay Install" is among the last in alphabetical order. If U5 fails in the manual test, it is decided separately.
  - `uplay_install.state` in the folder is not required: the Galaxy integration uses it to know whether an installation finished (first byte `0x0A`), but it is binary, is not present in all old games and does not carry the ID in a known way (assumption U9). A half-downloaded game may show up as installed; Play then opens Ubisoft Connect, which knows what state it is in.
- **Manual folders and "manual folders only":** there is no known file in the game folder that gives the `gameId` (U9). Without an ID there is no Play (the URI needs it), and an entry without an ID would be a game that cannot be opened. It is decided: **Ubisoft only detects with auto-detection.** With "manual folders only" or "configure it later" no Ubisoft game appears, and the Ubisoft card in Settings says so (`connectors.ubisoft.needsAutoDetection`: "Ubisoft Connect keeps its games in the Windows registry. To see them, turn on automatic detection"). This is what decision 42 ("the interface warns about it") and 69 already anticipated.

#### 4. Launch

**Options:**

- **A. URI `uplay://launch/<gameId>/0`** (recommended). Ubisoft Connect opens (asking to sign in if needed) and starts the game.
  - Advantages: it is the route used by Playnite, Lutris and the Galaxy integration; it does not need to know the executable; it meets the requirement of Ubisoft games, which almost always require the launcher (they carry `uplay_r1_loader` or `upc_r2_loader`, which is exactly what Playnite checks to know whether a game needs Ubisoft Connect).
  - Costs: it depends on Ubisoft Connect being installed and registering `uplay`; Ludiary does not know whether the game started (same as with Steam).
- **B. Direct `exec` of the game's executable.** Discarded: the registry does not say which the executable is (`configurations`, binary, would have to be read), and even if it were known, most Ubisoft games reopen the launcher or do not start without it.

**Format.** The sources use two forms: `uplay://launch/<id>/0` (community guides from 2015 and 2022, which copy it from the shortcuts Ubisoft Connect creates) and `uplay://launch/<id>` (Playnite, Lutris and the Galaxy integration). **`/0`** is chosen, the form the launcher itself writes in its shortcuts; the `0` is, presumably, the index of the launch option. Assumption U6: the manual test creates a shortcut from Ubisoft Connect and copies its target. If it does not carry `/0`, it is changed to Playnite's form: the template, the assertion of step 4 and its test change together, in the same commit (point 12, B2).

**Ubisoft's `resolveAction`** (`connectors/ubisoft/src/launch.ts`):

1. Action other than `play`: `null`. Null `storeGameId`: `null`.
2. `const m = /^([1-9][0-9]{0,9})$/.exec(storeGameId)`; if not, `action.unsupported` with `connectors.ubisoft.errors.invalidId`.
3. If `ctx.launchersResolved`, Ubisoft Connect is looked for: for each `ubisoft-launcher` location whose path meets the strict rule of point 3, `ctx.fs.exists` of `upc.exe` or `UbisoftConnect.exe` in that folder (assumption U3).
   - One exists: continue.
   - None exists and no check failed: `launch.launcher-missing` with `connectors.ubisoft.errors.launcherMissing` ("Ubisoft Connect not found. Install it from ubisoft.com and try again"). This is analogous to what the user chose for Steam and GOG.
   - Some check gave a read error (unreadable, not absent): continue to the URI. The check only serves to give a better message; the URI is safe anyway.
   - Without `launchersResolved` (non-automatic detection): nothing is checked, like Steam. In practice there are no Ubisoft games in that mode (point 3).
4. `const uri = \`uplay://launch/${m[1]}/0\``, built from the group and **asserted** at the end with `^uplay://launch/[1-9][0-9]{0,9}/0$`; if it does not match (a bug in the connector itself), `internal`.
5. Returns `{ kind: 'uri', uri }`.

- No `ConnectorError` carries paths or titles in `message` or `params`: at most the ID.
- **Core:** no new rules. `checkSpec` already checks the scheme against `uriSchemes` and the platform validates the URI again (decision 72).
- **Invariant 3:** the API receives only IDs; the URI is built with an ID that comes from the name of a registry subkey, validated with a digit pattern before interpolating it.

#### 5. Covers (revised in decision 80)

- ~~**Not included: no cover, with the gradient** (decision 71).~~ (Revised in decision 80: with the account connected, they come from the `thumb_image` of `configurations`, read with a custom parser, and from the launcher's CDN.)
- The only known route without an account is the launcher's CDN (`static3.cdn.ubi.com/orbit/uplay_launcher_3_0/assets/<thumb_image>`, the one Lutris uses; Playnite uses the equivalent at `ubistatic3-a.akamaihd.net`), but the file name (`thumb_image`) is only in `configurations`, discarded in point 3. No public Ubisoft service has been found that gives a cover from the ID without an account; the `ubiservices` APIs ask for application and session identifiers, and using them like that would clash with the official-routes rule (invariant 8).
- They will arrive with the IGDB or RAWG metadata fallback (decisions 6 and 31), as 31 already anticipated for Ubisoft and EA.
- Therefore, `resolveMedia` does not exist and `apiHosts` and `mediaHosts` are empty: **the connector makes no network request.** Neither the CSP nor the privacy guide changes.

#### 6. Ubisoft manifest

```ts
// connectors/ubisoft/src/index.ts (sketch)
export function createUbisoftConnector(): StoreConnector {
  return {
    contractVersion: 1,
    id: "ubisoft",
    nameKey: "connectors.ubisoft.name" as I18nKey,
    access: "local-only",
    capabilities: {
      library: false, scan: true, dlc: "none",
      actions: ["play"], launchKinds: ["uri"], uriSchemes: ["uplay"],
      storePlaytime: false, price: false,
    },
    minSyncIntervalMs: 60_000,          // only scans (ADR 50); no library sync exists
    authHosts: [], apiHosts: [], mediaHosts: [],
    locations: UBISOFT_LOCATIONS,       // ubisoft-installs, ubisoft-launcher (point 3)
    externalTools: [],
    scanInstalled: scanUbisoftInstalled,
    discoverRoots: discoverUbisoftRoots,
    resolveAction: resolveUbisoftAction,
  };
}
```

- `checkConnectorManifest` accepts it as is: `local-only` without `connection`, `play` with `uri` and its scheme.
- **Package `connectors/ubisoft`** (`@ludiary/connector-ubisoft`, `"private": true`), with the shape of `connectors/gog`: `src/` (`manifest.ts`, `paths.ts`, `scan.ts`, `launch.ts`, `index.ts`), `locales/es.json` and `en.json` (`connectors.ubisoft.*`), `fixtures/` and tests with `connector-testkit`.
- **`runtime`:** `createConnectors()` adds `createUbisoftConnector()`. `packages/i18n/src/connectors.ts` adds its line.
- **Web:** the Ubisoft card already exists in the simulator as `not-applicable` and `installed-only` (decision 68); it switches to real data. It adds the `needsAutoDetection` notice when the mode is not `auto-and-manual`. Play uses `game.launching` with `{store}` = Ubisoft.

#### 7. Process and playtime

Outside this slice (slice 2b). For 55, Ubisoft is the hard case: the process that opens the URI is the launcher (`upc.exe`), not the game, and the game may start seconds later. The reasonable approach, as Playnite does, is to watch the processes whose executable is inside `installPath` after the launcher appears. 55 is revalidated with Ubisoft in that slice.

#### 8. Automated tests

**Invented** fixtures: fictitious IDs (`900001`, `900002`…), invented titles and paths under `X:\Ubisoft Games`, never `C:\Users\…`. The fixture check of decision 48 applies the same way. There are no recorded responses: the connector does not use the network. That is why there is no `fixtures/` folder: the registry and folder trees are built in memory inside the tests (noted after the code audit, 23-10-2026). With no Playwright in the repository, the three Playwright cases of this point remain pending together with those of decisions 72 to 78.

- **`connectors/ubisoft`:**
  - Strict path rule (`paths.ts`): table with `/` and trailing slash (accepted after normalizing), UNC, `\\?\`, `\\.\`, relative path, `C:` without slash, drive root, `"` or `|`, `:` after position 1, `CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1`, `LPT9`, component ending in a dot or space, `..`, control characters.
  - `discoverRoots`: two games with a valid `subkey` → two roots with their `tag`; `subkey` missing, `0`, `abc`, with leading zeros, of 11 digits or with spaces → skipped; path that does not meet the rule → skipped and counted, without throwing; drive root → skipped; two IDs with the same folder (with different case) → the lower one is kept; ordered by ID; locations of another declaration ignored; the log contains no path.
  - `scanInstalled` with `memoryFiles`: root with a valid `tag` and existing folder → entry with the folder's title; absent folder → no entry and not unreadable; read error → `unreadableRoots`; `PathEscapesRootsError` → `unreadableRoots`; other error → propagated; user root and root without `tag` or with a `tag` of another form (`game-abc`, `library`) → ignored; repeated ID; title with control characters, only spaces (→ `Ubisoft <id>`), non-ASCII and of more than 200 characters.
  - `resolveAction` with a `ScopedFileReader` double: `play` → exactly `uplay://launch/900001/0`; `install` and other actions → `null`; non-numeric ID, with `/`, `?`, `%`, spaces or of 11 digits → `action.unsupported` without building the URI; Ubisoft Connect folder with `upc.exe` or with `UbisoftConnect.exe` → URI; with neither → `launch.launcher-missing`; `exists` that throws → the URI is returned; launcher path that does not meet the rule → does not count as found; `launchersResolved: false` → URI without checking; no error carries a path.
  - `assertConnectorConformance`.
- **`tray-helper` (Go):** `names` with the same length and order as `values`; a subkey without the value appears in neither list.
- **`platform-windows`:** `parseRegistryResponse` with `names` of a different length, with an empty name or with control characters → failed response; `subkey` only on `registry-subkeys` locations; `not-found` and `unsupported-type` → nothing, without throwing; helper that fails, `access-denied`, `failed` → `resolve` throws; the current Steam and GOG tests keep passing.
- **`core`:** `discover` with a `scan` declaration that throws → the stored roots are not touched and the scan uses the stored ones (games kept); `resolveLauncherLocations` with a declaration that throws → `launchersResolved: false`; a connector double whose roots carry `tag: 'game-<id>'` receives it in `ScanRoot` all the same after storing them.
- **`runtime`:** `createConnectors` registers the three (or four, if Epic is already merged); the `uplay` scheme reaches the platform's scheme list.
- **`i18n`:** parity with `connectors/ubisoft/locales`.
- **Playwright:** `LocationResolver` double that returns a temporary folder with `subkey: '900001'` and a `ProcessLauncher` that records. Cases: the Ubisoft game appears with its folder name and the gradient; Play records `uplay://launch/900001/0`; with "manual folders only", the Ubisoft card shows the notice and the game does not appear.

#### 9. Manual test (prepared by the `tester` in `docs/manual-tests/ubisoft.md`; done by the user)

- **Preparation:** install Ubisoft Connect from ubisoft.com, create or use a free Ubisoft account and install **Trackmania** (free with the "Starter" access, from Ubisoft and with its launcher, so it is the representative case) in a folder with spaces and a non-ASCII character, for example `X:\Juegos Ubisoft ñ`. Smaller alternative if space is short: **Brawlhalla**, free on Ubisoft Connect (about 1 to 2 GB according to low-quality sources; unverified). The size of Trackmania could not be checked.
- **What to check** (copy to the ADR, sanitized, the values that are requested):
  1. `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Ubisoft\Launcher" /s`: the launcher's `InstallDir` and the `Installs\<id>` subkey with `InstallDir` (format: separators and trailing slash). Note the ID (U1, U2, U3).
  2. `upc.exe` and `UbisoftConnect.exe` exist in the Ubisoft Connect folder (U3).
  3. `reg query "HKCR\uplay\shell\open\command"`: the scheme is registered and points to Ubisoft Connect (U4).
  4. Create a desktop shortcut of the game from Ubisoft Connect and copy its target: does it carry `/0`? (U6).
  5. `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Uplay Install <id>" /v DisplayName`: compare with the folder name (U5).
  6. Ludiary with auto-detection: Settings shows the game folder as detected from Ubisoft; the game appears with the folder name and the gradient.
  7. Play with Ubisoft Connect **closed**: the launcher opens and the game starts (it may ask to sign in). Repeat with the launcher **open** (U7).
  8. With "manual folders only": the game disappears and the Ubisoft card shows the notice. Go back to automatic: it appears again.
  9. Uninstall the game from Ubisoft Connect and scan: it disappears, and the `Installs` subkey no longer exists (U8).
  10. The exported log contains neither the game's path, nor its title, nor the launcher's.
  11. Optional: in the game folder, does `uplay_install.state` exist? With `Format-Hex`, is the ID visible in the first bytes? (U9). If the ID clearly appears, manual folders could be admitted in a separate decision.
  12. Optional, at the end: uninstall Ubisoft Connect leaving Ludiary with the game stored and press Play: "Ubisoft Connect not found".

#### 10. Implementation order and parallel work

1. **First** (`developer`, small): `subkey` in `contracts` and the comments; `names` in the Go helper; `parseRegistryResponse` and the resolver (with "absent versus unreadable"); the two core changes; their tests. It touches Steam and GOG: their tests must keep passing.
2. **In parallel:**
   - `connectors`: the complete `connectors/ubisoft` against `connector-testkit` (points 3, 4 and 6, with their tests). It does not depend on step 1 to start: the `testkit` already admits locations with any field.
   - `auditor`: review of this design (the ID in the `tag`, the copied path rule, "absent versus unreadable", the URI) before the code.
3. **Afterwards:** registration in `runtime`, texts (including the detection notice), Playwright and `auditor` review of the code.
4. **At the end:** manual test by the user (point 9), with the assumptions closed in this ADR, and the `docs-writer`:
   - user guide: Ubisoft is detected only with automatic detection; no covers for now; titles taken from the folder; Play opens Ubisoft Connect;
   - troubleshooting: "Ubisoft Connect not found" and "I don't see my Ubisoft games" (automatic detection turned off, more than 64 installed games);
   - privacy: the Ubisoft connector does not connect to the internet; it only reads the registry.

#### 11. What the user decides
