- **UB15 (unverified):** Ubisoft games activated from Steam or Epic appear in `ownedGames` with the `PC` group.

Sources consulted on October 23, 2026: [Playnite, `UplayLibrary.cs`](https://github.com/JosefNemec/PlayniteExtensions/blob/master/source/Libraries/UplayLibrary/UplayLibrary.cs), [`Uplay.cs`](https://github.com/JosefNemec/PlayniteExtensions/blob/master/source/Libraries/UplayLibrary/Uplay.cs) and [`UplayGameController.cs`](https://github.com/JosefNemec/PlayniteExtensions/blob/master/source/Libraries/UplayLibrary/UplayGameController.cs); [Lutris, `services/ubisoft.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/services/ubisoft.py), [`util/ubisoft/client.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/util/ubisoft/client.py), [`util/ubisoft/consts.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/util/ubisoft/consts.py) and [`util/ubisoft/parser.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/util/ubisoft/parser.py); Galaxy integration: [`backend.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/backend.py), [`consts.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/consts.py), [`local_client.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/local_client.py), [`local_file_parser.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/local_file_parser.py) and [`plugin.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/plugin.py); [Steam forum, `cache\ownership` folder](https://steamcommunity.com/app/488790/discussions/0/3182216552778658376).

Sources added for route C, consulted on October 23, 2026: [Lutris, `util/ubisoft/client.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/util/ubisoft/client.py), [`util/ubisoft/consts.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/util/ubisoft/consts.py), [`util/ubisoft/parser.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/util/ubisoft/parser.py) and [`services/ubisoft.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/services/ubisoft.py); Galaxy integration: [`backend.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/backend.py), [`consts.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/consts.py) and [`plugin.py`](https://github.com/FriendsOfGalaxy/galaxy-integration-uplay/blob/master/src/plugin.py); [Playnite, `UplayGameController.cs`](https://github.com/JosefNemec/PlayniteExtensions/blob/master/source/Libraries/UplayLibrary/UplayGameController.cs); [`wailsapp/go-webview2`](https://github.com/wailsapp/go-webview2) (`LICENSE`, `webviewloader`, `pkg/edge/chromium.go`); [`jchv/go-webview2`](https://github.com/jchv/go-webview2); [Microsoft Learn, WebView2 runtime distribution](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/distribution); [Openplanet, Ubisoft account](https://webservices.openplanet.dev/auth/ubi).

**Rationale:** the user wants the games from their Ubisoft account and chose the built-in window. Since Ubisoft has nothing to paste, it is the only route with an account that needs no technical steps and does not have the password typed on a Ludiary screen. It is placed in the Go helper that already exists, with no new binary, with a library without CGO that does not force distributing Microsoft DLLs. The connector only describes the window with a declarative step type; the window, navigation and script belong to the platform and the core, with validation in three layers. Only one credential is stored (`rememberMeTicket`). The API gives the owned games with a `spaceId` that is useless for launching, and `configurations`, already checked on this machine, translates it to the registry ID and gives the covers. Discarded alternatives: A (user's decision, point 17), B (nothing to paste), D (the password in Ludiary), E (does not give ownership), having the connector open the window (30 s and own I/O), capturing `ticket` and `sessionId` too (unnecessary), `jchv/go-webview2` (embedded DLL) and a .NET helper.

**Consequences:**

- Ubisoft becomes `access: 'unofficial-api'` with an account: fourth store with a real wizard, with its fragility icon. The Ubisoft row of the table in 40 and its consequence "stores without an account (Ubisoft and EA)" are revised. EA still has no account.
- 43 is revised for Ubisoft only (point 2); Steam, GOG and Epic do not change.
- The contract gains a step type, an internal input, an OS port (behind its own interface, invariant 1), the `library` purpose, `SyncContext.fs` and `readBytes`. Everything is additive: `contractVersion` stays at 1.
- The Go helper grows with WebView2: more size (measured by the `packager`), one more MIT dependency and the Microsoft runtime as a system requirement. There are still three binaries to sign (45 and 58).
- 79 is revised in its points 1 and 5, in the dropping of `configurations` in point 3 and in `access`. 42 is extended: with "manual folders only" there is no Ubisoft library.
- Fragility: a change in the login page, in the `localStorage` keys, in the API or in the `configurations` format breaks the account. The failure stays on the Ubisoft card (invariant 2), and the scan and Play continue.
- An owned game without a configuration on this machine does not appear until Ubisoft Connect is opened; the guide explains it.
- One new dependency, `yaml`, in `connectors/ubisoft`.
- The `auditor` reviews the design before the code and the code before closing; the `tester` extends `docs/manual-tests/ubisoft.md` (point 14); the `docs-writer`, the guides of point 15.
### 81. EA connector: installed games from `installerdata.xml` and Play with `origin2://` (extends decisions 40, 42 and 72; revises the EA row of the table in 40 and the comment of `ScopedFileReader.readText`; account, covers, Install and `access` revised in decision 82)

**Decision (recommended, October 23, 2026):** the user commissions the EA app connector (formerly Origin) on the `feature/eaconector` branch, which branches off `feature/ubisoftconector`. It is the sibling of 79: EA is `local-only` (decision 40), with no account or API, so the slice is detecting the installed games and playing them. The numbering skips 80 (Ubisoft), which is being written in another working copy.

**Starting point:** the user's PC does not have the EA app (checked on 23-10-2026, read-only: neither `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop` nor its equivalent in `WOW6432Node` exists, nor `Origin`; the `origin`, `origin2`, `link2ea` and `eadm` schemes are not registered; neither `C:\ProgramData\EA Desktop` nor `C:\ProgramData\Origin` exists). Everything about EA comes from public sources (Lutris, the GOG Galaxy integration for the EA app, GameFinder, other open-source managers and forums) and stays an assumption (list at the end) until the manual test in point 9.

#### 1. Scope

- **In:**
  - detection of the installed EA games by reading the `__Installer\installerdata.xml` file in each game's folder, with auto-detection of the default folders **and with manual folders** (decision 42; unlike Ubisoft, the ID is in a file in the game folder);
  - title taken from the file itself;
  - Play with `origin2://game/launch?offerIds=…`, after checking that the EA app is installed;
  - the `connectors/ea` connector registered in `runtime`, with its texts;
  - a small platform change that applies to all stores: `readText` understands UTF-16 with BOM (point 2).
- **Not applicable** (as in 79): Install, account, `connection` and `listLibrary`. `actions: ['play']`.
- **Out:**
  - **covers** (point 5);
  - **DLC:** `dlc: 'none'`. EA DLC are installed inside the base game's folder and have no `__Installer` of their own (assumption EAD10);
  - **cross-store matching:** an EA game bought on Steam or Epic may appear twice if the user adds that folder to EA (assumption EAD12);
  - **playtime** (slice 2b, point 7);
  - **EA account** (non-installed games, covers from the EA API): left for a later decision, as in Ubisoft. The known routes (the EA GraphQL that Lutris uses, entitlements that the Galaxy integration uses) require a session and are not official.

#### 2. Contract (extends decisions 40 and 72; `contractVersion` stays at 1)

- **Nothing new in the types.** There is no need for `subkey` or a `tag` with an ID (the ID comes from the file) or for `discoverRoots`: without it, the core already uses the resolved `scan` locations as roots (`sync.ts`, `discover`).
- **`ScopedFileReader.readText` decodes UTF-16 with BOM.** Third-party sources that read `installerdata.xml` warn that it appears in both UTF-8 and UTF-16 (assumption EAD3). Today `readText` decodes everything as UTF-8 and strips a UTF-8 BOM: a UTF-16 file would arrive as garbage text and the game would not appear. It is decided in the platform, not in the connector:
  - `packages/platform-node/src/local-files.ts`: if the first bytes are `FF FE`, the following ones are decoded as UTF-16 LE; if they are `FE FF`, as UTF-16 BE (`swap16` on a copy; with odd length, the last byte is dropped). Otherwise, as today (UTF-8, stripping the BOM). Same 1 MiB cap in bytes.
  - Comment of `ScopedFileReader` in `contracts`: "UTF-8 (a leading BOM is removed) or UTF-16 LE/BE with BOM (ADR 81)".
  - UTF-16 without BOM is not detected: it arrives with NUL characters and the connector's parser rejects it (point 3).
  - `memoryFiles` of the `testkit` does not change (it stores text, not bytes).
  - For Steam, GOG and Epic it only changes for the better: a UTF-16 file that used to fail to parse is now read correctly.
- `contractVersion` stays at 1: it is a more permissive behavior of an OS port, with no new fields.

#### 3. Scan

- **Single source: `<game folder>\__Installer\installerdata.xml`.** It is the EA installer's manifest. In the current format (root `DiPManifest`) it carries `contentIDs/contentID` (the game's offer IDs, several if there are editions) and `gameTitles/gameTitle` with a `locale` attribute; also `runtime/launcher/filePath` (assumptions EAD1 and EAD2). It is used by Lutris, the Galaxy integration's manager, EverythingBox (September 2026), Mira, nicedeck and the list of a manifest project that takes "the first `contentID`".
- **Discarded as a source:**
  - `C:\ProgramData\EA Desktop\530c1147…\IS` (the "IS.json"): encrypted with AES-256-CBC and a key derived from the machine's hardware (motherboard, BIOS, CPU, serial number of `C:`), according to GameFinder. Decrypting it would require reading hardware data and reimplementing an undocumented encryption that changes with any component: it is discarded.
  - `C:\ProgramData\EA Desktop\InstallData\…`: no public format is recorded; the Galaxy integration defines the path but does not use it.
  - `C:\ProgramData\Origin\LocalContent\*.mfst` (Origin): Origin closed on 17-04-2025; moreover, the `.mfst` files only give the ID and Playnite asked a public Origin API, no longer recorded, for the rest (path, executable).
  - Registry `HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Origin Games\<contentId>`: according to the Lutris thread of December 2023, the subkeys are not deleted on uninstall and also list DLC; it is useless for knowing what is installed. If the manual test shows that it carries the folder, it may serve to **find** non-standard folders (like the registry in GOG), in a separate decision (assumption EAD6).
  - Per-game registry `HKLM\SOFTWARE\[WOW6432Node\]<Publisher>\<Game>\Install Dir`: the key changes with each game (`Respawn\Apex`, `Maxis\The Sims 4`…) and is only known by reading `installerdata.xml`; it is not a fixed declaration.
  - EA installer's `Uninstall` entries: they force walking all of `Uninstall` (clashes with the cap of 256 subkeys, as 79 saw).
- **Manifest, `locations`:**
  - `ea-libraries` (`scan`): `{ kind: 'known-folder', folder: 'ProgramFiles', relative: 'EA Games' }`, the EA app's default folder (Lutris, EverythingBox; assumption EAD5), and `{ kind: 'known-folder', folder: 'ProgramFilesX86', relative: 'Origin Games' }`, Origin's, where the games installed before the migration remain (assumption EAD5). Only those that exist come out.
  - `ea-desktop` (`launcher`): `{ kind: 'known-folder', folder: 'ProgramFiles', relative: 'Electronic Arts\\EA Desktop\\EA Desktop' }`. The EA app installer does not let you choose a folder (EA forum) and `EADesktop.exe` and `EALauncher.exe` are there (assumption EAD7).
  - `ea-settings` (`scan`, added in point 13): EA app settings folders, read by `discoverRoots` and never scanned.
  - There are no registry sources, so `LocationsUnreadableError` does not appear for EA. The rules of 79 ("absent versus unreadable" per declaration, roots not stolen between stores, caps that do not delete) apply unchanged because they live in the core and the platform.
- **Manual folders and "manual folders only":** they work, because the scan does not depend on the registry. A user who installs in `X:\EA Games` adds that folder in Settings; the guide explains it. The Ubisoft `needsAutoDetection` notice is **not** needed. With "configure it later" there are no folders and nothing appears, as the first-run wizard already says (decision 69).
- **`scanInstalled`** (`connectors/ea/src/scan.ts`), for each root (discovered or the user's), with depth 1 like GOG:
  1. Candidates: the root itself and its direct subfolders (`readDir`), at most 2,000 per root.
  2. In each candidate, `ctx.fs.exists(join(candidate, '__Installer', 'installerdata.xml'))`. If it does not exist, it is not an EA game and the next one is processed without reading anything else.
  3. `readText` and `parseInstallerData` (below). If it is not valid: `store.unexpected-response`, that file is skipped and counted.
  4. Entry: `storeGameId` = the **first** valid ID, `kind: 'game'`, `title` from the file, `installPath` = the candidate. No `media`, `launchData` or `executables`: the rest of the IDs are read at launch (point 4), as GOG does with its `.info`, so that a game update takes effect immediately.
  5. A `storeGameId` already seen is skipped and the ID is logged (the core does it too).
  - **Errors**, with GOG's `isHandled` classification, copied: `readDir` of the root with an error, or an `exists`/`readText` with a read error → the root goes to `unreadableRoots` and keeps its installations; `PathEscapesRootsError` in a subfolder → that candidate is skipped; ~~on the root itself → unreadable root; a file of more than 1 MiB → `scan.root-unreadable` (given by `readText`), the root keeps its games~~ (revised by the auditor, point 12, M3: `PathEscapesRootsError` only makes the root unreadable if `readDir` of the root fails; a file of more than 1 MiB or that is not a regular file is `store.unexpected-response` and counts as an invalid file); any other `internal` is propagated.
  - (Revised in point 13: the roots from `downloadinplacedir` come from a file and go through `isStrictLocalPath`.) **No path comes from a file or the registry** (the roots are known folders or the user's, and `installPath` is a folder that Ludiary has walked), so the strict path rule of 79 is **not needed** here. `runtime/launcher/filePath` is not read.
  - In the log, only counters (`invalidFiles`, `invalidIds`, `duplicates`), codes and EA IDs; never paths or titles.
- **`parseInstallerData(text)`** (`connectors/ea/src/installerdata.ts`, pure, no dependencies; there is no XML library in the repository and none is added to read two lists). **Revised by the auditor (point 12, A1 and B1 to B3):** the expressions in this list say what is extracted; how it is extracted (without expressions of unbounded cost), the decoding and the handling of IDs are those of point 12, which prevails.
  1. If the text contains a NUL character (UTF-16 without BOM) or `<!DOCTYPE` or `<!ENTITY`: invalid. No declared entity is expanded.
  2. Comments `<!-- … -->` are removed.
  3. Format: `<DiPManifest\b` → current; otherwise, `<game\b` → old Origin (assumption EAD4); otherwise, invalid.
  4. **IDs:** first block `<contentIDs\b[^>]*>…</contentIDs>`; inside, each `<contentID\b[^>]*>([^<]*)</contentID>`. `\b` prevents `<contentIDs>` from counting as `<contentID>` (a real bug that Mira fixed in its reader). Each value is decoded (below), trimmed and must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$` (EverythingBox's rule: odd IDs are rejected, never cleaned). No duplicates, in order, at most 16 (the rest are ignored and counted). None valid: invalid.
  5. **Title:** in the current format, each `<gameTitle\b[^>]*\blocale="([^"]*)"[^>]*>([^<]*)</gameTitle>` inside `<gameTitles>`; in the old one, `<localeInfo\b[^>]*\blocale="([^"]*)"[^>]*>` followed by its `<title>([^<]*)</title>`. `en_US` is chosen, otherwise the first `en_*`, otherwise the first one. The interface language is not used: the title stays stable when the language changes and looks more like that of the other stores for future matching (decision 51).
  6. **Decoding:** `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&amp;`, `&quot;`, `&apos;` and numeric references `&#…;`/`&#x…;` to valid non-control code points; any other entity is left as is. A `CDATA` does not match `[^<]*` and leaves the title without a value (falls back).
  7. Title cleanup: no control characters, trimmed, at most 300. If it ends up empty, the last component of the folder (rule of 79) and, if that is also empty, `EA <id>` (a piece of data, not an interface text).
  8. Returns `{ ids, title }` or `null`.

#### 4. Launch

**Options:**

- **A. URI `origin2://game/launch?offerIds=<id>[,<id>…]`** (recommended). The EA app opens (asking to sign in if needed) and starts the game.
  - Advantages: it is the route of Lutris, of the Galaxy integration for the EA app (maintained after Origin's closure) and of EverythingBox (September 2026); it does not need to know the executable; it respects what EA games require, which almost always need the app open (their DRM reopens it even if the `.exe` is launched, according to the Lutris thread).
  - Costs: it depends on the EA app being installed and registering `origin2`; Ludiary does not know whether the game started; decision 22 records failures of EA URIs in some games.
- **B. `exec` of the executable in `runtime/launcher/filePath`.** Discarded in this slice: it is often not a path but a registry reference, such as `[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Respawn\Apex\Install Dir]EasyAntiCheat_launcher.exe` (GameFinder). Resolving it requires reading a registry key that names a file, not a fixed declaration (clashes with rule 8 of 40); keeping the tail relative to `installPath` assumes that `Install Dir` is the game folder; and even so the game reopens the EA app. It remains as plan B, with its own decision, if the manual test shows the URI fails.
- **C. `link2ea://launchgame/<id>?platform=…&theme=…`.** Discarded: it is the bridge that Steam and Epic use for EA games bought on those stores (all the examples found carry `platform=steam` and a `theme` with the game's short name, which `installerdata.xml` does not give). It does not apply to what was bought in the EA app.
- **D. `origin://launchgame/<id>`** (old Origin form): discarded. It is the one that, according to the EA forum thread, gave an access error; the one that worked was `origin2` with the numeric `contentID`. The failures in decision 22 most likely come from there and from using `Origin.SFT.…` IDs (assumption EAD9).

**Which IDs are passed.** `offerIds` is plural: Lutris passes all the `contentID`s separated by commas, and the Galaxy integration and EverythingBox just one. **All** are chosen, with the stored one first: if the file lists several editions and the user owns only one, the EA app finds theirs (assumption EAD8). The manual test compares the two forms; if it fails with several, it switches to a single one by changing the construction, the assertion and its test in the same commit. No `&autoDownload=1`: Lutris adds it when playing too, but the Galaxy integration only when installing, and here the game is already installed.

**EA's `resolveAction`** (`connectors/ea/src/launch.ts`):

1. Action other than `play`: `null`. Null `storeGameId`: `null`.
2. `storeGameId` must match the pattern of point 3; otherwise, `action.unsupported` with `connectors.ea.errors.invalidId`. Null `installPath`: `launch.not-installed`.
3. If `ctx.launchersResolved`, the EA app is looked for as in 79: for each `ea-desktop` location, `ctx.fs.exists` of `EADesktop.exe` or `EALauncher.exe`.
   - One exists: continue.
   - None exists and no check failed: `launch.launcher-missing` with `connectors.ea.errors.launcherMissing` ("EA app not found. Install it from ea.com and try again").
   - Some check gave a read error: continue to the URI (the check only improves the message).
   - Without `launchersResolved`: nothing is checked.
4. It reads `<installPath>\__Installer\installerdata.xml` with `ctx.fs` (confined to `installPath`) and `parseInstallerData`. First `exists` and then `readText` (revised by the auditor, point 12, M1):
   - the file does not exist: `launch.not-installed` with `connectors.ea.errors.installerDataMissing` (the game was uninstalled or moved; the next scan fixes it);
   - valid and contains the stored ID: `ids` = the stored one and then the others from the file, in their order, 16 at most;
   - valid but without the stored ID: `launch.not-installed` with the same key (that folder now holds another game);
   - unreadable, `PathEscapesRootsError` or invalid: `ids` = only the stored one (the URI is safe anyway); the code is logged, not the path.
5. `const uri = \`origin2://game/launch?offerIds=${ids.join(",")}\``, **asserted** at the end with `^origin2://game/launch\?offerIds=I(,I){0,15}$`, where `I` is the pattern of point 3; if it does not match (a connector bug), `internal`. The pattern's characters (`A-Za-z0-9._:-`) and the comma need no encoding in the query and `validateLaunchUri` accepts them.
6. Returns `{ kind: 'uri', uri }`.

- No `ConnectorError` carries paths or titles in `message` or `params`; at most the ID.
- **Core and platform:** no new rules. `checkSpec` checks the scheme against `uriSchemes` and the platform validates the URI again (decision 72).
- **Invariant 3:** the API receives only IDs. The URI is built with IDs that come from a local file in the game folder, each validated with a closed pattern before interpolating it, and with the one stored in the database always present.

#### 5. Covers (revised in decision 82: with the EA account, from `packArt`)

- **Not included: no cover, with the gradient** (decision 71). `resolveMedia` does not exist and `apiHosts` and `mediaHosts` are empty: **the connector makes no network request.** Neither the CSP nor the privacy guide changes.
- No public route without an account has been found: Lutris gets `packArt` and `keyArt` from the EA GraphQL with the user's session; the Galaxy integration, from the offers with a token; the public Origin API (`api1.origin.com/ecommerce2/public/supercat/…`) that Playnite used returned 404 in the test of 23-10-2026 and Origin no longer exists.
- **Hook for a common provider:** if decision 80 (Ubisoft) or a later one creates an external cover provider for stores without them (IGDB or RAWG, decisions 6 and 31), EA joins without touching the connector: its entries already carry a clean title and a stable `storeGameId`. It is not designed here.

#### 6. EA manifest

```ts
// connectors/ea/src/index.ts (sketch)
export function createEaConnector(): StoreConnector {
  return {
    contractVersion: 1,
    id: "ea",
    nameKey: "connectors.ea.name" as I18nKey,
    access: "local-only",
    capabilities: {
      library: false, scan: true, dlc: "none",
      actions: ["play"], launchKinds: ["uri"], uriSchemes: ["origin2"],
      storePlaytime: false, price: false,
    },
    minSyncIntervalMs: 60_000,          // only scans (ADR 50)
    authHosts: [], apiHosts: [], mediaHosts: [],
    locations: EA_LOCATIONS,            // ea-libraries, ea-desktop (point 3)
    externalTools: [],
    scanInstalled: scanEaInstalled,     // no discoverRoots: resolved locations are the roots
    resolveAction: resolveEaAction,
  };
}
```

- `checkConnectorManifest` accepts it as is (`local-only` without `connection`; `play` with `uri` and its scheme).
- **Package `connectors/ea`** (`@ludiary/connector-ea`, `"private": true`), with the shape of `connectors/ubisoft`: `src/` (`manifest.ts`, `installerdata.ts`, `scan.ts`, `launch.ts`, `index.ts`), `locales/es.json` and `en.json` (`connectors.ea.*`: `name`, `errors.invalidId`, `errors.launcherMissing`, `errors.installerDataMissing`) and tests with `connector-testkit`. No `paths.ts` (point 3).
- **`runtime`:** `createConnectors()` adds `createEaConnector()`. `packages/i18n/src/connectors.ts` adds its line.
- **Web:** the EA card already exists in the simulator as `not-applicable` and `installed-only`, with `C:\Program Files\EA Games` as the detected folder (decision 68); it switches to real data. Play uses `game.launching` with `{store}` = EA.

#### 7. Process and playtime

Outside this slice (slice 2b). Same case as Ubisoft for 55: the process that opens the URI is the EA app, not the game. The processes whose executable is inside `installPath` will be watched. 55 is revalidated with EA in that slice.

#### 8. Automated tests

**Invented** fixtures: fictitious IDs (`9000001`, `9000002`, `OFB-TEST:900001`), invented titles and paths under `X:\EA Games` or `C:\Program Files\EA Games`, never `C:\Users\…`. The test `installerdata.xml` files are written by hand (current and old format), not copied from a real game. No recorded responses (there is no network). The fixture check of decision 48 applies the same way.

- **`connectors/ea`:**
  - `parseInstallerData`: current format with one ID and with several; `<contentIDs>` and `<gameTitles>` do not count as stand-alone elements; ID with surrounding spaces (trimmed), empty, starting with `.`, with `/`, `?`, `&`, `%`, `,`, an inner space or of 65 characters → rejected without cleaning; duplicates; more than 16; no valid ID → `null`; preference `en_US`, other `en_*`, first; entities (`&amp;`, `&#8482;`, `&#x2122;`, an unknown one that stays as is, a numeric control one that is not decoded); comment with a `<contentID>` inside (ignored); `<!DOCTYPE>` or `<!ENTITY>` → `null`; NUL character → `null`; old `<game>` format with `localeInfo`/`title`; unknown root → `null`; title empty, only spaces, with control characters or of more than 300.
  - `scanInstalled` with `memoryFiles`: root with two games in subfolders; the root itself as a game folder; subfolder without `__Installer` (no reads); invalid file → skipped and counted; unreadable `readDir` of the root → `unreadableRoots`; unreadable `readText` → `unreadableRoots`; `PathEscapesRootsError` in a subfolder → skipped, on the root → unreadable; other error → propagated; same ID in two folders → one entry; user root the same as the discovered one; fallback title with the folder name; the log contains no paths or titles.
  - `resolveAction` with a `ScopedFileReader` double: `play` → exactly `origin2://game/launch?offerIds=9000001,9000002`, with the stored one first even if it is second in the file; `install` and others → `null`; invalid stored ID → `action.unsupported` without building the URI; null `installPath` → `launch.not-installed`; file absent or without the stored ID → `launch.not-installed`; unreadable, escaping or invalid file → URI with only the stored one; `EADesktop.exe` or `EALauncher.exe` present → URI; neither → `launch.launcher-missing`; `exists` that throws → URI; `launchersResolved: false` → URI without checking; no error carries a path.
  - `assertConnectorConformance`.
- **`platform-node`:** `readText` with UTF-8 BOM (stripped), UTF-16 LE with BOM, UTF-16 BE with BOM (with a non-ASCII character, for example `ñ` and `™`), UTF-16 of odd length, and without BOM (UTF-8, as today); the 1 MiB cap remains in bytes.
- **`runtime`:** `createConnectors` registers EA; the `origin2` scheme reaches the platform's scheme list.
- **`i18n`:** parity with `connectors/ea/locales`.
- **Playwright** (pending together with those of decisions 72 to 79): temporary folder with an invented EA game as a discovered root and a `ProcessLauncher` that records. Cases: the game appears with the file's title and the gradient; Play records the expected URI; with "manual folders only" and the folder added by hand, the game still appears.

#### 9. Manual test (prepared by the tester in `docs/manual-tests/ea.md`; done by the user)

- **Preparation:** install the EA app from ea.com, create or use a free EA account and install **The Sims 4** (the base game has been free since October 2022, is from EA and requires its app, so it is the representative case) in the default folder. Its size could not be checked and it is large. Smaller alternative: an old game the user already has in their EA account (for example, from Origin's "On the House" gifts), which would also test the old file format.
- **What to check** (copy to the ADR, sanitized, the values that are requested; no usernames or account IDs):
  1. `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop"` and the same in `WOW6432Node`: names of the values (in case a registry source is needed for the app) and whether the folder is `C:\Program Files\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop\EA Desktop` with `EADesktop.exe` and `EALauncher.exe` (EAD7).
  2. `reg query "HKCR\origin2\shell\open\command"` and `HKCR\link2ea`: which schemes the app registers and what they point to (EAD9).
  3. In the game folder, `__Installer\installerdata.xml`: `Format-Hex -Count 4` (encoding, EAD3), root tag, how many `contentID` and of what form, what `locale` the `gameTitle` have and what `runtime/launcher/filePath` says (EAD1, EAD2, EAD4).
  4. `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Origin Games" /s`: does the game's subkey exist and does it carry the folder in some value? (EAD6).
  5. Do `C:\ProgramData\EA Desktop\machine.ini` (or `.inf`) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop\user_*.ini` exist, and do they have `downloadinplacedir`? Only the key name and the form of the path (EAD6).
  6. Ludiary with auto-detection: Settings shows `C:\Program Files\EA Games` as detected from EA; the game appears with its title and the gradient.
  7. Play with the EA app **closed** and **open**: the app opens and the game starts (EAD8, EAD11). If it fails, try with Win+R `origin2://game/launch?offerIds=<first ID>` and note which one works. If the game has several `contentID`, check that the URI with commas reaches the EA app whole through `rundll32` (point 12, NV1): the EA app's log or the result must match those of the same URI typed in Win+R.
  7b. ID stability (point 12, M2): note the list of `contentIDs` before and after the EA app updates the game. If the first one changes, option (b) of M2 applies.
  8. Create a shortcut of the game from the EA app (if it allows) and copy its target.
  9. "Manual folders only": the game disappears; add `C:\Program Files\EA Games` by hand: it appears again.
  10. Uninstall the game from the EA app and scan: it disappears. Does the `__Installer` folder remain? (EAD13).
  11. The exported log contains neither the game's path, nor its title, nor the EA app's.
  12. Optional, at the end: uninstall the EA app leaving the game stored in Ludiary and press Play: "EA app not found".

#### 10. Implementation order and parallel work

1. **In parallel:**
   - `developer` (small): UTF-16 in `readText`, the `contracts` comment and its tests.
   - `connectors`: the complete `connectors/ea` against `connector-testkit` (points 3, 4 and 6). It does not depend on the previous step: `memoryFiles` already returns text.
   - `auditor`: review of this design (XML parser without a library, ID in the URI, reading at launch, UTF-16) before the code.
2. **Afterwards:** registration in `runtime`, texts, Playwright and `auditor` review of the code.
3. **At the end:** manual test by the user (point 9), with the assumptions closed in this ADR, and the `docs-writer`:
   - user guide: EA is detected in `C:\Program Files\EA Games` and in the folders the user adds; no covers for now; Play opens the EA app;
   - troubleshooting: "EA app not found" and "I don't see my EA games" (installed in another folder: add it in Settings);
   - privacy: the EA connector does not connect to the internet; it only reads each game's folder.

#### 11. What the user decides

**Applied by default (23-10-2026), unless the user says otherwise:** 11.1 (a).

1. **Play without the EA app installed:** (a) message "EA app not found" (recommended, the same as in Steam, GOG and Ubisoft); (b) try the URI anyway and let Windows show its dialog.
2. **Game for the manual test:** (a) The Sims 4 (recommended: free, from EA and with its app); (b) a small game they already have in their EA account, if disk space matters.
3. **What comes next:** (a) merge Ubisoft (79 and 80) and EA and do their manual tests (recommended: with EA all five stores detect installed games and every open branch complicates the merge); (b) slice 2b (playtime), to close 55; (c) cross-store matching; (d) a cover provider for Ubisoft and EA.

#### 12. Auditor review of the design (October 23, 2026)

No critical findings. What follows takes precedence over points 2, 3 and 4 where they differ. The code is written by the `connectors` agent (and the `developer` does the platform change of M3).

- **A1 (high). Parser without expressions of unbounded cost.** Measured by the auditor: 44,000 characters of repeated `<gameTitle locale="x" ` take 52 s with the expression of point 3, and repeated `<contentIDs>`, 5 s with 480 KB. The server is single-threaded: a file like that freezes it entirely. It is decided:
  - comments (`<!--` … `-->`), `CDATA` and the `<contentIDs>` … `</contentIDs>` block (and `<gameTitles>`) are located with `indexOf`, never with an expression that walks the text with `[\s\S]*?`;
  - tags are recognized with bounded quantifiers (for example, attributes of at most 512 characters, `[^<>]{0,512}`), and an element's value with `[^<]{0,1024}`;
  - the `locale` attribute is read separately, on the already isolated tag text, with `\blocale="([^"<>]{1,32})"`;
  - the end of a tag name is checked with `(?=[\s/>])` instead of `\b` (`<contentID` followed by `s` does not match, nor does `<contentID-x`);
  - `<!DOCTYPE` and `<!ENTITY` are searched case-insensitively;
  - performance test: each of the auditor's hostile inputs (and one of 1 MiB of open tags never closed) is parsed in **under 200 ms**.
- **M1 (medium). At launch, `exists` before `readText`.** `exists` false → `launch.not-installed` with `installerDataMissing`; `exists` or `readText` with a read error (or `PathEscapesRootsError`) → URI with only the stored ID. This way a deleted folder is not confused with an unreadable file.
- **M2 (medium). ID stability.** **(a)** is decided: accept EAD2 (the first `contentID` is stable) and check it in the manual test (point 9, step 7b, before and after an update). **(b)**, if it fails: that the core keeps the `storeGameId` of an ownership whose `installPath` does not change, in its own decision.
- **M3 (medium). Permanent problems of a file are not an unreadable root.**
  - `PathEscapesRootsError` only makes the root unreadable if `readDir` of the root itself fails; on a candidate or its file, the candidate is skipped.
  - **Platform change, for all stores:** `readText` of a file of more than 1 MiB or that is not a regular file throws `store.unexpected-response` instead of `scan.root-unreadable`. It is permanent: marking the root as unreadable would keep forever games that may no longer be there. The connectors count it as an invalid file and continue (in Steam, GOG and Epic that is already what they do with `store.unexpected-response`). The `ScopedFileReader` comment in `contracts` says so. `contractVersion` stays at 1. The `platform-node` and `testkit` tests (`memoryFiles`, which must imitate it) change with it.
- **B1 (low). CDATA:** a title in `CDATA` is taken as is, without decoding entities, locating it with `indexOf` (`<![CDATA[` … `]]>`); an unclosed `CDATA` invalidates the title (falls back).
- **B2 (low). Raw ID.** The `contentID`s are **not** decoded: any `&` in the value invalidates it (the pattern no longer admits it). Only spaces are trimmed.
- **B3 (low). Title entities** in a single pass (no double decoding: `&amp;lt;` gives `&lt;`), excluding numeric references to surrogates (`0xD800`–`0xDFFF`), greater than `0x10FFFF` and control ones. After decoding UTF-16 in the platform, `toWellFormed()` replaces lone surrogates.
- **B4 (low). A single pattern.** `ID_BODY = "[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}"` shared for validating and for the final URI assertion. "The others" are those in the file **different from the stored one**. The stored one is looked for in the full list **before** cutting it to 16 (if it is the 20th, it is launched with it first and 15 more).
- **B5 (low).** Candidate subfolders are walked sorted by name (case-insensitive) so that the ID that wins among duplicates is stable.
- **NV1 (unverified).** That the commas of the URI reach the EA app intact through `rundll32` (`openUri`). It moves to the manual test (point 9, step 7). If they are lost, it is launched with only the stored ID.
- **Tests added by the review:** the performance ones of A1; `<contentID-x>` and `<CONTENTIDS>`; lowercase `<!doctype>`; `exists` false versus unreadable `readText` at launch; file of more than 1 MiB and folder with the file's name → invalid file, readable root; `PathEscapesRootsError` on the root's file → skipped, readable root; ID with `&amp;` → rejected; `&amp;lt;` → `&lt;`; `&#xD800;` and `&#x110000;` not decoded; UTF-16 with a lone surrogate; title in `CDATA`; stored one in position 20; candidate order.

#### 13. EAD6 closed: folders of the EA app from its settings (October 23, 2026)

Takes precedence over points 3 and 11 and over EAD6 where they differ.

- **Checked on the user's machine** (read-only, without copying names): `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop\user_<number>.ini` carries `user.downloadinplacedir=X:\` and `C:\ProgramData\EA Desktop\machine.ini` carries `machine.downloadinplacedir=C:\Program Files\EA Games\`. The real game `X:\My Game\__Installer\installerdata.xml` is a UTF-8 `DiPManifest` with a single `contentID` (confirms EAD1; EAD3 in part: UTF-8 yes, UTF-16 not seen).
- **Implemented in the connector:**
  - new location `ea-settings` (purpose `scan`): `LocalAppData\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop` and `ProgramData\EA Desktop`;
  - `discoverRoots` reads `machine.ini` and `user_<n>.ini` in them (16 files at most, 64 KiB each), looks for the key with `indexOf` per line, without expressions of unbounded cost, and adds the value as an `ea-libraries` root (no duplicates);
  - the value is validated with `isStrictLocalPath` (strict rule of 79); a drive root (`X:\`) is valid as a library;
  - the settings folders are **never** a root: they are only read;
  - the `user_<n>.ini` name carries the account ID: it **never** goes to the log, only counters (`files`, `unreadable`, `invalidPaths`).
- **Revises from point 3** "No path comes from a file or the registry": now a root comes from a file of the EA app, and that is why it goes through `isStrictLocalPath`. The `Origin Games` registry key remains discarded.

#### EA assumptions (verify in the manual test; those marked "unverified" have no source other than the one indicated)

- **EAD1:** each game installed by the EA app has `__Installer\installerdata.xml` in its folder, with root `DiPManifest`, `contentIDs/contentID` and `gameTitles/gameTitle locale="…"`. Sources: Lutris (`ea_app.py`), nicedeck, EverythingBox (PR 479), Mira (PR 62), GameFinder (wiki), EA forum.
- **EAD2:** the **first** `contentID` is stable and is the one that identifies the game (used by Lutris to match with the account and by the 626-game-manifest project, which requires it explicitly; numeric examples of 8 digits).
- **EAD3 (unverified on a machine):** the file may be in UTF-8 or in UTF-16 with BOM (EverythingBox says it reads both).
- **EAD4 (unverified):** old Origin games use a `<game>` root with `metadata/localeInfo/title` (EverythingBox) and also `contentIDs/contentID`.
- **EAD5:** the EA app's default folder is `C:\Program Files\EA Games` (Lutris inside Wine, EverythingBox) and Origin's was `C:\Program Files (x86)\Origin Games` (unverified).
- **EAD6 (closed on 23-10-2026, point 13: `downloadinplacedir` of `machine.ini` and `user_<n>.ini` gives the folder; original text follows):** there is no unencrypted source that gives the folder of installed games outside the default folder. Candidates for a separate decision: `Origin Games\<contentId>` in the registry (not deleted on uninstall, according to Lutris), `machine.inf`/`machine.ini` with `machine.downloadinplacedir` (EA forum) and `user_<n>.ini` with `user.downloadinplacedir` (Lutris thread).
- **EAD7:** the EA app is always installed in `C:\Program Files\Electronic Arts\EA Desktop\EA Desktop`, with no folder choice, with `EADesktop.exe` and `EALauncher.exe` (EA forum, Lutris installer). Otherwise the message of 11.1 would appear by mistake with the app installed: a registry source would be added (step 1 of the test).
- **EAD8 (unverified):** `origin2://game/launch?offerIds=<id1>,<id2>` starts the game of the ID the user owns. Lutris uses the list; the Galaxy integration and EverythingBox, a single ID.
- **EAD9:** the EA app registers `origin2` (the Galaxy integration checks that handler before launching). The failures in decision 22 correspond to `origin://` and to `Origin.SFT.…` IDs (a single EA forum thread, unverified).
- **EAD10 (unverified):** DLC have no `__Installer` of their own outside the base game's folder.
- **EAD11 (unverified):** the URI works with the app closed and open.
- **EAD12 (unverified):** an EA game bought on Steam or Epic also carries `__Installer\installerdata.xml`; it would only appear under EA if the user adds that folder, and then Play through `origin2` might not work (the purchase is on another store).
- **EAD13 (unverified):** uninstalling from the EA app deletes the game folder, including `__Installer`. If it remains, the game would keep appearing: it would be decided to require something more (for example, the executable from `filePath`).
- **EAD14:** without an account there is no public route for covers (point 5).

Sources consulted on October 23, 2026: [Lutris, `services/ea_app.py`](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/blob/master/lutris/services/ea_app.py); [Lutris, issue 5160](https://github.com/lutris/lutris/issues/5160); [GameFinder, EA Desktop wiki](https://github.com/erri120/GameFinder/wiki/EA-Desktop) and [`EADesktopHandler.cs`](https://github.com/erri120/GameFinder/blob/master/src/GameFinder.StoreHandlers.EADesktop/EADesktopHandler.cs); GOG Galaxy integration for the EA app: [`plugin.py`](https://github.com/BellezaEmporium/galaxy-integration-ead/blob/galaxy-2.1/src/plugin.py) and [`lgames_manifests.py`](https://github.com/BellezaEmporium/galaxy-integration-ead/blob/galaxy-2.1/src/lgames_manifests.py); [Playnite (old copy), `OriginLibrary.cs`](https://github.com/ofear/playnite/blob/master/source/Plugins/OriginLibrary/OriginLibrary.cs); [EverythingBox, PR 479](https://github.com/cubman3134/EverythingBox/pull/479); [Mira, PR 62](https://github.com/Mira-Launcher/Mira/pull/62); [nicedeck, `launcher` package](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/mateussouzaweb/nicedeck/src/platforms/launcher); [626-game-manifest, PR 25](https://github.com/estevanhernandez-stack-ed/626-game-manifest/pull/25); [EA forum, launching a game by command](https://forums.ea.com/discussions/ea-play-general-discussion-en/launch-ea-game-using-command/7575680) (only the search engine excerpt; the page returned 403); [EA forum, app installation folder](https://forums.ea.com/discussions/ea-app-feedback-en/ea-desktop-client-custom-installation-folder/7480080/replies/7480081); [EA forum, `machine.inf`](https://forums.ea.com/discussions/ea-app-technical-issues-fr/changer-le-r%c3%a9pertoire-dinstallation-sur-ea-desktop-impossible/7519697); [Steam forums on `link2ea`](https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/5330625727564017662/); [heise, Origin closure](https://heise.de/-10248905).

**Rationale:** it is the smallest slice that puts EA in the library and makes it playable, **with no network, no secrets, no migration and no new types**. `installerdata.xml` is the only unencrypted source that gives both the ID and the title, and since it is in the game folder, EA also works with manual folders (better than Ubisoft). The `origin2` URI leaves to the EA app what its games require of it anyway and is the route of all current tools. Reading the file at launch avoids `launchData` and holds after an update. Discarded alternatives: decrypting `IS` (key tied to the hardware); the `Origin Games` registry key (not cleaned on uninstall); `exec` (registry references and the game reopens the app); `link2ea` (for purchases on Steam or Epic); an XML library to read two lists.

**Consequences:**

- Fourth store in the library and second `local-only`. It adds no hosts, CSP or privacy changes.
- The EA row of the table in decision 40 changes from "`uri` or `exec`, to be validated with real games" to "`uri` (`origin2://game/launch?offerIds=…`), decided in 81; assumptions EAD8 and EAD9".
- `ScopedFileReader.readText` accepts UTF-16 with BOM in all stores and, after the auditor's review (point 12, M3), gives `store.unexpected-response` for a file of more than 1 MiB or that is not a regular file.
- Known limit (revised in point 13): the games in the default folder, in Origin's and in the EA app's download folder (`downloadinplacedir`) are detected automatically. Those installed in another folder (for example, an earlier folder the user changed afterwards) only appear if the user adds it.
- The `auditor` reviews before closing: the XML parser (entities, DTD, comments, `\b`), the IDs in the URI and the assertion, the reading at launch confined to `installPath`, UTF-16 in `readText`, and that neither the log nor the errors carry paths or titles.
- The `developer` and `connectors` agents have their specification here; the `tester` writes `docs/manual-tests/ea.md` (point 9); the `docs-writer` updates the guides of point 10.
### 82. EA account with the embedded login window (extends decisions 40, 74, 80 and 81; revises decision 43 for EA by user choice; revises from 81 the account, the covers, Install and `access: 'local-only'`; extends the helper of 80 with capturing the JSON text of the page and reaching `doneUrl` by navigation; connection route revised in its point 14: browser and paste, no embedded window and no revision of 43; library DLC revised in decision 83)

**Decision (route chosen by the user on October 23, 2026; design recommended by the architect):** after the installed-games slice of 81, the user wants for EA the same as for Ubisoft: the uninstalled games of their account, with covers, and Install. **They chose the same route as for Ubisoft:** the embedded login window of 80 (WebView2 from the Go helper) with the official EA page. The difference from Ubisoft is what is captured: there is nothing useful in `localStorage`. The window, with its own session, finally navigates to an EA URL that answers with a JSON carrying an access token, and the capture reads **only** that `access_token` from the page text. With it, EA's GraphQL gives the owned games with the same `contentId` as `installerdata.xml` (81), with no local cache or file-based translation.

**Revised on 24-10-2026 (point 14, user decision):** the embedded window cannot be used to sign in with Google. EA is connected only in the user's browser, by opening the same token URL and pasting the JSON, as in Epic. What follows about the window (points 1 to 3 and 8 to 12) is revised by point 14 where it does not match; the session, the library, the covers and Install (points 4 to 7) do not change.

#### 1. Scope

- **In:**
  - the EA wizard with the `embedded-login` step of 80 (point 2);
  - a small change to the helper and to the step contract: capturing the JSON text of the page and reaching `doneUrl` by navigation (point 3);
  - the minimal session: the encrypted access token with its expiry, without renewal (point 4);
  - `listLibrary` with the owned games and their `contentId` (point 5);
  - covers from `packArt` (point 6);
  - Install with `origin2://…&autoDownload=1` (point 7);
  - "Connected as <name>", disconnect, `expired` and the gray veil, as in 77 and 80;
  - the "EA app not found" message of 81 also for Install.
- **Out:**
  - renewal without the user (there is no renewal token in this flow; point 4 and 12.2);
  - DLC (`dlc: 'none'`, they are skipped and counted);
  - play time, matching across stores, subscriptions (EA Play) beyond what the API gives as owned;
  - sign-in with external providers (Google, Apple, consoles…): if the page offers them and they leave `authHosts`, the window blocks them (point 2);
  - Docker mode (the window needs the user's desktop; phase 2 with the local agent);
  - covers of installed games without an account (as in 81).
- **Revision of 43 for EA (withdrawn in point 14: for EA, 43 applies again as is).** It is the same one that 80 made for Ubisoft (80, point 2), with the same mandatory mitigations: the user types the password on the official EA page, but inside a window controlled by Ludiary. The user chose this route and confirmed it expressly on 23-10-2026 (point 12). Steam, GOG and Epic do not change.
- **Fixed rules of this decision:**
  - Ludiary **does not take cookies** out of the window or store them: the EA session lives in the window's temporary profile, which is emptied and deleted on close (80, A3);
  - the `client_secret` of the EA app and any hardware fingerprint are not used, and neither the EA app nor its `User-Agent` is imitated;
  - only the `access_token` crosses the helper's pipe, validated in three layers (helper, platform and core), as in 80.

#### 2. Login and capture (`connectors/ea/src/wizard.ts` and `auth.ts`) (revised in point 14: the step table, `authHosts` and the `embedded` entry no longer apply; the token URL and "On receiving" remain)

**Route checked on 23-10-2026** (public requests without an account): `https://www.ea.com/login` answers 303 to `accounts.ea.com/connect/auth` (`client_id=EADOTCOM-WEB-SERVER`, return to `https://www.ea.com/login_check`), which answers 302 to `signin.ea.com/p/juno/login`, where the password is typed. On the other hand, `accounts.ea.com/connect/auth?client_id=ORIGIN_JS_SDK&response_type=token&redirect_uri=nucleus:rest&prompt=none` answers with a JSON: without a session, `login_required`; with the window's session, an access token. This is how Lutris and the old Origin integration for Galaxy do it (assumptions EAA1 and EAA2).

| Id | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `login` | `embedded-login` | `url`: `https://www.ea.com/login`. `doneUrl`: `https://www.ea.com/login_check` (reached by navigation, point 3). `captureUrl`: `https://accounts.ea.com/connect/auth?client_id=ORIGIN_JS_SDK&response_type=token&redirect_uri=nucleus:rest&prompt=none`, a constant in `auth.ts` (with a query, point 3). `capture`: a single field, `accessToken`, with `source: 'document-json'`, `jsonField` `access_token`, the `pattern` from point 4 and `maxLength` 8192. Body: "A window with the official EA page will open. Sign in there, also with the verification code if it asks for one; the window will close by itself. Ludiary does not store your password". |

- **`authHosts` = `allowedHosts`:** `www.ea.com`, `accounts.ea.com` and `signin.ea.com`, the three of the checked route (three of the four the helper admits). If the manual test shows another needed host in `blockedHosts`, the list is extended with a note in this decision and an `auditor` review (80, B5).
- **No language parameter:** which one `www.ea.com/login` accepts has not been checked; the page uses its own. If the test shows one, it is added according to `ctx.locale` in a small change.
- **Constants:** `ORIGIN_JS_SDK` and `nucleus:rest` go in a public URL and are not secrets. There is no `client_secret` or headers of the EA app.
- **What happens in each case:**
  - the user signs in: the window goes through `login_check`, navigates to the token URL and the capture reads `access_token`;
  - the token URL answers `login_required` or has no `access_token` (for example, because the session was not created): after the 10 s retries, `capture-missing` → `wizard.embedded.captureMissing`;
  - if EA answered with a redirect to `nucleus:rest#…` instead of a JSON, the window cancels it as an external protocol (80, A1): nothing leaves and the result is `capture-missing`.
- **Common text:** `wizard.embedded.captureMissing` becomes "The session could not be read. Try again", without the "Remember me" checkbox, which was specific to Ubisoft. The Ubisoft body already asks for it (80, B2).
- **On receiving `embedded`** (`submit`, with the usual 30 s):
  1. identity query to the GraphQL (point 5) with the captured token; it proves the token is valid, like the renewal in 80;
  2. 401 or 403: `auth.invalid` with `connectors.ea.error.login` ("EA did not accept the sign-in. Try again"); 429: `store.rate-limited`; any other failure: its code;
  3. `secrets.set('accessToken', …)` and `secrets.set('accessTokenExpiresAt', …)` (point 4);
  4. `done` with `accountLabel` = the visible name from the response, without control characters and trimmed to 64; if missing, no name.
- No `choose` step: without an account, EA stays as in 81 (installed games and Play), and canceling leaves it that way.

#### 3. Change to the helper and to the `embedded-login` step (extends 80, points 5 and 6; additive, `contractVersion` stays at 1; per point 14, `document-json` and `captureUrl` with a query are unused for now and reaching by navigation continues for Ubisoft)

Three small changes. They apply to any store; for Ubisoft the result does not change (step 1 of its manual test is repeated, point 10).

**a) `document-json` capture mode.** (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)

- Contract: each `capture` field admits `source?: 'local-storage' | 'document-json'`, by default `'local-storage'` (what exists today). With `'document-json'`, `storageKeys` is empty or absent; with `'local-storage'`, 1 to 3 keys as today. All the fields of a step use the same `source`. The same in the `EmbeddedLogin` port and in the helper protocol (`"source"` in each field). (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)
- **Second fixed script**, a constant in Go, with the parameters as a JSON literal from `json.Marshal` (like the first one):
  - it takes the `textContent` of the first `pre` child of `body` if it exists (Chromium renders a JSON document that way, assumption EAA3) and, if not, `document.body.textContent`;
  - if that text exceeds 64 KiB, it returns everything as `null`;
  - `JSON.parse` inside a `try`; only an object that is not a list is valid;
  - for each field, it takes the own property `[jsonField]` only if it is text;
  - it returns an object with the requested names and nothing else.
- It does not read cookies, `localStorage`, forms or keystrokes. The 64 KiB limit on the result, the `Source()` check before each `ExecuteScript` and the 500 ms retries for 10 s still apply (80, M3).

**b) `captureUrl` with a query, only in `document-json`.** (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)

- The core (`wizards.ts`) and the helper accept a query in `captureUrl` only if the step uses `document-json`; with `local-storage` it still has no query. Fragment, never. `doneUrl` still has no query. (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)
- With `document-json`, the match against `captureUrl` (on arriving at it and before each `ExecuteScript`) is **exact** in scheme, host, path and query, not just origin and path. Reason: in EA the path `/connect/auth` also appears during login with a different `client_id`; only the page the helper itself navigated to is read. (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)

**c) Reaching `doneUrl` by navigation.**

- Today (80, point 19) the machine goes from `start` to `done` when the main document **finishes loading** at `doneUrl`, even if the load fails (`atDone`). In EA, `login_check` is probably a redirect (assumption EAA4) and never finishes loading as such.
- New rule, for all stores:
  1. in `start`, an **allowed** `NavigationStarting` of the main document (also with `IsRedirected`) whose URL matches `doneUrl` in origin and path leaves the machine **armed**;
  2. once armed, the next `NavigationCompleted` of the main document, with or without success and at whatever URL, moves to `done`; then the helper navigates to `captureUrl` (or captures, if they are the same);
  3. when not armed, no load counts. `atDone` is replaced by this rule (it covers it) and its test is adapted.
- States are still never skipped: `capture` requires `done`, and `done` requires having navigated to `doneUrl`. The first visit to a page with the path of `captureUrl` is never read.

**Helper tests (Go):** `document-json` script built with `json.Marshal` (quotes, slashes and line breaks escaped); `captureUrl` with a different query → not captured; text in `pre` and without `pre`; text over 64 KiB → `capture-missing`; JSON that is a list, text or number, and `access_token` absent or not text → `capture-missing`; fields with mixed `source`, `storageKeys` with `document-json` or a query in `captureUrl` with `local-storage` → `bad-request`; armed by a `NavigationStarting` with `IsRedirected` → the next load, at another URL, leads to `captureUrl`; a `NavigationStarting` canceled by the filter does not arm; when not armed nothing is captured; the Ubisoft route (`/ready` with 404 and then `/login`) still captures. (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)

#### 4. Session and errors (decision 46, minimum of this slice)

- **What is stored,** encrypted in `secrets` with scope `store:ea`: `accessToken` and `accessTokenExpiresAt` (milliseconds, as text; it is not a secret, but goes alongside the token to avoid adding a table). Nothing else: this flow gives no renewal token and Ludiary does not store cookies.
- **Accepted form:** `^[A-Za-z0-9+/=_.-]{64,8192}$` (assumption EAA5). It is a subset of the redactor pattern of 80 (B3, `[A-Za-z0-9+/=_.-]{64,}`), so **the redactor does not change**. If the test shows another form, the acceptance pattern and the redactor pattern are changed together, with the second as a superset of the first (as in UB3).
- **Expiry:** `accessTokenExpiresAt = ctx.now() + 50 minutes` on capture. Assumption EAA6: the token lasts about 60 minutes (`expires_in` of 3599 s in the old Origin integration for Galaxy; unverified); the 10-minute margin avoids making requests with a token about to expire. `expires_in` is not read so as not to capture a second value; if the test shows another duration, the constant is changed.
- **`connection.status`** (local): `connected` if both values are read and `now < accessTokenExpiresAt`; otherwise, `expired`.
- **In `listLibrary`:**
  - no readable token: `auth.required` (the store shows as `expired`);
  - expired by the clock: `auth.expired` with `connectors.ea.error.expired` ("The EA session has expired. Reconnect to update your EA games"), **with no request at all**;
  - 401 or 403: `auth.expired`, the same;
  - 429: `store.rate-limited` with `Retry-After`; network error: its code, without moving to `expired`; any other status: `store.unexpected-response`.
  - With `auth.*` the core moves the store to `expired` and does not touch the library. The secret's row is not deleted.
- **What this means for the user** (consequence of the minimum, product decision in 12.2): the EA library is updated in the sync that follows connecting. After one hour, the store becomes `expired`: the games already stored stay in the library with the gray veil, installed ones can be played and **Install keeps working** (the URI does not need the token). To update the list you have to reconnect, with the full login, because the window's profile is new on each login (80, A3).
- **Epoch, disconnect, `expired` and gray veil:** identical to 77 and 80, with scope `store:ea`. No remote revocation. `connectors.ea.disconnect.hint`: "Ludiary deletes its EA session from this computer. To sign out of all sessions, change your password at ea.com".
- **Never leave** the token, the account name, any person ID or the email: not in logs, not in errors, not in the helper (which logs nothing).

#### 5. Library and ID translation (`connectors/ea/src/library.ts`)

- **Request:** `POST https://service-aggregation-layer.juno.ea.com/graphql` with `authorization` = `makeSecret('Bearer ' + token.reveal())` and JSON body `{ query, variables }`, with the queries as constants in `library.ts`. No `User-Agent`, `Origin` or `Referer` of its own. If EA rejects the `POST`, it switches to `GET` with the query in the URL, like Lutris, in the same commit as its test (assumption EAA7). In all cases: 401 or 403 → `auth.expired`; 429 → `store.rate-limited`; `errors` in the body, another status or without the expected list → `store.unexpected-response`.
- **Identity** (only in the wizard): the player's visible name (`me { player { displayName } }` according to Lutris; assumption EAA8, unverified). Person IDs are not requested.
- **Order in `listLibrary`:**
  1. token and expiry (point 4), without network if they are not valid;
  2. **`getEntitlements`**, paginated with `next`. From each entitlement only the offer ID is read. Limits: 200 pages and 50,000 entitlements; a repeated `next` (cycle) or an exceeded limit → `store.unexpected-response`. Offer IDs must meet `ID_BODY` of 81 (point 12, B4; for example `Origin.OFR.…`); if not, they are skipped and leave `complete: false`. No duplicates;
  3. **`getOffers`** in batches of 50 IDs (assumption EAA9). From each offer only the offer ID, `contentId`, the title, `packArt` and the field saying whether it is a base game or additional content are read;
  4. **per offer:**
     - additional content: out and counted (`notGame`); without the type field: treated as a game and counted (`noType`), because losing a game is worse than showing a DLC;
     - `contentId` absent or not meeting `ID_BODY`: out and counted (`untranslated`), with `complete: false` (rule B7 of 80);
     - entry `{ storeGameId: contentId, kind: 'game', title, media }`. `title` without control characters, trimmed and at most 300; if missing, `EA <contentId>`. `media`, from point 6;
     - duplicates by `storeGameId` (several editions with the same `contentId`): the offer with the lowest ID wins and is counted (`duplicateContent`);
  5. **`complete`:** `true` if all pages were read, `getOffers` returned all the requested offers and there were no invalid IDs or `untranslated`. The core already protects against an empty list with stored games (74).
- **ID translation:** no cache or file is needed. The offer's `contentId` is the same as the `contentID` of `installerdata.xml` with which 81 stores the installed game (assumption EAA10), so same ID = same ownership, and the API title replaces that of the file (rule of 74). If the test shows that the API gives another of the file's `contentID`s (editions), the game would appear twice; that would be decided separately.
- **Games bought in another store:** they appear if the API gives them as owned, with the same criterion the user chose for Ubisoft (80, point 16).
- **Log:** counters only (`pages`, `entitlements`, `offers`, `notGame`, `noType`, `untranslated`, `duplicateContent`, `invalidArt`). No name, person ID, titles or offer IDs.
- **Core:** the `library` operation of 74 does not change. No `library` locations or `ctx.fs`. `minSyncIntervalMs` goes from 60 s to 30 minutes, like GOG, Epic and Ubisoft (scans are not subject to that floor, decision 72), and `trigger: 'open'` stays at 12 h.

#### 6. Covers

- **Source:** `packArt` of the offer. It is valid only if it is text with an `https` URL, without user or port, with the exact host of `mediaHosts` and at most 1024 characters; then it is `coverUrl`. If not (another host, another form, an object), no cover and it is counted (`invalidArt`).
- **`mediaHosts: ['drop-assets.ea.com']`.** The `packArt` host is **not confirmed**: it is the one the EA website uses for its images (assumption EAA11). The CSP (`img-src`) and `vite.config.ts` add it (parity test of 71). If the manual test shows another host, `mediaHosts`, the CSP and `vite.config.ts` are changed in the same commit, with a note here and an `auditor` review.
- `resolveMedia` does not exist: the browser requests the images with the user's IP, as with the other stores (invariant 9).
- Owned installed games get a cover through the same entry; without an account, they still have no cover (81, point 5).

#### 7. Install

- `resolveAction('install')` (`connectors/ea/src/launch.ts`):
  1. `storeGameId` must meet `ID_BODY`; if not, `action.unsupported` with `connectors.ea.errors.invalidId`;
  2. same EA app check as `play` (81, point 4.3), with `launch.launcher-missing` and `connectors.ea.errors.launcherMissing`;
  3. `installerdata.xml` is not read (the game is not installed);
  4. `const uri = \`origin2://game/launch?offerIds=${id}&autoDownload=1\``, with **a single ID**, the stored one;
  5. **final assertion:** `^origin2://game/launch\?offerIds=ID_BODY&autoDownload=1$`, with the same `ID_BODY` as 81; if it does not match (connector failure), `internal`;
  6. `{ kind: 'uri', uri }`.
- It is the URI used by Lutris and the Galaxy integration for the EA app (assumption EAA12). `validateLaunchUri` accepts it (`&` and `=` are in its range and there are no quotes) and `openWithShellHandler` passes it to `rundll32` without a shell; that the `&` reaches the EA app intact is NV2, like NV1 in 81.
- `actions: ['play', 'install']`. No changes in the core or in `uriSchemes`. The web shows "Opening the EA app…" (`game.installing` with `{store}`).

#### 8. Manifest (changes over 81; `authHosts` and texts revised in point 14)

- `access: 'unofficial-api'` (formerly `'local-only'`), with its fragility icon.
- `capabilities`: `library: true`, `scan: true`, `dlc: 'none'`, `actions: ['play', 'install']`, `launchKinds: ['uri']`, `uriSchemes: ['origin2']`, `storePlaytime: false`, `price: false`.
- `minSyncIntervalMs: 1_800_000` (decision 50; scans are not subject to it).
- `authHosts: ['www.ea.com', 'accounts.ea.com', 'signin.ea.com']`, `apiHosts: ['service-aggregation-layer.juno.ea.com']`, `mediaHosts: ['drop-assets.ea.com']`.
- `locations` unchanged (`ea-libraries` and `ea-desktop`); no `library` location.
- `connection: eaConnection` (`wizard.ts`) and `listLibrary: listEaLibrary` (`library.ts`).
- `checkConnectorManifest` accepts it as is: `connection` with `authHosts` and `library` with `apiHosts`.
- **New files** in `connectors/ea/src`: `auth.ts`, `wizard.ts` and `library.ts`; `launch.ts` and `manifest.ts` grow. No new dependencies.
- **New texts** (es and en): `connectors.ea.login.title`, `.login.body`, `.login.window`, `connectors.ea.error.login`, `.error.expired` and `connectors.ea.disconnect.hint`. The common `wizard.embedded.captureMissing` changes (point 2).
- **Web:** `real.ts` extends the list of stores with a real wizard to `['steam', 'gog', 'epic', 'ubisoft', 'ea']`; the simulator adds the EA step; the EA card stops being `not-applicable`.
- The EA row of the table in 40 becomes `unofficial-api` with an account through the embedded login window (per point 14, with an account through the browser and paste).

#### 9. Tests

**Invented fixtures**, copying nothing from real responses: token `ea-test-access-token-…` of 64 characters or more; name `TestUser`; offers `Origin.OFR.50.0000001`…; `contentId` `9000001`…; `packArt` `https://drop-assets.ea.com/test/9000001.jpg`. `privacy.ts` adds those constants to `ALLOWED` and a rule that rejects `"access_token"` followed by any other value.

- **Helper (Go):** those of point 3.
- **Platform:** `embedded-login.ts` passes `source` to the helper and validates the response as today; a field with an unknown `source` → `failed`.
- **Core (`wizards.ts`):** `document-json` with `storageKeys` → `internal`; a query in `captureUrl` with `local-storage` → `internal`; mixed `source` → `internal`; a query in `captureUrl` with `document-json` → accepted; the rest of the tests of 80 keep passing. (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)
- **`connectors/ea`:**
  - wizard: exact step (`url`, `doneUrl`, `captureUrl`, `capture`); with `embedded`, identity query with the header as `Secret`; `set` of the two values with `accessTokenExpiresAt = now + 50 min`; sanitized or absent name; 401 → `auth.invalid`; token with another form → rejected by the core before reaching the connector;
  - session: `status` `connected` before the time and `expired` after; expired `listLibrary` → `auth.expired` **with no request at all**; without a token → `auth.required`; 401, 403, 429 and network error;
  - `getEntitlements`: several pages with `next`; repeated `next`; 201 pages; 50,001 entitlements; invalid offer ID → skipped and `complete: false`;
  - `getOffers`: batches of exactly 50; offer not returned → `complete: false`; additional content → out; without type → game and `noType`; without `contentId` → `untranslated` and `complete: false`; two offers with the same `contentId` → the one with the lowest ID; `errors` in the body;
  - covers: valid `packArt` → exact `coverUrl`; another host, `http`, with user or port, of 1025 characters or not text → no cover and `invalidArt`;
  - `install` → exactly `origin2://game/launch?offerIds=9000001&autoDownload=1`; invalid ID → `action.unsupported` without building the URI; without the app → `launch.launcher-missing`;
  - no log or error carries the token, the name, offer IDs, titles or paths;
  - `assertConnectorConformance`.
- **`runtime`:** CSP parity with `drop-assets.ea.com`; the redactor masks a token of the form in point 4.
- **Web:** `real.ts` sends EA to the API; the EA card with the login step. Playwright with a test double port, pending as in 72 to 81.

#### 10. Manual test (prepared by the `tester` in `docs/manual-tests/ea.md`, section "Account (ADR 82)"; done by the user; steps 1 to 3 revised in point 14)

The login and the library do not need the EA app; Install and Play do (today it is not on the user's PC, 81).

1. Connect from Settings: the window opens with the EA page; sign in (and the code, if asked); the window closes by itself and "Connected as <name>" appears (EAA1, EAA2, EAA4, EAA8). Note `blockedHosts` from the log.
2. Close the window without signing in, and again press Cancel in the web: message in the same step.
3. After each attempt, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ludiary\tmp` has no `webview-*` folders.
4. Library: the owned games appear with cover (EAA11) and veil. Note from the log `entitlements`, `offers`, `notGame`, `noType`, `untranslated`, `duplicateContent` and `invalidArt`. If an installed game appears twice, note both IDs (EAA10).
5. With the EA app installed: Install on an uninstalled game opens its download in the app (EAA12, NV2); note whether it starts downloading without asking.
6. Sync one hour after connecting: the card shows "The EA session has expired…", the library stays with the veil and Install keeps working. Note the approximate time (EAA6).
7. Reconnect: the list is updated.
8. Disconnect: gray veil on the uninstalled ones; the installed ones remain playable.
9. The exported log does not contain the token, the name, the email, offer IDs or paths.
10. **Ubisoft regression** (point 3): repeat step 1 of the test in 80.

#### 11. Implementation order and parallel work

1. **First, in parallel:**
   - `packager`: point 3 in the helper (`document-json`, exact query, arming by navigation) with its Go tests, and `source` in `embedded-login.ts`;
   - `developer`: `source` in the contract, the step validation in `wizards.ts`, the common `captureMissing` text and `privacy.ts`;
   - `auditor`: review of the design **before the code**: the second script, the exact match with a query, arming by navigation (so that it does not allow reading a page the helper did not navigate to), the hosts and that no cookies are read.
2. **Then:** `connectors`: `auth.ts`, `wizard.ts`, `library.ts`, `install`, manifest and texts, against the `testkit`. Then web, `runtime` and CSP, and the `auditor` review of the code.
3. **At the end:** the manual test (point 10) and the `docs-writer`:
   - EA connection guide: the window, the password typed on the official page inside a Ludiary window, and that **the session lasts about an hour** and you have to reconnect to update the list;
   - privacy: what goes to EA and that the window is Microsoft Edge WebView2 (as in 80, B6);
   - unofficial-route notice;
   - troubleshooting: "The EA session has expired", `captureMissing` and `runtimeMissing`.

#### 12. What the user decides (product only)

**Decided by the user on 23-10-2026:** the embedded window route, the same as in Ubisoft (revised on 24-10-2026 in point 14: browser and paste; the following confirmation becomes moot for EA).

**Expressly confirmed by the user on 23-10-2026** ("Yes, like Ubisoft"): they accept for EA the same as for Ubisoft (80, point 2), the password is typed on the official EA page inside a window controlled by Ludiary.

**Decided by the user on 23-10-2026:** 12.2 (a), "Reconnect on expiry" (as designed). (b), keeping the window's profile, is discarded for now.

**Applied by default, unless the user says otherwise:** 12.1 (a), 12.3 (a) and 12.4 (a).

1. **Account name:** (a) "Connected as <name>" (recommended, as in the other stores); (b) just "Connected".
2. **When the session expires (about an hour):** (a) the store becomes `expired` and the user reconnects whenever they want to update the list (recommended for now: it is the minimum and stores nothing but the token); (b) later, renew without the user by keeping the window's profile between logins, encrypted, to repeat the token URL without asking for the password. (b) revises the mitigation of 80 that the profile is deleted on each login and stores the EA session on disk; it would go in its own decision, with an `auditor` review.
3. **Install:** (a) with `autoDownload=1`, like Lutris and Galaxy (recommended: the user already pressed Install), even though the EA app may start the download without asking (EAA12); (b) without `autoDownload`, if the test shows that this makes the app open the game's page.
4. **EA games bought on Steam or Epic:** (a) they also appear under EA if the API gives them as owned, as they chose for Ubisoft (recommended for consistency); (b) only those bought on EA, if the API makes it possible to tell them apart.

#### 13. Auditor review of the design (October 23, 2026)

No criticals. What follows takes precedence over points 2 to 9 where it does not match.

- **M1 (medium). Arming bound to its navigation** (point 3 c):
  - arming stores the `NavigationId` of the `NavigationStarting` that armed; only the `NavigationCompleted` with that same id counts (another `NavigationCompleted` does not move to `done`);
  - "if they are the same" compares the request's `doneUrl` and `captureUrl`, not the URL that was reached;
  - with `document-json`, the `capture` state starts only with the `NavigationCompleted` of the navigation to `captureUrl` that the helper launched after `done`; any `NavigationStarting` of the main document during `capture` gives `capture-missing`; (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)
  - Go test for each rule.
- **M2 (medium). `blockedHosts` without URL.** For a URL without a host (for example `nucleus:rest#access_token=…`), `blockedHosts` stores only the scheme with `:` (`nucleus:`) or nothing; never the URL or the fragment. Tests: Go (navigation to `nucleus:rest#access_token=…` → the token does not appear in `blockedHosts`) and platform (an entry without a host form is discarded).
- **M3 (medium). User confirmation** about the password in the window: already given (point 12).
- **Lows:**
  - references in 80 to this change: flow in point 5 (reaching `doneUrl`), TS in point 6 (`doneUrl`, `captureUrl` and `source?: "local-storage" | "document-json"`), step validation, `ExecuteScript` in point 18 and `atDone` in point 19; (withdrawn on 5-11-2026, see 82)
  - the core rejects (`internal`) a step whose `url` and `doneUrl` have the same origin and path (it would arm on the first navigation);
  - `captureUrl` is compared after `url.Parse` by `Scheme`, lowercase `Host`, and exact `Path` and `RawQuery`;
  - the `ORIGIN_JS_SDK` constant is a terms-of-use risk (it identifies an EA client), like the `Ubi-AppId` of 80; it is declared as such in the guide and in "Main risks";
  - new assumption EAA0: EA has no official API for the library;
  - `getOffers` only accepts offers from the requested batch (the others are ignored and counted); the fallback `GET` (EAA7) builds the query with `URLSearchParams` and never logs the URL; requests run in series and without retries;
  - the log adds `invalidArtHosts`: at most 8, host only, to adjust EAA11;
  - "Main risks" is updated: Ubisoft and EA have an account through a login window on unofficial internal APIs; in EA the session lasts about an hour.

#### 14. Login with Google: browser and paste (user decision, 24-10-2026; revises points 1 to 3 and 8 to 12 for EA)

**Finding from the manual test (24-10-2026).** With "Sign in with Google" in the embedded window nothing opens:

- the window denies all pop-up windows (protection A1 of 80) and Google opens a pop-up with `accounts.google.com`;
- moreover, Google blocks sign-in in embedded browsers (Google policy since 2021, warning "This browser or app may not be secure"). Getting around it would require imitating a browser, against the fixed rules of point 1;
- the user always signs in to EA with Google, so the embedded window is of no use to them.

**User decision (24-10-2026, relayed by the main session):** EA is connected **only** through the user's browser and by pasting the result, as in Epic (decision 78). It applies to Google and to email and password. **The embedded window is no longer used for EA**; it remains only for Ubisoft (80). There is no step to choose between two routes: the wizard contract does not allow it without extending it, and with a single route it is not needed.

**Single wizard step** (`connectors/ea/src/wizard.ts`; replaces the table in point 2):

| Id | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `login` | `open-external`, `awaits: 'input'`, with a field | `url`: the token URL from point 2, a constant in `auth.ts`: `https://accounts.ea.com/connect/auth?client_id=ORIGIN_JS_SDK&response_type=token&redirect_uri=nucleus:rest&prompt=none`. Body: "First sign in to ea.com in your browser (with Google if you like). Then open the link. You will see a text between braces: copy all of it and press Paste". Field `accessToken`: `secret: true`, `paste: true`, `extract: 'json-field:access_token'`, the `pattern` from point 4 (`^[A-Za-z0-9+/=_.-]{64,8192}$`) and `maxLength` 8192. |

- **Extraction:** the `json-field` rule of 78 (core and web), with no type changes. The web sends **only** the extracted value, never the pasted text (78, M2). The pasted text may carry other fields (`token_type`, `expires_in`): they are not read.
- **Page error:** if what was pasted is a JSON object without the requested field but with an own property `error` of type text (for example `login_required`), the web sends nothing and shows the new common text `wizard.paste.storeError`: "The page answered with an error instead of the code. Sign in first on the store's website in your browser and open the link again". The value of `error` is neither shown nor logged.
