`updates.notes`, `updates.restartConfirm`, `updates.state.downloading`, `updates.privacy`, `updates.error.*` and `tray.updateAvailable` are reused.

**Tests:**

- `runtime` (`updates-service.test.ts`):
  - with no stored setting, `mode` is `notify` and there is a request at 60 s **without** a completed wizard or `noticeSeen` (replaces the test "no request before the wizard or `noticeSeen`" of point 18);
  - `off` still makes no request at all (double that fails if called);
  - new version with a bad signature or from another key → `failed` with `manifest-invalid`, without `latest` or `available`; with a good signature → `available`;
  - already verified version: the next cycle (`304`) does not download the manifest again;
  - version in `badVersions`: verified the same and `latestFailedBefore` comes out;
  - `later`: `snoozed` for 24 h, disappears when the time passes, with a newer version and in a new instance of the service;
  - `updated` survives a download that starts before the `ack`.
- `api-contract` and `api` (`updates.test.ts`): `later` accepted; `noticeSeen` rejected; `mode: null` is no longer valid in the state; `PUT` with `later` requires a session and the origin key.
- `web` (`updates.test.ts`): `showPrompt` (notify/auto/off, `available`, `ready`, `latestFailedBefore`, `snoozed`); those of `needsChoice` are deleted. Adjust `data/mock.ts` and `data/real.test.ts`.
- Manual test (point 16): step 7 becomes "`notify` by default: without touching anything, the notice appears with the link to the notes; Later hides it until restart; Ignore asks for confirmation and leaves About at `off`; Apply downloads, restarts and opens the new version with the banner, which does not return once closed". Step 1 is done by choosing `auto` in the wizard. Step 6 (`off`, no connection) is kept.

**Reason.** The user wants to learn about every version without configuring anything and to decide for themselves when to install, with `auto` as an option. With invariant 9 changed, the M5 gate no longer protects anything and the card only asked for a choice that now has a default value. Notifying only after verifying the signature avoids announcing a version that would later be rejected; it costs two 64 KiB downloads per new version, outside the API quota. Composing the link instead of using `html_url` leaves the web with no data from the network. "Later" in memory needs no setting or migration. Everything else (modes, download, "Restart and update", one-time notices, ack) is reused.

**Consequences.**

- Closes 15.1 (`notify`) and 15.2 (a). Revises M5 (no gate) and points 5 and 10 (no single card; notice with three buttons). Decision 32 asked for `auto` by default: the user changes it to `notify`, with `auto` selectable.
- Outgoing call to GitHub from the first run, unless the user chooses `off`; two more requests to `github.com` per new version.
- No migration or new routes; contract with breaking changes (`mode` without `null`, `noticeSeen` out, `later` and `snoozed` in), with no external clients (the browser API's `contractVersion`, if it exists, does not change: web and server go together).
- Files: `packages/runtime/src/updates/service.ts` and `facade.ts`; `packages/api-contract/src/index.ts`; `apps/web/src/app/updates.ts`, `components/UpdatesNotice.tsx`, `components/UpdatesPanel.tsx` (selector comment), `pages/Welcome.tsx`, `data/mock.ts`; `es.json` and `en.json`; and their tests.
- `docs-writer`: privacy guide (check active by default, what goes out, how to turn it off) and updates guide (the three buttons and the banner).
- Cost: low (about 150 lines with tests).

#### 21. Semi-automatic publishing: draft from CI and local signing (November 4, 2026; specifies 11.3 and 11.6 with 15.3 (a); revises 11.1 and 11.6; tag form revised in point 22)

Assignment from the user (semi-automatic mode): when a PR is merged into `main`, GitHub Actions builds on `windows-latest`, generates the installer and an unsigned `ludiary-update.json` and creates a **draft** release `v<version>` with the PR description as notes. The maintainer signs on their machine with `release:sign`, uploads the `.sig` and publishes. The private key never goes to GitHub. Version according to the PR label (`release:patch`, `release:minor`, `release:major`); with no label, there is no version.

**Decision.**

1. **Trigger and permissions.**

   | Option | Advantages | Costs |
   |---|---|---|
   | A. `pull_request` with `types: [closed]` and `merged == true` | Brings the PR in the event. | In a PR from a *fork*, the `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only whatever `permissions` says (assumption CI1), so it could not create the draft. It is a project open to contributions (60): it would fail precisely on those PRs. |
   | **B. `push` to `main` and look up the commit's PR** (chosen) | It always runs in the repository's context, with the already merged workflow (reviewed in the PR) and the token each job asks for. A direct `push`, without a PR, does not generate a version. If the label was forgotten, it is set and the run is re-run. | One more call: `GET /repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls`. |

   - `on: push: branches: [main]`. `permissions: {}` at the root of the workflow; each job asks for its own. All jobs with `if: github.repository == 'chamanRMA/Ludiary'` (a *fork* publishes nothing).
   - **Forbidden:** `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` and any `secrets.*`. The workflow has no secrets: only the `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
   - Three jobs:

     | Job | System | Permissions | Does |
     |---|---|---|---|
     | `plan` | `ubuntu-latest` | `contents: read`, `pull-requests: read` | Finds the PR, reads the label, computes the version and writes the notes (points 2 and 3). No `pnpm install`. |
     | `build` | `windows-latest` | `contents: read` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `release:build` and `release:manifest`. Uploads the files as an artifact. |
     | `release` | `ubuntu-latest` | `contents: write` | Downloads the artifacts and creates the draft with `gh`. No `checkout` or `pnpm`. |

     Reason for separating `build` and `release`: `pnpm install` runs third-party dependency code. That code must not run with a token that can write to the repository.

2. **Version.**

   | Option | Advantages | Costs |
   |---|---|---|
   | **A. The latest `v*` tag plus the bump; only a tag is created** (chosen) | No robot commit in `main`: no clash with branch protection, no `push` loops and no `contents: write` in `plan`. The scripts already accept `LUDIARY_VERSION` (`version()` in `release-lib.mjs`). | `package.json` does not say the published version (the tag does). |
   | B. `version` in `apps/desktop/package.json`, bumped with a commit | The version is in the tree. | The robot pushes to `main` (branch protection, one more `push` that triggers the workflow again and write permissions before building). |

   - **Base** (*revised in point 22: between `vX.Y.Z` and `X.Y.Z`, and the new tag is given by `tagFor`*): the greatest version among the repository's `refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` tags (`gh api --paginate repos/{repo}/git/matching-refs/tags/v`). Only those matching `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` count; the rest are ignored. With none, the base is `0.0.0`. A draft's tag does not exist until it is published (assumption CI2), so an unpublished draft does not consume a version.
   - **Bump:** `release:patch` gives X.Y.(Z+1); `release:minor`, X.(Y+1).0; `release:major`, (X+1).0.0. With no `release:*` label: `plan` ends green with "no release:* label, no version" in the summary, and `build` and `release` are skipped. With more than one: it fails with a clear message and nothing else runs.
   - **The commit's PR:** from the response of `commits/{sha}/pulls`, the only PR with a non-null `merged_at`, `base.ref == "main"` and `merge_commit_sha == GITHUB_SHA`. It works for merge, *squash* and *rebase*. If there is none (direct `push`), there is no version.
   - **No commit:** `apps/desktop/package.json` stays at `0.0.0`, the mark of development builds (`0.0.0-proto`, `unsupported`, point 19). The version reaches `build` as an output of `plan`, already validated with `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`, and is passed in `env: LUDIARY_VERSION` (never written inside `run:`). `release-build.mjs` and `release-manifest.mjs` already read it from there. The tag is created by GitHub when publishing, over `--target <GITHUB_SHA>`. For a manual publication without CI, the maintainer passes `LUDIARY_VERSION`.
   - It is done by a new script, `apps/desktop/scripts/release-plan.mjs` (only `node:*`, no dependencies). It reads the JSON files that `gh` leaves and writes to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` (`release`, `version` and `pr`) and to `notes.md`. The logic lives in an exported pure function, `planRelease({ pulls, tags, sha })`, with tests.

3. **PR notes without injection.**
   - The body is never interpolated into `run:`, neither with `${{ github.event.* }}` nor with any output that comes from the PR. `gh api … > pulls.json` leaves it in a file. `release-plan.mjs` reads it with `JSON.parse` and writes `notes.md`, which travels as an artifact. `release` passes it with `gh release create … --notes-file notes.md`. It does not go through any shell, nor `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, nor `$GITHUB_ENV`.
   - The only outputs of `plan` used in other jobs are `release` (`true` or `false`), `version` (validated with its expression) and `pr` (integer). `plan` validates them before writing them.
   - **Cap:** 30,000 characters, cutting at a character boundary and not a byte one. If cut, "… (notes truncated, see PR #N)" is appended. An empty or null body is replaced by the PR title. A line with `PR #N` and the short commit is always appended at the end. The cap leaves margin under GitHub's limit for a release body (assumption CI3).
   - The notes are seen only on GitHub, which sanitizes the Markdown. The SPA does not render remote text (point 20). The maintainer reviews them in the draft before publishing.

4. **Actions.** Only GitHub's own (`actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node` with `node-version-file: .node-version`, `actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file: apps/desktop/launcher/go.mod`, `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact`), each **pinned by the full commit SHA**, with the version in a comment. No third-party action. Everything else, with `gh` and what the runner provides.
   - **pnpm:** `corepack enable`, which reads `packageManager` (Node 24 still ships corepack; assumption CI4). No `pnpm/action-setup`. This revises the assumption in the line "`pnpm/action-setup` reads it" of decision 39.
   - **Inno Setup:** it is not listed in the `windows-2025` image (assumption CI5). The official installer is downloaded from `github.com/jrsoftware/issrc/releases` (jrsoftware.org no longer hosts the `.exe` files) at the pinned version (the 6.x with which the prototype was validated), its SHA-256, written in the workflow, is checked, and it is installed with `/VERYSILENT /CURRENTUSER /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART`. `build-installer.mjs` already looks for `ISCC.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Inno Setup 6`. No Chocolatey or winget.
   - `checkout` with `persist-credentials: false` in `plan` and in `build`.
   - SHA updates are manual, in a normal PR. Dependabot is outside this slice.

5. **What each uploads and keys.**
   - **The workflow uploads** to the draft: `Ludiary-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe`, `ludiary-update.json` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` (the three that `release:manifest` leaves in `dist/installer`). The artifact between `build` and `release` lasts 7 days.
   - **The maintainer adds** `ludiary-update.json.sig` and publishes. This gives the four files of point 11.1.
   - **Before creating the draft**, `release` checks with `gh release list --json tagName,isDraft` and `gh release view` that there is no pending draft and that `vX.Y.Z` does not exist. If either fails, it stops with a clear message (point 7).
   - **Without real keys, the workflow fails and does not create the draft** (chosen over generating the draft anyway). `release:build` already rejects `update-keys.json` with fewer than two keys or with test keys (`build.mjs`, B4). That error, which appears at the start of `build`, is the clear message: "a release needs the two public keys…". The step repeats it as a `::error::` annotation.
   - Reason: a draft without keys would give an installer that could never update (`unsupported`) and that `release:sign` could not sign (unknown keyId). Publishing it would leave a version forever without a way out: *immutable releases* do not allow changing it.
   - Until the user generates the keys (point 18, step 6 of the order), a PR with a `release:*` label leaves the run red. That is why none is labeled until then.
   - CI does not use `LUDIARY_UPDATE_KEYS_FILE` or `--allow-test-keys`.

6. **Maintainer helper script:** `release:publish <X.Y.Z> <path to the private key> [--id k1]` (`apps/desktop/scripts/release-publish.mjs`, new; reuses `release-sign.mjs` and `release-lib.mjs`). It runs `gh` and `git` with `execFileSync` and fixed arguments, without a shell.
   1. `gh release view vX.Y.Z --json isDraft,targetCommitish,assets`. It requires that it be a draft, that it have exactly the three assets of point 5 and that it have no `.sig`. It shows the commit and the link to the run so the maintainer reviews them (11.6).
   2. It checks that `apps/desktop/update-keys.json` in their local copy is byte-for-byte identical to the one in the draft's commit (`git show <sha>:apps/desktop/update-keys.json`, after `git fetch`). This way the verification of `release:sign` uses the same keys the installer carries.
   3. `gh release download` into a new temporary folder outside the repository (`mkdtemp` in `os.tmpdir()`, checked with `insideRepo`).
   4. It verifies:
      - that the manifest's `version` is X.Y.Z;
      - that `files["windows-x64"]` has the name `Ludiary-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe` and the `size` and `sha256` of the downloaded installer;
      - that `SHA256SUMS.txt` matches the two files.
      If anything does not match, it stops without signing.
   5. It runs `release-sign.mjs <key> --id <id>` with `LUDIARY_INSTALLER_DIR=<temporary>` (the variable already exists; its comment now says "for tests and for `release:publish`") and `stdio: "inherit"` for the passphrase. That script already signs and verifies right away.
   6. `gh release upload vX.Y.Z <temporary>/ludiary-update.json.sig`.
   7. It asks for written confirmation (`yes`) and runs `gh release edit vX.Y.Z --draft=false --latest`.
   8. It deletes the temporary folder. If `gh release verify` is available, it suggests running it (GH6).
   - It does not print the key or the passphrase, and stores nothing in the repository.
   - **Revised after the code audit:** before step 1 of the list it checks with `gh api repos/chamanRMA/Ludiary/releases/<id>/assets` that the `uploader.login` of the three assets is `github-actions[bot]`; the `yes` confirmation is asked **before** uploading the `.sig` (a "no" leaves nothing uploaded); the downloaded manifest must have exactly the keys `schema`, `product`, `channel`, `version`, `publishedAt` and `files` (only `windows-x64`), with `schema` 1, `product` "ludiary" and `channel` "stable". The provenance attestation (`gh attestation verify`) remains a possible improvement, not implemented.
   - `release-plan.mjs` requires a value for `--pulls`, `--tags`, `--sha` and `--out` (not starting with `--`) and aborts if any is missing; `pulls.json` is read with a direct `JSON.parse` and the tags arrive one per line (`gh api --paginate --jq '.[].ref'`), without rebuilding JSON.

7. **Two merges in a row.** There is **only one pending draft at a time**.
   - The `release` job carries `concurrency: { group: release-draft, cancel-in-progress: false }`, so that two runs do not check "there is no draft" at the same time. `plan` and `build` run in parallel without problem.
   - If a draft already exists when `release` is reached, it fails with "there is a pending draft vA.B.C: publish it or delete it and re-run this run with "Re-run all jobs"". When re-running everything, `plan` recomputes the version over the already published tag, or over the same base if the draft was deleted. Re-running only the failed job uses the old version: if that tag already exists, `release` fails again with the same notice, so nothing is ever overwritten.
   - Discarded alternative: the second draft replaces the first. The robot would have to delete releases and mix the notes of two PRs.
   - GitHub keeps only one pending run per group. A third run that arrives while the second waits cancels the second. It shows as "cancelled" and is re-run the same way. It is a rare case, accepted and noted.

8. **Guide `docs/release.md`** (written by the `docs-writer`, in English). Contents:
   - **One-time setup:**
     - generate the two keys with `release:keygen` and keep them outside the repository, the reserve one elsewhere;
     - add the public ones to `update-keys.json` in a PR;
     - create the three `release:*` labels;
     - enable *immutable releases*, 2FA and "Workflow permissions: read" by default in the repository;
     - protect `main`.
   - **Publish a version:**
     1. set the label on the PR before merging (and the notes in its description);
     2. check that the run is green;
     3. review the draft;
     4. `pnpm --filter @ludiary/desktop release:publish X.Y.Z <key>`.
   - What to do if it fails:
     - no keys;
     - more than one label;
     - pending draft and "Re-run all jobs";
     - cancelled run;
     - forgotten label: set it and re-run everything.
   - **Manual publication without CI:** with `LUDIARY_VERSION`, `release:build`, `release:manifest`, `release:sign` and `gh release create --draft`.
   - Response to a compromised key (B7, point 13) and loss of both keys (11.4).
   - How the actions' SHAs and the Inno version with its hash are updated.
   - That the version is set by the tag, not by `package.json`.

**Reason.** `push` to `main` is the only trigger that also works with PRs from *forks* without resorting to `pull_request_target`. Separating `build` (third-party code, read-only) from `release` (write, no repository code) limits what a malicious dependency can do. Tagging without a commit prevents the robot from writing to `main`, and the scripts already read `LUDIARY_VERSION`. Failing without keys prevents publishing a version that could never update. A single pending draft makes publishing out of order impossible (GH1) without replacement logic. The helper script reuses `release-sign.mjs` as is and adds only the checks that what is signed is what CI built.

**Consequences.**

- Revises 11.1 (the version is set by the tag, not by `package.json`) and 11.6 (trigger). With 15.3 (a), the GitHub account can create drafts but not sign: a version without a valid `.sig` is accepted by no installation (point 3.3).
- New files:
  - `.github/workflows/release.yml`;
  - `apps/desktop/scripts/release-plan.mjs` and `release-publish.mjs`;
  - the `release:publish` script in `apps/desktop/package.json`;
  - cases in `packages/runtime/test/release-scripts.test.ts`, which are those of `planRelease`:
    - no PR, no label and with two labels;
    - each bump, with base `0.0.0` and non-semver tags ignored;
    - different `merge_commit_sha`;
    - null body, long body cut without splitting a character and the footer with the PR;
    - an invalid version or PR number, which never reach the output;
  - and the checks of `release-publish` on the manifest with made-up files: size, hash, name, version and `SHA256SUMS`.
- Small changes in existing files:
  - the comment in `release-build.mjs` ("version from package.json" becomes "from `LUDIARY_VERSION`, set by CI from the tag");
  - the comment of `LUDIARY_INSTALLER_DIR` in `release-lib.mjs`.
- No secret on GitHub. No change in the product, the API or the contract.
- `auditor`: reviews `release.yml` and `release-publish.mjs` before the first labeled PR: permissions, absence of PR interpolations in `run:`, pinned SHAs and Inno hash.
- `docs-writer`: `docs/release.md` (point 8).
- Cost: low-medium (a workflow of about 120 lines, two scripts of about 150 lines with tests).

**Assumptions (4-11-2026):**

- **CI1 (secondary sources, unverified in the official documentation):** in a `pull_request` event from a *fork*, the `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only even if the workflow asks for write. Sources: GitHub's 2021 changelog on `permissions` and third-party guides. If it were false, option A would also work, but B remains correct.
- **CI2 (community sources, unverified):** creating a draft does not create the tag. It is created when publishing, over `target_commitish`. If it were not so, the rule of point 7 still avoids clashes: `release` checks that the tag does not exist and that there are no drafts.
- **CI3 (unverified):** the body of a GitHub release admits about 125,000 characters. The cap of 30,000 leaves plenty of margin.
- **CI4 (unverified):** Node 24 includes corepack and knows how to activate `pnpm@11` from `packageManager`. If not, it is installed with `npm i -g pnpm@<packageManager version>`, with no third-party action.
- **CI5 (unverified in the image's README):** `windows-latest` (`windows-2025`) does not ship Inno Setup. There is an open request in `actions/runner-images` (#11644). If it did ship it, the pinned version is used anyway.

#### 22. Tags without "v" from 0.1.2, with 0.1.1 as a bridge (November 5, 2026; revises point 3 (form of `tag_name`), 21.2 (base), 21.5, 21.6 and the link to the notes in point 20)

Assignment from the user: tags change from `vX.Y.Z` to `X.Y.Z`. `v0.1.0` is already published as an *immutable release* and cannot be renamed.

**What 0.1.0 accepts (verified in the code of `main`; assumption TV1).**

- `parseLatestRelease` (`packages/runtime/src/updates/release.ts`, l. 26) rejects any `tag_name` that does not start with `v`: `!tag.startsWith("v") || !isVersion(tag.slice(1))`. Each asset's URL is required to equal `${downloadBase}/${tag}/${name}` (l. 33), so that part already works for any tag.
- `readCache` (`service.ts`, l. 147) revalidates the stored version by rebuilding the tag as `` `v${version}` ``: with a tag without "v", the stored URLs would stop matching and the cache would be discarded on every cycle.
- `releaseNotesUrl` (`apps/web/src/app/updates.ts`) composes `…/releases/tag/v<version>`.
- Manifest verification does not look at the tag: `tagVersion` is `release.version`, already without the prefix (TS), and in Go `verifyManifest` compares `version` with `to`, which comes from `versions.json`. The Go launcher neither composes URLs nor reads tags. Neither point 18 (M1) nor the vectors (`tag` is already `X.Y.Z`) change.

Consequence: **a 0.1.0 that reads a tag `0.1.1` in `releases/latest` considers it invalid (`check-failed`) and never updates itself**.

**Decision.**

| Option | Advantages | Costs |
|---|---|---|
| A. Without "v" from 0.1.1 | Immediate cut. | Every 0.1.0 installation is left without updates forever: the check fails and a manual reinstall is needed. |
| **B. Bridge: 0.1.1 goes out as `v0.1.1` and already accepts both forms; without "v" from 0.1.2** (chosen) | 0.1.0 updates to 0.1.1 with the code it already carries. From 0.1.1, any form works. Small, bounded change. | One more version with "v". A 0.1.0 that does not update before 0.1.2 is published gets stuck (see Consequences). |
| C. Keep "v" always | No risk. | What the user does not want. |

1. **Single tag rule.** `LAST_V_TAG = "0.1.1"`. `tagFor(version)` = `` `v${version}` `` if `version` ≤ `LAST_V_TAG`; otherwise `version`. It lives in `apps/desktop/scripts/release-lib.mjs` (used by `release-plan.mjs` and `release-publish.mjs`) and, copied with the same name and constant, in `apps/web/src/app/updates.ts` (the web does not import scripts). Both copies carry a test with `0.1.0`, `0.1.1` and `0.1.2`.
2. **Version computation (`planRelease`, revises 21.2).** `TAG` becomes `^refs\/tags\/v?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$`: the base is the greatest between `vX.Y.Z` and `X.Y.Z`. The rest (bumps, `0.0.0` with no tags, non-semver tags ignored) does not change. `planRelease` also returns `tag: tagFor(version)`, and `main()` writes `tag=<tag>` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and uses it in the summary and in the message (today they say `v${version}` by hand).
3. **`release.yml`.**
   - `plan`: `gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref'` (without the final `v`, to bring both forms). New output `tag`.
   - `release`: receives `TAG` through `env:` and validates it with `^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` and, in addition, that it is `VERSION` or `v$VERSION`. The existence check looks at **both** forms (`git/ref/tags/${VERSION}`, `git/ref/tags/v${VERSION}` and `gh release view` of both). `gh release create "$TAG"`. The title is still `Ludiary ${VERSION}`; the summary says `release:publish ${VERSION}`.
4. **`release-publish.mjs` (revises 21.6).** `const tag = tagFor(version)` instead of `` `v${version}` ``. The messages of `checkDraft` use the tag. Usage is still `release:publish X.Y.Z`.
5. **Client (`release.ts`, revises point 3).**
   - `tag_name` must satisfy `^v?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$` (with `isVersion` on the capture); the version is the capture. Rule B3 for the URL does not change: it still requires the tag **as it arrives**.
   - `LatestRelease` gains `tag: string`. `readCache` revalidates with `tag_name: typeof rel.tag === "string" ? rel.tag : \`v${rel.version}\`` (a cache written by 0.1.0 has no `tag`, and its tags had "v"). If it does not pass `parseLatestRelease`, it is discarded as today.
   - No other form is accepted (`V1.2.3`, `release-1.2.3`, suffixes): same trust rules as before.
6. **Link to the notes (revises point 20).** `releaseNotesUrl(version)` = `…/releases/tag/${tagFor(version)}`. It still does not use `html_url`, and works for the banner after updating.
7. **Sequence.** The PR that implements this point carries `release:patch` and yields `v0.1.1` (base `v0.1.0`, `tagFor("0.1.1")` with "v"). The next PR with a `release:*` label yields `0.1.2`, without "v". **Before publishing 0.1.2**, the maintainer checks on a real 0.1.0 that it updates to 0.1.1 (the test of point 19 that was already pending).
8. **`docs/release.md`** (docs-writer): `vX.Y.Z` becomes "the tag (`X.Y.Z`; `v0.1.0` and `v0.1.1` are the only ones with "v")" in the summary, in the failure table and in the manual publication (`gh release create X.Y.Z …`).

**Reason.** Only the already published code decides what 0.1.0 accepts, and it requires the "v". The only way not to leave those installations behind without reinstalling is for the next version to still carry "v" and already understand the new form. A constant and a shared function are enough; there is no need to store the tag in the contract or in the manifest.

**Consequences.**

- **For the user:** 0.1.1 will still be called `v0.1.1` on GitHub; from 0.1.2, without "v". A 0.1.0 installation that does not get to update to 0.1.1 before 0.1.2 is published will see "Could not check" forever and will have to download the installer by hand. With 0.1.0 published a day ago, it is acceptable; the more time passes between 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, the fewer installations are left behind (how long to wait is the user's decision).
- The old tags do not change. `releases/latest` is always a single version: there is no way to serve 0.1.0 and 0.1.2 at the same time.
- No changes in the manifest, the signature, Go, the vectors, the contract or the API.
- Tests: `planRelease` with a mixed base (`v0.1.0` and `0.1.2` → base `0.1.2`) and `tag` of 0.1.1 and 0.1.2; `parseLatestRelease` with `0.1.2`, `v0.1.2` and rejection of `V0.1.2` and of a URL with the other form; `readCache` with an old cache without `tag` and with `tag` without "v"; `releaseNotesUrl("0.1.1")` with "v" and `("0.3.0")` without it (changes the current expectation of `updates.test.ts`).
- `auditor`: reviews the change in `release.yml` (new variable in `env:`, validation) and in `release.ts` (trust boundary).
- `docs-writer`: `docs/release.md` (step 8).

**Assumptions (5-11-2026):**

- **TV1 (verified on 5-11-2026):** `release.ts`, `service.ts` and `updates.ts` in `main` are those of `v0.1.0`. The tag `v0.1.0` is commit 07df48f, identical to `main` in `packages/runtime/src/updates`, `apps/web/src/app/updates.ts` and `apps/desktop/update-keys.json`, and its key `k1` is the correct one. It was checked with `git diff v0.1.0 -- packages/runtime/src/updates apps/web/src/app/updates.ts`. If 0.1.0 already accepted tags without "v", `LAST_V_TAG` becomes `"0.1.0"` and 0.1.1 already goes out without "v".
- **TV2:** `gh release create 0.1.2 --target <sha>` creates the tag `0.1.2` when publishing, just as with "v" (CI2), and `matching-refs/tags/` without a prefix returns all the tags.

#### 23. A stored update state never outlives the installed version (November 9, 2026; revises point 18)

**Context.** On 9-11-2026 a manual install of 0.1.1 showed "La actualización no pasó la última comprobación" and no longer offered 0.1.2. Two causes: (1) `state.json` kept `applying → 0.1.2` from the update of 6-11, because that trial passed during the only run of 0.1.2 and the next start was a development build, which does not reconcile; the 0.1.1 start then read it as `verify-failed`. (2) A stored `failed` was cleared only by `acknowledge()`, which the interface offers for notices, not for failures, so the state hid `available` for good and "Buscar ahora" did not clear it either.

**Decision (the user's rule: a check looks at the installed version, it does not trust a record that may be stale).**

1. `reconcileState`: `applying` whose target is the installed version or older becomes `idle`; `failed`, like `ready` and `downloading`, becomes `idle` when its version is not newer than the installed one.
2. Every check that gets an answer from GitHub (`200`, `304` or `404`, automatic or manual) turns a stored `failed` into `idle`, keeping `retryBad`, `updated` and `downgraded`. What is offered then depends only on the installed version and the release. A version that Go marked bad keeps its protection: `latestFailedBefore`, no prompt, and a confirmation before downloading it again (point 18, M4).
3. A failure in the current session (`lastError`) is still shown until the next check, as before.

**Consequences.** A false `verify-failed` like that of 9-11 (target newer than the installed version, so reconcile cannot tell it from a real one) is shown until the next check that gets an answer: the automatic one about a minute after start, or "Buscar ahora" in mode `off` or under a rate limit. Neither the check nor reconcile touches `state.json` while a trial or a rollback is running (A1), so `rollback-interrupted` is kept. A stale `applying` whose target is the installed version keeps the `updated` notice. Tests in `updates-apply.test.ts` and `updates-service.test.ts`. `auditor` review of 9-11-2026: no critical or high; the medium (clearing during a trial or rollback) and the lows are applied. No changes in Go, the manifest, the contract or the interface.

### 91. Import the Steam and GOG wishlists into the price watch list (extends decisions 40, 74, 77 and 86; resolves option 12.1 (c) of 86 for the stores; contract, lock, errors and volume reviewed by the auditor in its point 13)

Assignment (03-11-2026, after trying the comparator): import the stores' wishlists into the watch list (`price_watch`) of 86. Numbers 89 and 90 are taken on other branches.

#### 1. What is already decided

- **86:** local watch list of at most 500 items per user, with IsThereAnyDeal ID; lookup by store ID only for Steam (`app/<appid>`) and GOG (product ID); budget of 200 requests every 5 minutes; nothing goes out except what the user looks at. Decision 86 left the import (12.1 c) for its own slice.
- **40:** optional, additive connector operations, with `contractVersion` 1 (like `importCollections` in 87); the core validates all output as untrusted.
- **74 and 77:** Steam connects with OpenID (SteamID) and the user's API key, encrypted in `store:steam`, and requires a profile with "Game details" public; GOG, with the official login and the Galaxy token in `store:gog`, which rotates the `refresh_token` on every renewal.
- **Invariants 8 and 9:** official routes when they exist; nothing goes out except to the stores and the services the user configures.

#### 2. What each store offers (verified on 03-11-2026 except where indicated)

| Store | Route | With the connection Ludiary already has | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Steam** | `GET https://api.steampowered.com/IWishlistService/GetWishlist/v1/?steamid=<id>` | Yes: only the SteamID; the host is already in `apiHosts` | **In.** It is Valve's web API, but it is not in the Steamworks documentation (`partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi` does not list `IWishlistService`); the community reference `steamapi.xpaw.me` marks it as undocumented and keyless. Same status as `IStoreBrowseService/GetItems`, accepted in 73. With someone else's profile it returned `{"response":{}}` (SW2). There is no documented route, so it is the most official one that exists (invariant 8) |
| **GOG** | `GET https://embed.gog.com/user/wishlist.json` with `Authorization: Bearer` | Yes: the token of 77; the host is already in `apiHosts` | **In.** Unofficial, like all the GOG API the connector already uses (`user/data/games`, 77). Shape of the response unverified (GW1) |
| **Epic** | Only the web store's GraphQL, with persisted queries and the browser session | No: the token of 78 is a launcher one | **Out** (NW1) |
| **Ubisoft** | The wishlist lives on the web store (`store.ubisoft.com`), with its session | No | **Out** (NW1) |
| **EA** | No wishlist is known in the EA app and no API | No | **Out** (NW1) |
| **IsThereAnyDeal (waitlist)** | `GET /waitlist/games/v1`, OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and scope `wait_read` (ITAD15) | No: Ludiary only has the API key | **Out for now** (point 4) |

#### 3. Decision: contract

```ts
// packages/contracts/src/connector.ts (ADR 91). Optional, additive; contractVersion stays 1.
export interface StoreConnector {
  // ...
  /**
   * ADR 91. Optional. The user's wishlist in the store, read with the stored connection. Never in a sync, only
   * when the core asks (point 5). Requires `connection` and `apiHosts`. Untrusted output: the core validates and caps.
   */
  readWishlist?(ctx: SyncContext): Promise<WishlistSnapshot>;
}

/** ADR 91. */
export interface WishlistSnapshot {
  /** false: the store answered with an empty or unreadable list that may be hidden (Steam `{}`), or the list is partial. */
  readonly complete: boolean;
  /** Store order (Steam priority, GOG as received). At most 5000; storeGameId with the store's own format. */
  readonly entries: readonly { readonly storeGameId: string; readonly title: string; readonly addedAt?: string; readonly media?: EntryMedia }[];
}
```

- `checkConnectorManifest`: `readWishlist requires a connection wizard` and `readWishlist requires apiHosts`.
- Only **Steam** and **GOG** implement it.
- **Steam (`connectors/steam/src/wishlist.ts`):** `GetWishlist` with the SteamID as a `Secret` in the query, **without the API key** (it does not need it, SW2; less exposure). `response.items[]` with `appid` (SW1); out of range or repeated, it is skipped and the result is left `complete: false`. `response` without `items` → `{ complete: false, entries: [] }` (empty or hidden: they cannot be told apart, SW2). Titles with `resolveSteamTitles` (`GetItems`, batches of 50; no title → `Steam <appid>`, SW3); media with `steamMedia(appid)`, no request. `addedAt` from `date_added` (seconds) if valid. Errors with `throwForStatus` from `library.ts`.
- **GOG (`connectors/gog/src/wishlist.ts`):** `refreshSession(ctx)` and `GET embed.gog.com/user/wishlist.json`; only the keys of `wishlist` with value `true` and shape `^\d{1,20}$` (GW1). 401/403 → `store.unexpected-response` with `connectors.gog.error.wishlist` (the renewal already went well; code review, 04-11-2026: `expiredError` contradicted point 13 M2). Titles and covers with `api.gog.com/products?ids=` in batches of 50 and the media of 76 (`images.gog.com`); a product that does not come back appears as `GOG <id>` and without an image (GW2).
- **Image privacy:** the media of an imported item comes from the store itself (Steam's or GOG's CDN), not from IsThereAnyDeal. It fits 71: Valve and GOG already know their own wishlist.

#### 4. The IsThereAnyDeal waitlist: out for now

Reading it requires OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (ITAD15): the user would have to register in their IsThereAnyDeal application a return URL to `ludiary.localhost:<port>`, when the port can change (28 and 53); a wizard type with `awaits: 'callback'` for services, which 86 (point 15, A1) forbids on purpose; and storing and renewing OAuth tokens in addition to the key. A lot of cost for a list that the user can already fill on the IsThereAnyDeal website by importing their Steam list there. If requested, it goes in its own decision.

#### 5. Core (`packages/core/src/prices.ts`, new operation `importWishlist(store)`)

1. **Requirements:** IsThereAnyDeal connected and not `invalid` (86, M2); the store connected and with `readWishlist`. A country is not needed (the lookup does not use it).
2. **Reading:** with that store's sync context (write `secrets`, because GOG rotates the `refresh_token`), **chained with its sync** (the same per-store lock of the loop of 50 and 88: two simultaneous GOG renewals would invalidate the session) and with the store's epoch.
3. **Validation:** at most 5000 entries; `storeGameId` with each store's format (that of `validate.ts`); titles without control characters and at most 300; media with `validateMedia(m, connector.mediaHosts)`; duplicates out.
4. **Match with IsThereAnyDeal:** only the IDs that are not already in `price_watch` with that origin (point 6); `lookupByStore(store, ids)` in batches of 200 (3 requests for 500), within the budget of 86. **No lookup by title**: a store ID that IsThereAnyDeal does not know is counted as `notFound`, is not stored and is looked up again in the next import.
5. **Write**, in a transaction, only if neither the store's epoch nor that of `service:itad` has changed (M3):
   - new `service_game_id` → row with `origin = <store>`, `origin_store_game_id`, the store's title and media, `type` null, `added_at` = now; **in the store's order and until the limit of 500 is filled** (those that do not fit are counted, `overLimit`);
   - `service_game_id` already followed (by hand or from the other store) → not touched (`alreadyWatched`); **what was added by hand is never changed or removed by an import**;
   - point 9.2 (a): if `complete` and the list brings at least one item, the rows with that `origin` whose `origin_store_game_id` is no longer there are deleted. With `complete: false` or an empty list nothing is deleted (like the empty-library guard of 83).
6. **Result:** `{ added, removed, alreadyWatched, notFound, overLimit, hiddenOrEmpty }`, counters only. Prices are not requested here: the page requests them with the normal refresh of 86.
7. **Floor:** 1 minute per store (`MANUAL_SYNC_FLOOR_MS`, 50); below that, `rate-limited` without network.
8. **Logs:** counters only (`requested`, `found`, `notFound`, `added`, `removed`). Never IDs, titles or the SteamID.
9. Disconnecting the store does not touch `price_watch`: it is user data (86, point 8). With another account, the next complete import removes what is not in its list.

#### 6. Data (on this decision's branch: `packages/db/drizzle/0008_watch_origin.sql`, embedded id `0009_watch_origin`)

| Table | New columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `price_watch` | `origin` (`text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual'`, `CHECK` in `manual` / `steam` / `gog`), `origin_store_game_id` (`text`, null) | `CHECK ((origin = 'manual') = (origin_store_game_id IS NULL))`. Index (`user_id`, `origin`). Current rows stay as `manual`. Whatever `drizzle-kit` generates with the table rebuild, as in 85 |

- Numbering: after `0007_watch_media` of point 17 of 86. If another branch (89, 90) merges a migration first, the one that arrives later is renumbered before merging; embedded IDs are not reused.
- Backups: the whole database (86, point 8), so the origin goes in without doing anything.

#### 7. API

| Route | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/prices/wishlist/:store/import` | `WishlistStoreParamsSchema` (`{ store: 'steam' \| 'gog' }`, `strict`); body `EmptyObjectSchema` | 200 `WishlistImportSchema` (the counters of point 5.6, integers from 0 to 5000, and `hiddenOrEmpty: boolean`) |
| `GET /api/prices` | the current one | `PriceBoardSchema` adds `wishlistStores: StoreId[]` (connected stores with `readWishlist`) and `WatchItemSchema` adds `origin: 'manual' \| 'steam' \| 'gog'` |

- `session+key` (67), like all those of 86. Errors: without IsThereAnyDeal → `action-unavailable` with `prices.errors.notConnected`; store not connected → `auth.required` with that store's text; store without `readWishlist` → `action-unavailable`; below the floor → `rate-limited`; the store's (`account.private-profile`, `auth.expired`…) with their texts, and IsThereAnyDeal's with `connectors.itad.errors.*`.

#### 8. What the user sees

- **Comparator:** an "Import Steam wishlist" button and another for GOG, only for the stores in `wishlistStores`. Before importing, a dialog: "Ludiary will read your Steam wishlist and send IsThereAnyDeal the identifiers of those games to follow their price. What you added by hand does not change." When finished, a notice with the counters ("12 added, 3 already followed, 2 without data in IsThereAnyDeal, 4 do not fit: the list allows 500").
- `hiddenOrEmpty`: "No games were found. If your Steam wishlist is not public, change it in your profile's privacy settings (Game details) and try again."
- Each imported item carries a small label "Steam wishlist" or "GOG wishlist". With 9.3 (a), "Unfollow" on an imported one warns that it will come back in the next import if it is still in the store's wishlist.
- Texts in `packages/i18n` (`prices.wishlist.*`) and each connector's errors in their `locales/` (6).

#### 9. What the user decides (product only)

While they do not decide, the recommended option of each point is applied.

1. **When it is imported:** (a) **recommended:** with the button, on request (the user knows when their wishlist goes out to IsThereAnyDeal); (b) also automatically at the end of each store sync, with a switch off by default in Settings (like the mirror of 88).
2. **If the game is removed from the store's wishlist** (or bought, which removes it): (a) **recommended:** on the next complete import it stops being followed, only if the import brought it; (b) it always stays and the user removes it by hand.
3. **"Unfollow" an imported one that is still in the store's list:** (a) **recommended:** it comes back in the next import, with a notice when removing it; (b) it is remembered and does not come back (one more discard table and its interface).
4. **Limit:** (a) **recommended:** 500 in total, imported in the store's order and the ones that do not fit are reported; (b) raise it to 1000 (double the price requests when opening the Comparator).
5. **Epic, Ubisoft and EA:** (a) **recommended:** out, no button; (b) out, with a text explaining why.

#### 10. Tests

- **Steam:** made-up responses with the shape of SW1 (no real SteamID): normal list, `{"response":{}}`, `appid` out of range or repeated, 401/403, 429 with `Retry-After`, 5xx, odd body; the API key is **not** sent; the SteamID goes as a `Secret`; titles in batches of 50 and fallback title.
- **GOG:** `wishlist` with `true` and `false`, keys that are not IDs, 401 → expired, session renewed before requesting; missing products.
- **Contract:** `checkConnectorManifest` with `readWishlist` without `connection` or without `apiHosts`; conformance of the five connectors (Epic, Ubisoft and EA do not declare it).
- **Core:** without IsThereAnyDeal or with `invalid`, no network; only new IDs are looked up; `notFound` is not stored; limit of 500 with `overLimit`; manual items are never touched; deletion only with `complete` and a non-empty list, and only of the same origin; store or service epoch changed midway → nothing written; chained with that store's sync; 1-minute floor; logs without IDs or titles.
- **`db`:** `0008_watch_origin.sql` (id `0009_watch_origin`) over `0007_watch_media.sql` (id `0008_watch_media`) with data (rows stay `manual`); the `CHECK`s of `origin` and of the `origin` / `origin_store_game_id` pair.
- **API:** without origin key → 401 `origin_key_required`, like the rest of the API; `:store` other than `steam`/`gog` → 400; body with keys → 400.
- **Web:** buttons only for `wishlistStores`, dialog, summary, `hiddenOrEmpty`, origin label.

#### 11. Manual test (prepared by the `tester`; done by the user with their accounts)

1. Steam with a public wishlist: import; check titles, images and prices; note the shape of the response in the debug log (closes SW1 and SW3).
2. Set the list to private (or "Game details" to friends only): import and see the `hiddenOrEmpty` notice without anything being deleted (closes SW2).
3. Remove a game from the list on Steam and import: it stops being followed (9.2 a); one added by hand stays.
4. GOG: import with the connected account; note whether `wishlist.json` responds to the Galaxy token and its shape (closes GW1 and GW2) and whether IsThereAnyDeal finds the GOG IDs (closes ITAD4).
5. Import twice in a row (the second waits for the floor) and once during a GOG sync: the GOG session remains valid.
6. The exported log has no SteamID, IDs or titles.

#### 12. Cost and branch

| Part | Size |
|---|---|
| `readWishlist` contract and manifest check | S |
| Steam and GOG `readWishlist` with tests | S + S |
| Core `importWishlist` | M |
| Migration, repository, API | S |
| Web (buttons, dialog, summary, label) | S |
| Total | M |

**Recommended branch:** a new one, `feature/listas-deseos`, **from `feature/comparador-precios`** when it has point 17 of 86. Reason: it touches the stores' contract and two connectors (with the GOG session), so it needs its own `auditor` review, and the comparator can be closed and merged without waiting for it. Order: contract (`developer`, reviewed by the architect) → `connectors` (Steam and GOG) and `developer` (core, data, API) in parallel → web → `tester`, `auditor` and `docs-writer` (privacy: the wishlist goes out to IsThereAnyDeal when imported).

#### 13. Auditor review of the design (03-11-2026, commit `db8d1a0`; takes precedence over points 3 to 12)

No criticals or highs. All findings accepted.

**M1 (medium). The lock of point 5.2 does not exist.** Verified: `inFlight` is private to `createSyncService` (`packages/core/src/sync.ts`, l. 51) and `schedule` (l. 73-82), with a pass in progress, **queues** if forced and **skips** if not: it does not wait. The following is added to `SyncService`:

```ts
// packages/core/src/sync.ts (ADR 91, point 13, M1). Shares inFlight with schedule().
/** Runs fn alone for this store: waits for the pass in flight (if any), then holds the store's slot until fn settles. */
exclusive<T>(store: StoreId, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
```

- `exclusive` waits for that store's `inFlight` promise (without propagating its error), registers its own in the same `inFlight` and removes it in `finally`; two consecutive `exclusive` calls are chained.
- A pass requested **during** the import is always **queued** (also without `force`, because otherwise the sync on opening the web would be lost) and starts when the import ends with today's loop (`runLoop` over `queued`).
- `importWishlist` runs inside `exclusive(store, …)`. Risk it avoids: two GOG `refreshSession` calls at once, one of them with the `refresh_token` already rotated → `auth.expired` and the connection marked as expired.
- Tests in both directions: import requested with a pass in progress → waits and there are no two overlapping `refreshSession` calls; pass (forced and not forced) requested during an import → queued and executed afterwards.

**M2 (medium). Steam errors.** `throwForStatus` from `connectors/steam/src/library.ts` (l. 14-18) is not reused: it marks a 401/403 as `auth.invalid` with "invalid key", and `GetWishlist` goes without a key. In `wishlist.ts`, 401/403 → `store.unexpected-response` with the own key `connectors.steam.error.wishlist` ("Steam would not let the wishlist be read"); 429 → `store.rate-limited` with `retryAfterMs`; 5xx → `network.unavailable`. **`importWishlist` never changes the state of the store's connection** (`store_connections`, `services.itad.status` aside, which follows M2 of 86), except for a rejected GOG renewal, which gives `auth.expired` as in the sync (77). Test: a 401/403 from `GetWishlist` leaves Steam `connected` and does not show the key's text.

**M3 (medium). Volume.** A list of 5000 cost 100 `GetItems` and 25 lookups to bring in at most 500. The operation is split into two phases (replaces the contract of point 3):

```ts
// packages/contracts/src/connector.ts (ADR 91, point 13, M3). Both optional; present together or not at all.
/** Ids only, in store order, at most 5000. No title or media requests. */
readWishlist?(ctx: SyncContext): Promise<{ readonly complete: boolean; readonly entries: readonly { readonly storeGameId: string; readonly addedAt?: string }[] }>;
/** Titles and media of at most 500 ids the core chose (point 5). Ids missing from the result: `<Store> <id>` and no image. */
describeWishlistItems?(storeGameIds: readonly string[], ctx: SyncContext): Promise<ReadonlyMap<string, { readonly title: string; readonly media?: EntryMedia }>>;
```

- `checkConnectorManifest`: both together or neither, plus the rules of point 3. `WishlistSnapshot` remains as the return type of `readWishlist` (without `title` or `media`).
- Core order: `readWishlist` → remove the IDs already in `price_watch` with that origin → lookup in batches of 200 **in the store's order, stopping as soon as the ones found fill the gap** up to 500 → `describeWishlistItems` only with those to be added → write. For the deletion of point 5.5 the IDs from `readWishlist` are enough, with no lookup.
- **Own floor for the import: 10 minutes per store** (`WISHLIST_IMPORT_FLOOR_MS`, in memory), separate from the sync's `MANUAL_SYNC_FLOOR_MS` (replaces point 5.7). Below that, `rate-limited` without network, with the time at which importing is possible again.

**Lows:**

- **(a)** `validateMedia` without a port check: fixed in 86, point 18, and applies here to Steam and GOG media.
- **(b) Deletion by origin** when the same IsThereAnyDeal game comes from two IDs. **Choice:** within one store it is checked; between stores the risk is accepted.
  - **Same store** (two AppIDs that IsThereAnyDeal merges into one game): before deleting the row of an `origin_store_game_id` that is no longer there, it checks whether another ID of the current list was matched in this import with the same `service_game_id`; if so, the row stays and moves to that ID. It is cheap: that other ID was not an origin, so it was already looked up in this pass.
  - **Two stores** (in the Steam and GOG lists): the row carries a single origin; if it is removed from that store's list it is deleted, even if it remains in the other, and it comes back in the other store's next import (with 9.1 a, when the user requests it). Accepted because it corrects itself. Checking the other store's last complete list would require storing the lists, a new table just for this case.
- **(c)** If **any** batch of `lookupByStore` or `describeWishlistItems` fails, nothing is written, deletions included: everything is computed beforehand and written in a single transaction at the end. Test: second batch with 429 or 5xx → `price_watch` unchanged.
- **(d)** Uniform citation: **`0008_watch_origin.sql` (id `0009_watch_origin`)**, corrected in the index, in the consequences, in point 10 and in "Open questions".
- **(e)** The `ConnectorError`s of `wishlist.ts` (Steam and GOG) carry a fixed English message, with no response text and no `cause` (also those from `JSON.parse`), like point 15 (B2 and B6) of 86 (point 5.8). Test: an odd body with a marker text does not appear in the log or in the API response.

The questions of point 9 remain open; meanwhile, the recommended option of each applies.

#### Assumptions

- **SW1 (unverified):** `GetWishlist/v1` responds `{ response: { items: [{ appid, priority, date_added }] } }`, in priority order. What has been verified (03-11-2026): the route exists and responds 200 without a key; `steamapi.xpaw.me` lists it with a single parameter, `steamid`, and marks it as undocumented.
- **SW2 (unverified):** it does not need the API key and only returns the list if the profile's "Game details" are public (the requirement of 74); a hidden list and an empty one both give `{"response":{}}`, with no way to tell them apart (verified with someone else's profile; replaces ITAD10 of 86).
- **SW3 (unverified):** `GetItems` gives a name also for not-yet-released games on the wishlist.
- **GW1 (unverified):** `embed.gog.com/user/wishlist.json` accepts the Galaxy token of 77 and responds `{ wishlist: { "<productId>": true, … }, checksum }`. Verified only that third-party clients use it (the Rust `gog` *crate* with `Bearer`); `gogapidocs` does not document it.
- **GW2 (unverified):** `api.gog.com/products` returns title and images for the wishlist products, also for those not yet on sale.
- **NW1 (search of 03-11-2026, no result):** Epic has no wishlist readable with the launcher token; Ubisoft only on its web store with the browser session; EA has no known wishlist. If a route appears with the current connection, it is added in its own decision.
- **Verification of the connectors (03-11-2026, public read-only calls, no credentials).** *Confirmed:* `GetWishlist/v1` responds 200 with `{"response":{}}` for a SteamID with no visible list and no key (SW2, the "no key" part and the empty/hidden shape); `api.gog.com/products?ids=` responds without a token with `title`, `game_type` and `images.background` in `images-N.gog-statics.com`, and the same file `<64-hex hash>.jpg` is in `images.gog.com` (GW2, the catalog part; the image comes out as `heroUrl`, the catalog has no vertical cover); `embed.gog.com/user/wishlist.json` without a token responds 403 (it exists and asks for a session). *Remains for the manual test (point 11):* shape of `items` with a visible list (`appid`, `priority`, `date_added`, and whether the order is the priority one; SW1), that `GetItems` gives a name to unreleased games (SW3), that `wishlist.json` accepts the Galaxy token and its shape (GW1), that the catalog returns products not yet sold (GW2), and GOG's order: `JSON.parse` sorts numeric keys, so GOG's "store order" is not recoverable and comes out by ascending ID (with more than 500 items, low IDs get in first). The connector tests use made-up responses (`connectors/*/fixtures/wishlist/`).

**Reason:** Steam and GOG are the two stores with a wishlist readable with the connection the user has already made, and the only two that IsThereAnyDeal matches by store ID (86, ITAD5), so the import does not need to match by title, which could follow the price of another game. An optional connector operation, like `importCollections` in 87, keeps the fragile part isolated and does not change `contractVersion`. Marking the origin allows mirroring the store's list without ever touching what was added by hand. Importing on request lets the user decide when their list goes out to IsThereAnyDeal. Discarded alternatives: the IsThereAnyDeal waitlist via OAuth (point 4); matching by title what the lookup does not find (risk of following the wrong game); Epic, Ubisoft and EA through their web store routes (no route with the current connection, NW1); importing the library at the same time (it already has its panel in the detail view).

**Consequences:**

- New optional operation `readWishlist` in the stores' contract (additive, `contractVersion` 1) and `WishlistSnapshot`; row of 40 in the index.
- Migration `0008_watch_origin.sql` (id `0009_watch_origin`) with prior copy; the watch list distinguishes what is imported from what is added by hand.
- Ludiary sends IsThereAnyDeal the wishlist IDs when importing it: the dialog and the privacy guide say so.
- Two more routes that can break without warning (Steam undocumented and GOG unofficial): the failure is shown in the summary with the store's text and the rest of the comparator continues.
- The `docs-writer` updates the comparator guide and the privacy note; the `tester`, the responses and the test of point 11; the `auditor` reviews design and code.

### 92. Export the logs and know whether a game is open (specifies decisions 35 and 55 for the updater; revises the zip export of 59 and the disabled button of point 7.6 of 90)

Assignment from the main session (5-11-2026, branch `feature/registros-y-partidas`): the two pieces that point 19 of 90 leaves as "Pending", with the minimum change.

#### 1. What exists today (read on 5-11-2026)

- **Logs:** `createFileLogger` (`packages/runtime/src/files.ts`) writes `logs/server.log`, `logs/launcher.log` and `logs/crash.log`, with `redactHome` applied on writing, 512 KiB and a single rotated file (`.log.1`). It is the provisional replacement of 59 (without `pino`). Inno's log goes to `updates/<v>/install.log`, with full paths (90, M6).
- **Web:** Settings > Privacy and logs already has the "Export logs" row, only in the simulator (`isSimulated`); `real.ts` returns `unavailable` in `exportLogs`. The rollback notice (`UpdatesNotice`, `rolledBack`) already links to `/settings/privacy` with `updates.notice.exportLogs`.
- **Playtime:** only what the store reports (`storePlaytimeMinutes` and `storeLastPlayedAt`, today from Steam). **There is no process detection**: no `ProcessWatcher`, no `play_sessions` table, no polling after launching. `InstalledEntry.executables` exists in the contract, but the core does not use it. `ProcessLauncher` launches detached and without keeping the PID; with URIs (Steam, Epic, Ubisoft, EA) the process that starts is `rundll32` and the store, never the game.

#### 2. Export: what is exported

**Decision: a single text file, not a zip (revises 59).**

| Option | Advantages | Costs |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) A `.txt` (recommended)** | No dependencies; the user can read it before attaching it, which gives confidence in the filtering; GitHub accepts `.txt` in issues | Somewhat larger than a zip (the total is already bounded) |
| (b) Zip, as 59 said | Smaller; separate files | A new dependency (no zip one is installed) or a zip writer of our own; the user does not see what they send without unzipping |

- **Name:** `ludiary-logs-<version>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.txt` (UTC time).
- **Header**, values and codes only:
  - `Ludiary <version>`, `os.version()` and `os.release()`, `process.arch`, Node version, interface language and the generation time.
  - Updater state if it exists (`mode`, `state`, `current`, `latest`, error code): it is what an issue needs after a rollback.
  - Per store: `store`, `connection`, `mode` and, of each sync state, the type, the state, the last run and the error code. **Never `accountLabel`** or any other account name.
- **Body:** one section per file, with the relative name as title (`===== logs/server.log.1 =====`), first the rotated one and then the current one:
  - the normal files in `logs/` whose name matches `^[a-z0-9-]+\.log(\.1)?$`;
  - `updates/<v>/install.log` of each folder whose name is a valid version (M6 of 90).
  - Nothing else: no database, no `runtime.json`, `state.json`, `versions.json`, backups, tokens or settings.
- **Filtering:** `redactHome` is applied **again** to each file on export. It is mandatory for `install.log`, which does not pass through the logger, and it covers lines written by versions with an earlier filter.
- **Caps:** the last 2 MiB of each file and 16 MiB in total. Whatever is cut is indicated with a `[truncated]` line. Unreadable file: a line with the code (`unreadable`), without path or system message.
- Absolute paths appear neither in the section titles nor in the header.
- `install.log` is today deleted with `updates/<to>` after a passed trial, which is correct. After a **rollback** it must stay there until another version is downloaded (`cleanOtherFolders`). That is precisely when it is needed. A test checks it.

#### 3. Export: route and access level

- **`POST /api/logs/export`**, body `{}` (`EmptyObjectSchema`) and level `session+key` (the default: nothing is declared). It exports files, so 67 and invariant 4 require the origin key.
- Without `exportLogs`, the response is `409 action-unavailable` even though 72 assigns 422 to that code on other routes: 92 **revises 72 for this route only**.
- Response `200`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and the global `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- `POST` is used and not `GET` because it is an action with the key in the header: it cannot be requested with a normal link, and so no browser caches it or preloads it.
- **Where it lives:** it is composed by the server role of `packages/runtime` (`log-export.ts`), which knows `dataDir`, the version and `redactHome`. It reaches `createLocalServer` as an optional dependency `exportLogs?: () => Promise<{ filename: string; body: string }>`, just like `updates`. Without it, the route responds `409 action-unavailable`. The stores' state comes from the core facade that already exists (store list); the core does not read log files.
- The log only notes "logs exported", with the size in bytes.

#### 4. Export: button and link with the updater

- **Button:** the row that already exists in **Settings > Privacy and logs** stops being simulator-only.
- **`exportLogs()` in `real.ts`:**
  1. calls a new method of `http.ts` that makes the same `POST` request, with the origin key and the same error handling, and returns a `Blob`;
  2. takes the name from `Content-Disposition` (if it is not found, `ludiary-logs.txt`);
  3. downloads with `URL.createObjectURL`, a temporary `<a download>` and `revokeObjectURL`.
- Under the button, an **"Open an issue on GitHub"** link to `https://github.com/chamanRMA/Ludiary/issues/new`, which opens outside (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`), with the same fixed repository as `releaseNotesUrl` (90, point 20). 35 asks for it and it is missing today.
- **Link with the updater:** no changes. `updates.notice.exportLogs` of the `rolledBack` notice already leads to `/settings/privacy`, where the button is.
- **Texts** (es/en): `settings.privacy.issue`; `settings.privacy.exportHint` changes to "A text file to attach to an issue. You can read it first: it contains no keys and not your Windows user name.".

#### 5. Game in progress: what counts as a game

**Decision: a game is open if there is a process whose executable is inside the install folder of an installed game in the library, whether Ludiary, the store or a shortcut launched it.**

| Option | Advantages | Costs |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Follow the process launched by Ludiary | No polling | With URIs, Ludiary never sees the game's process (point 1). With `exec` (GOG), the PID is that of the executable, which may delegate to another. It does not see games launched from the store |
| **(b) On-demand polling by install folder (recommended)** | Covers all stores and all origins; a single query when needed, no timers; it is the base of 55's `ProcessWatcher` | False positives from helper processes living in the game's folder (they only postpone) |
| (c) Continuous polling, like 55's, for playtime | Serves playtime at the same time | Depends on 55's real-world tests; not needed for the updater |

- **Installations that count:** the stored ones of ownerships with `kind: 'game'` and no `removed_at`, from any store. `install_path` values that are a drive root (`X:\`) are ignored: a malformed entry cannot make any process count.
- **Comparison** in the core, pure and without disk: lowercase, `/` → `\`, and `install_path` with a trailing `\`. There is a match if the process path starts with it; this way, `C:\Games\Foo` does not match `C:\Games\Foobar\x.exe`.
- *Shortcut:* a game moved with `mklink /J` does not match, because the process path is the real one (72, point 11). It is a harmless false negative (point 6). It improves when 55 closes playtime.
- No exclusion list in this slice: a helper open in the game's folder also postpones. 55's list arrives with playtime.
- **Reason for also counting what the store launched:** stopping the server does not close games (90, point 7.7). What is annoying is that Inno's progress window and the web that opens at the end steal focus from a full-screen game, wherever it came from.

#### 6. Game in progress: how it is queried and what the updater does

- **OS port** (`packages/contracts/src/ports.ts`), optional in `CoreDeps`; without it (Docker, tests), there is never a game:

  ```ts
  // ADR 92 (and the base of ADR 55's ProcessWatcher)
  export interface ProcessWatcher {
    /** Full image paths of the running processes this user can query; the ones it cannot read are left out. Never logged. */
    listExecutables(signal: AbortSignal): Promise<readonly string[]>;
  }
  ```

- **Windows (revises the last point of 55: the native call is chosen, not CIM):** subcommand `ludiary-tray.exe --processes` of the Go helper, with the same pattern as `--known-folder` (89):
  - `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`, and for each PID `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` and `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`;
  - whatever fails is skipped;
  - it writes a line `{"paths":[…]}` without duplicates, with a maximum of 8192 paths, and exits with 0.
  - `platform-windows` launches it with a 5 s maximum time and 4 MiB of output. It only accepts strings that are absolute local paths of at most 32767 characters.
  - CIM is discarded: it forces launching PowerShell, which is slow and depends on the execution policy (the same reasons as in 64).
- **Core:** `isGameRunning(): Promise<boolean>` in the facade (`core.ts`), in a small module (`running.ts`).
  - It reads the install paths with a repository query (new if none suitable exists) and applies point 5.
  - Only a boolean comes out: process paths are personal data and go neither to the log nor to the API.
  - If the port fails or times out: `false` and a log warning, with only the error's name.
- **Updater** (`packages/runtime/src/updates/service.ts`): new option `isGameRunning?: () => Promise<boolean>`, which `server-role.ts` connects to the facade.
  - `restart()` queries it after the `ready` checks and before marking `restarting`.
  - If there is a game: `UpdateError("update.game-running", 409)`. The state stays `ready`: the update is **postponed**, not lost, and is applied on the next cold start (point 7 of 90) or when pressing again with the game closed.
- **Notice:**
  - In the web, `POST /api/updates/restart` gives `409 update.game-running`. About and the version notice (`UpdatesNotice`, "Apply") show the error with its `errorKey`: `core.errors.update.game-running` = "A game is open. Close it and try again; otherwise the update will be installed the next time you open Ludiary." (es/en).
  - In the tray: "Update ready: restart" with a game in progress opens the web (`createOpenUrl("name")`, like `update-available`) instead of doing nothing. There the button shows the reason.
- **Revises point 7.6 of 90:** the button is **not** disabled in advance, because that would force querying processes on every `GET /api/updates`, which the web requests every 2 s. It answers with the 409 when pressed. `updates.restartConfirm` does not change.
- **It is not queried on a cold start** (inner launcher, code 20): if the server was not running, the user has just pressed the shortcut and is on the desktop. The `auto` mode never restarts by itself (90, point 7), so nothing more is needed.
- **Failing open is acceptable:** a false negative (unreadable path, anti-cheat, junction) only restarts Ludiary with the game open, which stays open (90, point 7.7). A false positive only postpones. Neither loses data.
